title.en: Volume 255 Biographies 143: Liu Zongzhou, Huang Daozhou

sentences.zh: 劉宗周

translations.literal: Liu Zongzhou
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zongzhou

sentences.zh: 〈（祝淵王毓蓍）〉

translations.literal: (Zhu Yuan, Wang Mushu)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Sub-biographies: Zhu Yuan and Wang Mushu)]〉

sentences.zh: 黃道周

translations.literal: Huang Daozhou
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou

sentences.zh: 〈（葉廷秀）〉

translations.literal: (Ye Tingxiu)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Ye Tingxiu)]〉

sentences.zh: 劉宗周，字起東，山陰人。

translations.literal: Liu Zongzhou, styled Qidong, was a man of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zongzhou, whose style name was Qidong, came from Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 父坡，為諸生。

translations.literal: His father Po was a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liu Po held licentiate status.

sentences.zh: 母章氏妊五月而坡亡。

translations.literal: His mother, née Zhang, was five months pregnant when Po died.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Zhang, was five months pregnant when Po died.

sentences.zh: 既生宗周，家酷貧，攜之育外家。

translations.literal: After Zongzhou was born, the family was desperately poor, and she took him to be raised at her parents' home.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zongzhou was born, the household was desperately poor, and his mother took him to be raised at her parents' home.

sentences.zh: 後以宗周大父老疾，歸事之，析薪汲水，持藥糜。

translations.literal: Later, because Zongzhou's grandfather was aged and ill, he returned home to serve him, splitting firewood, drawing water, and preparing medicinal gruel.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his grandfather grew old and ill, Zongzhou returned home to care for him, chopping firewood, drawing water, and preparing medicinal gruel.

sentences.zh: 然體孱甚，母嘗憂念之不置，遂成疾。

translations.literal: Yet his constitution was very frail; his mother constantly worried about him without cease, and thus fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: But he was very frail in body, and his mother worried over him incessantly until she herself fell ill.

sentences.zh: 又以貧故，忍而不治。

translations.literal: Because of poverty as well, she bore it and did not seek treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Poverty compelled her to endure the illness without seeking treatment.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十九年，宗周成進士，母卒於家。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Wanli, Zongzhou passed the jinshi examination; his mother died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of the Wanli reign, Zongzhou passed the jinshi examination, but his mother died at home.

sentences.zh: 宗周奔喪，為堊室中門外，日哭泣其中。

translations.literal: Zongzhou hurried home for the mourning; he built a mourning hut inside the middle gate and outside it, and wept there daily.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou rushed home for the funeral and built a mourning hut within and outside the middle gate, weeping there day after day.

sentences.zh: 服闋，選行人，請養大父母。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, he was selected as a courier official and requested leave to support his grandparents.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period ended, he was appointed courier official and asked leave to support his grandparents.

sentences.zh: 遭喪，居七年始赴補。

translations.literal: He encountered further bereavements and remained at home for seven years before taking up his post.
translations.idiomatic: Further deaths in the family kept him at home for seven years before he finally reported for duty.

sentences.zh: 母以節聞於朝。

translations.literal: His mother was reported to the court for her chastity.
translations.idiomatic: His mother's steadfast virtue was reported to the court.

sentences.zh: 時有昆黨、宣黨與東林為難。

translations.literal: At the time the Kun faction, the Xuan faction, and the Donglin were at odds.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Kun and Xuan factions were at odds with the Donglin.

sentences.zh: 宗周上言：「東林，顧憲成講學處。

translations.literal: Zongzhou submitted a memorial, saying: "The Donglin is where Gu Xiancheng lectured.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou memorialized the throne: "The Donglin was where Gu Xiancheng taught.

sentences.zh: 高攀龍、劉永澄、姜士昌、劉元珍，皆賢人。

translations.literal: Gao Panlong, Liu Yongcheng, Jiang Shichang, and Liu Yuanzhen were all worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Panlong, Liu Yongcheng, Jiang Shichang, and Liu Yuanzhen were all men of worth.

sentences.zh: 於玉立、丁元薦，較然不欺其誌，有國士風。

translations.literal: Yu Yuli and Ding Yuanjian clearly did not betray their principles and had the bearing of men of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yuli and Ding Yuanjian plainly never betrayed their principles and bore the spirit of true statesmen.

sentences.zh: 諸臣摘流品可也，爭意見不可；

translations.literal: It is permissible for ministers to sort men by pedigree, but not to quarrel over opinions;
translations.idiomatic: Ministers may rank men by pedigree, but they must not quarrel over opinions;

sentences.zh: 攻東林可也，黨昆、宣不可。」

translations.literal: it is permissible to attack the Donglin, but not to form Kun and Xuan factions."
translations.idiomatic: they may criticize the Donglin, but they must not form Kun and Xuan factions."

sentences.zh: 黨人大嘩，宗周乃請告歸。

translations.literal: The factionalists raised a great outcry, and Zongzhou then requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: The factionalists erupted in protest, and Zongzhou thereupon asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年，起儀制主事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi, he was recalled as director of rites in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianqi he was recalled to serve as director of rites.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「魏進忠導皇上馳射戲劇，奉聖夫人出入自由。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "Wei Jinzhong leads the emperor in riding, archery, and theatrical amusements, and the Lady of Fengsheng comes and goes at will.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Wei Jinzhong leads the emperor into riding, archery, and theatrical diversions, while the Lady of Fengsheng comes and goes as she pleases.

sentences.zh: 一舉逐諫臣三人，罰一人，皆出中旨，勢將指鹿為馬，生殺予奪，制國家大命。

translations.literal: In one stroke three remonstrating officials were expelled and one punished, all by secret edicts; the trend is toward calling a deer a horse, holding the power of life and death, and controlling the great destiny of the state.
translations.idiomatic: In a single move three remonstrating officials were driven out and one punished, all by secret edicts; the trend is toward calling a deer a horse, wielding the power of life and death, and controlling the fate of the realm.

sentences.zh: 今東西方用兵，奈何以天下委閹豎乎？」

translations.literal: Now war is waged in the east and west—how can the empire be entrusted to eunuchs?"
translations.idiomatic: War rages in the east and west—how can the empire be entrusted to eunuchs?"

sentences.zh: 進忠者魏忠賢也，大怒，停宗周俸半年。

translations.literal: Jinzhong was Wei Zhongxian; enraged, he suspended Zongzhou's salary for half a year.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong was Wei Zhongxian, who in a fury suspended Zongzhou's salary for half a year.

sentences.zh: 尋以國法未伸請戮崔文升以正弒君之罪，戮盧受以正交私之罪，戮楊鎬、李如楨、李維翰、鄭之範以正喪師失地之罪，戮高出、胡嘉棟、康應乾、牛維曜、劉國縉、傅國以正棄城逃潰之罪；

translations.literal: Soon afterward, on the grounds that national law had not been enforced, he asked that Cui Wensheng be executed to rectify the crime of regicide, that Lu Shou be executed to rectify the crime of private collusion, that Yang Hao, Li Ruzhen, Li Weihan, and Zheng Zhifan be executed to rectify the crime of losing armies and territory, and that Gao Chu, Hu Jiadong, Kang Yingqian, Niu Weiyao, Liu Guojin, and Fu Guo be executed to rectify the crime of abandoning cities and fleeing in rout;
translations.idiomatic: He soon urged that, since the law had not been upheld, Cui Wensheng should be executed for regicide, Lu Shou for illicit collusion, Yang Hao, Li Ruzhen, Li Weihan, and Zheng Zhifan for losing armies and territory, and Gao Chu, Hu Jiadong, Kang Yingqian, Niu Weiyao, Liu Guojin, and Fu Guo for abandoning cities and fleeing in rout;

sentences.zh: 急起李三才為兵部尚書，錄用清議名賢丁元薦、李樸等，諍臣楊漣、劉重慶等，以作仗節徇義之氣。

translations.literal: he urgently asked that Li Sancai be recalled as Minister of War, that renowned men of clear opinion such as Ding Yuanjian and Li Pu be employed, and that remonstrating officials such as Yang Lian and Liu Chongqing be restored, to rouse the spirit of upholding integrity and dying for righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: he urged the immediate recall of Li Sancai as Minister of War, the employment of celebrated men of clear opinion such as Ding Yuanjian and Li Pu, and the restoration of remonstrating officials such as Yang Lian and Liu Chongqing, to revive the spirit of holding fast to integrity and dying for righteousness.

sentences.zh: 帝切責之。

translations.literal: The emperor sharply rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 累遷光祿丞、尚寶、太仆少卿，移疾歸。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, director of the Court of Imperial Seals, and vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, then returned home on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, director of the Court of Imperial Seals, and vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, then retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 四年，起右通政，至則忠賢逐東林且盡，宗周復固辭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was recalled as right vice commissioner of the Transmission Office; when he arrived, Zhongxian had already driven out the Donglin nearly to the last man, and Zongzhou again firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was recalled as right vice commissioner of the Transmission Office, but on arrival he found Zhongxian had nearly wiped out the Donglin, and Zongzhou again firmly declined the post.

sentences.zh: 忠賢責以矯情厭世，削其籍。

translations.literal: Zhongxian charged him with affectation and world-weariness and struck him from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian accused him of affectation and disdain for public life and struck him from the official rolls.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年冬，召為順天府尹。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Chongzhen, he was summoned as metropolitan prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Chongzhen he was summoned to serve as metropolitan prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 辭，不許。

translations.literal: He declined; the request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He declined, but the court would not accept his resignation.

sentences.zh: 明年九月入都，上疏曰：

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the following year he entered the capital and submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the following year he entered the capital and submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 陛下勵精求治，宵旰靡寧。

translations.literal: Your Majesty strives with vigor to seek good government and is restless from dawn till late night.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty strives tirelessly for good government and finds no rest from dawn till night.

sentences.zh: 然程效太急，不免見小利而速近功，何以致唐、虞之治？

translations.literal: Yet you press for results too urgently, and must seize small gains and hurry after near-term achievements—how can this attain the governance of Tang and Yu?
translations.idiomatic: Yet in pressing for results too urgently, you cannot help seizing small gains and rushing after quick victories—how can this bring about the governance of Tang and Yu?

sentences.zh: 夫今日所汲汲於近功者，非兵事乎？

translations.literal: Is not what you are urgently pursuing today for near-term success military affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Is not what you are urgently pursuing today for quick results military affairs?

sentences.zh: 誠以屯守為上策，簡卒節餉，修刑政而威信布之，需以歲月，未有不望風束甲者，而陛下方銳意中興，刻期出塞。

translations.literal: Truly, if garrison defense is taken as the supreme strategy, troops are streamlined and rations economized, and penal administration is rectified so that authority and trust are spread abroad, then given months and years none would fail to lay down arms at the first rumor—but Your Majesty is now keen on revival and has set a deadline for campaigning beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: If garrison defense were truly taken as the supreme strategy, with streamlined troops, economized rations, and rectified penal administration spreading authority and trust, then in time none would fail to submit at the first rumor—but Your Majesty is now bent on revival and has set a deadline for campaigning beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 當此三空四盡之秋，竭天下之力以奉饑軍而軍愈驕，聚天下之軍以博一戰而戰無日，此計之左也。

translations.literal: At this season when the treasury, granaries, and armories are empty and resources exhausted, exhausting the empire's strength to feed hungry troops only makes the army more arrogant; gathering the empire's armies to gamble on one battle yet finding no day for battle—this plan is mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: At this season when treasury, granaries, and armories stand empty and resources are exhausted, draining the empire to feed hungry troops only makes the army more arrogant; massing the empire's armies to gamble on one battle yet finding no day fit for battle—this strategy is deeply mistaken.

sentences.zh: 今日所規規於小利者，非國計乎？

translations.literal: Is not what you are scrupulously pursuing today for small gains national finance?
translations.idiomatic: Is not what you are scrupulously pursuing today for petty gains national finance?

sentences.zh: 陛下留心民瘼，惻然恫辟，而以司農告匱，一時所講求者皆掊克聚斂之政。

translations.literal: Your Majesty attends to the people's afflictions and is moved with compassion, yet because the Minister of Revenue reports shortage, what is sought at once are all policies of extortion and accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty attends to the people's afflictions with compassionate concern, yet because the Minister of Revenue reports shortage, what is sought at once are all policies of extortion and exaction.

sentences.zh: 正供不足，繼以雜派；

translations.literal: When regular levies are insufficient, miscellaneous surcharges follow;
translations.idiomatic: When regular levies fall short, miscellaneous surcharges follow;

sentences.zh: 科罰不足，加以火耗。

translations.literal: when assessed penalties are insufficient, melting-loss fees are added.
translations.idiomatic: when assessed penalties fall short, melting-loss fees are added.

sentences.zh: 水旱災傷，一切不問，敲撲日峻，道路吞聲，小民至賣妻鬻子以應。

translations.literal: Flood, drought, and disaster harm are altogether ignored; beatings grow harsher by the day, travelers on the roads dare not speak, and common people even sell wives and children to meet demands.
translations.idiomatic: Flood, drought, and disaster harm go altogether unheeded; beatings grow harsher by the day, people on the roads dare not speak out, and common folk even sell wives and children to meet demands.

sentences.zh: 有司以掊克為循良，而撫字之政絕；

translations.literal: Local officials take extortion for conscientious administration, and policies of nurturing the people are extinct;
translations.idiomatic: Local officials treat extortion as conscientious administration, and policies of nurturing the people have vanished;

sentences.zh: 上官以催征為考課，而黜陟之法亡。

translations.literal: superiors take urgent collection as the basis for evaluation, and the methods of promotion and demotion are lost.
translations.idiomatic: superiors take urgent tax collection as the basis for evaluation, and the methods of promotion and demotion are lost.

sentences.zh: 欲求國家有府庫之財，不可得已。

translations.literal: To seek that the state have wealth in its treasuries is already impossible.
translations.idiomatic: To hope that the state will have wealth in its treasuries is already impossible.

sentences.zh: 功利之見動，而廟堂之上日見其煩苛。

translations.literal: As the view of utility and profit stirs, the court daily grows more vexatious and harsh.
translations.idiomatic: As the pursuit of utility and profit gains sway, the court daily grows more vexatious and harsh.

sentences.zh: 事事糾之不勝糾，人人摘之不勝摘，於是名實紊而法令滋。

translations.literal: Matters are investigated beyond what investigation can bear, men are picked at beyond what picking can bear; thus names and realities are confused and laws and orders multiply.
translations.idiomatic: Every matter is investigated beyond endurance, every man is picked at beyond endurance; thus names and realities fall into confusion and laws and orders multiply without end.

sentences.zh: 頃者，特嚴贓吏之誅，自宰執以下，坐重典者十余人，而貪風未盡息，所以導之者未善也。

translations.literal: Recently punishments for corrupt officials were made especially severe; from the chief ministers downward, more than ten suffered heavy penalties, yet the wind of greed has not fully ceased—the means of guidance have not been good.
translations.idiomatic: Recently punishments for corrupt officials were made especially severe; from the chief ministers downward, more than ten suffered heavy penalties, yet the wind of greed has not fully ceased—the means of guidance have not been sound.

sentences.zh: 賈誼曰：「禮禁未然之先，法施已然之後。」

translations.literal: Jia Yi said: "Rites forbid what has not yet happened; law is applied after it has already happened."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi said: "Rites forbid wrong before it happens; law is applied after it has already happened."

sentences.zh: 誠導之以禮，將人人有士君子之行，而無狗彘之心，所謂禁之於未然也。

translations.literal: If they are truly guided by rites, all will have the conduct of scholar-gentlemen and none the heart of dogs and swine—this is what is called forbidding before it happens.
translations.idiomatic: If men are truly guided by rites, all will have the conduct of scholar-gentlemen and none the heart of dogs and swine—this is what is meant by forbidding wrong before it happens.

sentences.zh: 今一切詿誤及指稱賄賂者，即業經昭雪，猶從吏議，深文巧詆，絕天下遷改之途，益習為頑鈍無恥，矯飾外貌以欺陛下。

translations.literal: Now all who have erred in office or been accused of bribery, even when already cleared, still follow the clerks' deliberations; tortuous statutes and cunning slander cut off the empire's path of reform, and men increasingly learn to be dull and shameless, adorning their outward appearance to deceive Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Now all who have erred in office or been accused of bribery, even when already cleared, still face the clerks' deliberations; tortuous statutes and cunning slander cut off every path of reform, and men increasingly learn to be dull and shameless, adorning their outward appearance to deceive Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 士節日隳，官邪日著，陛下亦安能一一察之。

translations.literal: The integrity of scholars daily decays and official corruption daily grows plain. How can Your Majesty examine each case one by one?
translations.idiomatic: The integrity of scholars decays by the day and official corruption grows plainer by the day. How can Your Majesty examine each case one by one?

sentences.zh: 且陛下所以勞心焦思於上者，以未得賢人君子用之也，而所嘉予而委任者，率奔走集事之人：以摘發為精明，以告訐為正直，以便給為才谞，又安所得賢者而用之？

translations.literal: Moreover, the reason Your Majesty toils and burns with thought above is that worthy gentlemen have not been obtained for employment, yet those you praise and entrust are all men who rush about gathering tasks: taking exposure for shrewdness, accusation for uprightness, and ready compliance for talent—how then can worthy men be obtained and employed?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the reason Your Majesty toils and burns with anxiety above is that worthy gentlemen have not been obtained for employment, yet those you praise and entrust are all men who rush about gathering tasks: taking exposure for shrewdness, accusation for uprightness, and ready compliance for talent—how then can worthy men be found and employed?

sentences.zh: 得其人矣，求之太備，或以短而廢長；

translations.literal: When the right man is found, you seek perfection too far and may discard his strengths for his faults;
translations.idiomatic: When the right man is found, you demand perfection too far and may discard his strengths for his faults;

sentences.zh: 責之太苛，或因過而成誤。

translations.literal: you blame too harshly and may turn a fault into a fatal error.
translations.idiomatic: you blame too harshly and may turn a fault into a fatal error.

sentences.zh: 且陛下所擘畫，動出諸臣意表，不免有自用之心。

translations.literal: Moreover, what Your Majesty plans often goes beyond what ministers expect, and you cannot avoid a mind bent on acting on your own.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, what Your Majesty plans often goes beyond what ministers expect, and you cannot avoid a tendency to act on your own judgment.

sentences.zh: 臣下救過不給，讒諂者因而間之，猜忌之端遂從此起。

translations.literal: Ministers below have no leisure to remedy faults; slanderers and flatterers take advantage to drive wedges, and the beginnings of suspicion arise from this.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers below have no leisure to remedy faults; slanderers and flatterers take advantage to drive wedges, and suspicion begins from this.

sentences.zh: 夫恃一人之聰明，而使臣下不得盡其忠，則耳目有時壅；

translations.literal: To rely on one man's intelligence and not let ministers below fully exert their loyalty is for the ears and eyes sometimes to be blocked;
translations.idiomatic: To rely on one man's intelligence and not let ministers fully exert their loyalty is for the ears and eyes sometimes to be blocked;

sentences.zh: 憑一人之英斷，而使諸大夫國人不得衷其是，則意見有時移。

translations.literal: to rely on one man's keen judgment and not let grandees and the people settle what is right is for opinions sometimes to shift.
translations.idiomatic: to rely on one man's keen judgment and not let grandees and the people settle what is right is for opinions sometimes to shift.

sentences.zh: 方且為內降，為留中，何以追喜起之盛乎？

translations.literal: There are secret edicts and memorials held in the palace—how can you pursue the splendor of the Xixi and Qiyuan reigns?
translations.idiomatic: There are secret edicts and memorials held in the palace—how can you pursue the splendor of the Xixi and Qiyuan reigns?

sentences.zh: 數十年來，以門戶殺天下幾許正人，猶蔓延不已。

translations.literal: For decades factionalism has killed how many upright men of the empire, and it still spreads without end.
translations.idiomatic: For decades factionalism has destroyed how many upright men of the empire, and it still spreads without end.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲折君子以平小人之氣，用小人以成君子之公，前日之覆轍將復見於天下也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty wishes to break the gentlemen to appease the petty men's anger and employ petty men to accomplish the gentlemen's public duty—the overturned cart of former days will appear again in the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty wishes to break the gentlemen to appease petty men's anger and employ petty men to accomplish the gentlemen's public duty—the overturned cart of former days will appear again throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 陛下求治之心，操之太急。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's heart in seeking good government is handled too urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's zeal for good government is pressed too urgently.

sentences.zh: 醞釀而為功利，功利不已，轉為刑名；

translations.literal: It ferments into utility and profit; utility and profit unceasing turn into penal statutes;
translations.idiomatic: It ferments into utility and profit; utility and profit without end turn into penal statutes;

sentences.zh: 刑名不已，流為猜忌；

translations.literal: penal statutes unceasing flow into suspicion;
translations.idiomatic: penal statutes without end flow into suspicion;

sentences.zh: 猜忌不已，積為壅蔽。

translations.literal: suspicion unceasing accumulates into obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: suspicion without end accumulates into obstruction.

sentences.zh: 正人心之危，所潛滋暗長而不自知者。

translations.literal: The peril of rectifying people's hearts is what secretly grows in the dark without one's knowing it.
translations.idiomatic: The peril of rectifying people's hearts is what secretly grows in the dark without one's knowing it.

sentences.zh: 誠能建中立極，默正此心，使心之所發，悉皆仁義之良，仁以育天下，義以正萬民，自朝廷達於四海，莫非仁義之化，陛下已一旦躋於堯、舜矣。

translations.literal: If you can truly establish the central standard and silently rectify this heart, so that what the heart sends forth is all the goodness of benevolence and righteousness—benevolence to nurture the empire, righteousness to rectify the myriad people—from the court reaching to the four seas, none not the transforming power of benevolence and righteousness—Your Majesty would at once ascend to the level of Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: If you can truly establish the central standard and silently rectify your heart, so that what your heart sends forth is all the goodness of benevolence and righteousness—benevolence to nurture the empire, righteousness to rectify the myriad people—from the court to the four seas, all transformed by benevolence and righteousness—Your Majesty would at once stand beside Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 帝以為迂闊，然嘆其忠。

translations.literal: The emperor thought him impractical and broad, yet sighed at his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought him impractical and broad-minded, yet sighed at his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 未幾，都城被兵，帝不視朝，章奏多留中不報。

translations.literal: Before long the capital was beset by troops; the emperor did not hold court, and memorials were mostly held in the palace without response.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the capital came under attack; the emperor ceased holding court, and memorials were mostly held in the palace without response.

sentences.zh: 傳旨辦布囊八百，中官競獻馬騾，又令百官進馬。

translations.literal: An edict was transmitted to prepare eight hundred cloth sacks; eunuchs vied to present horses and mules, and officials were also ordered to present horses.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was transmitted to prepare eight hundred cloth sacks; eunuchs vied to present horses and mules, and officials were also ordered to present horses.

sentences.zh: 宗周曰：「是必有以遷幸動上者。」

translations.literal: Zongzhou said: "There must be someone moving the emperor toward relocating the court."
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou said: "Someone must be moving the emperor toward relocating the court."

sentences.zh: 乃詣午門叩頭諫曰：「國勢強弱，視人心安危。

translations.literal: He then went to the Meridian Gate, kowtowed, and remonstrated, saying: "Whether the state's strength is great or small depends on whether the people's hearts are secure or in peril.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to the Meridian Gate, kowtowed, and remonstrated: "Whether the state's strength is great or small depends on whether the people's hearts are secure or in peril.

sentences.zh: 乞陛下出禦皇極門，延見百僚，明言宗廟山陵在此，固守外無他計。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to come out and take the throne at the Gate of Imperial Zenith, extend audience to the hundred officials, and declare plainly that the ancestral temples and imperial tombs are here, and that steadfast defense is the only plan beyond which there is no other."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to come out and take the throne at the Gate of Imperial Zenith, extend audience to the hundred officials, and declare plainly that the ancestral temples and imperial tombs are here, and that steadfast defense is the only plan—there is no other."

sentences.zh: 俯伏待報，自晨迄暮，中官傳旨乃退。

translations.literal: He prostrated himself awaiting reply; from morning till evening he waited, and only when a eunuch transmitted an edict did he withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated himself awaiting a reply; from morning till evening he waited, and only when a eunuch transmitted an edict did he withdraw.

sentences.zh: 米價騰躍，請罷九門稅，修賈區以處貧民，為粥以養老疾，嚴行保甲之法，人心稍安。

translations.literal: As rice prices soared, he asked to abolish the nine-gate levies, repair market quarters to house the poor, provide gruel to nourish the aged and sick, and strictly enforce the baojia system; the people's hearts were somewhat calmed.
translations.idiomatic: As rice prices soared, he asked to abolish the nine-gate levies, repair market quarters to house the poor, provide gruel to nourish the aged and sick, and strictly enforce the baojia system; popular sentiment was somewhat calmed.

sentences.zh: 時樞輔諸臣多下獄者，宗周言：「國事至此，諸臣負任使，無所逃罪，陛下亦宜分任咎。

translations.literal: At the time many grand secretaries and assisting ministers were imprisoned; Zongzhou said: "State affairs have come to this—the ministers bear responsibility as envoys and cannot escape guilt; Your Majesty should also share the blame.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many grand secretaries and assisting ministers were imprisoned; Zongzhou said: "State affairs have come to this—the ministers bear responsibility and cannot escape guilt; Your Majesty should also share the blame.

sentences.zh: 禹、湯罪己，興也勃焉。

translations.literal: Yu and Tang blamed themselves, and rose swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and Tang blamed themselves, and their states rose swiftly.

sentences.zh: 曩皇上以情面疑群臣，群臣盡在疑中，日積月累，結為陰痞，識者憂之。

translations.literal: Formerly Your Majesty suspected the ministers on grounds of personal ties; the ministers were all within suspicion, and day by day and month by month it formed a hidden blockage—those who understood were troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Your Majesty suspected the ministers on grounds of personal ties; the ministers were all within suspicion, and day by day and month by month it formed a hidden blockage—those who understood were deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 今日當開示誠心，為濟難之本，禦便殿以延見士大夫，以票擬歸閣臣，以庶政歸部、院，以獻可替否予言官。

translations.literal: Today you should reveal sincere heart as the foundation for relieving difficulty: hold court in the side hall to extend audience to scholar-officials, return draft rescripts to the Grand Secretariat, return ordinary administration to ministries and courts, and give remonstrating officials the power to approve what is fit and reject what is not.
translations.idiomatic: Today you should reveal sincere heart as the foundation for relieving difficulty: hold court in the side hall to extend audience to scholar-officials, return draft rescripts to the Grand Secretariat, return ordinary administration to ministries and courts, and give remonstrating officials the power to approve what is fit and reject what is not.

sentences.zh: 不效，從而更置之，無坐錮以成其罪。

translations.literal: If they are ineffective, then replace them accordingly; do not imprison them on the spot to make them guilty.
translations.idiomatic: If they are ineffective, then replace them accordingly; do not imprison them on the spot to make them guilty.

sentences.zh: 乃者朝廷縛文吏如孤雛，而視武健士不啻驕子，漸使恩威錯置。

translations.literal: Lately the court has bound civil officials like lone chicks while treating martial stalwarts no differently from spoiled sons, gradually reversing favor and awe.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the court has bound civil officials like helpless chicks while treating martial stalwarts no differently from spoiled sons, gradually reversing favor and awe.

sentences.zh: 文武皆不足信，乃專任一二內臣，閫以外次第委之。

translations.literal: Neither civil nor military men are trusted enough, and one or two inner eunuchs are exclusively relied upon; beyond the commanderies authority is delegated to them in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Neither civil nor military men are trusted enough, and one or two inner eunuchs are exclusively relied upon; beyond the commanderies authority is delegated to them in turn.

sentences.zh: 自古未有宦官典兵不誤國者。」

translations.literal: From antiquity there has never been a case where eunuchs commanded armies without harming the state."
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity there has never been a case where eunuchs commanded armies without harming the state."

sentences.zh: 又劾馬世龍、張鳳翼、吳阿衡等罪，忤帝意。

translations.literal: He also impeached Ma Shilong, Zhang Fengyi, Wu Aheng, and others for their crimes, offending the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Ma Shilong, Zhang Fengyi, Wu Aheng, and others for their crimes, offending the emperor.

sentences.zh: 三年以疾在告，進祈天永命之說，言：

translations.literal: In the third year, on leave for illness, he advanced the doctrine of praying to Heaven for enduring mandate, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on leave for illness, he advanced the doctrine of praying to Heaven for an enduring mandate, saying:

sentences.zh: 法天之大者，莫過於重民命，則刑罰宜當宜平。

translations.literal: Of the great ways of patterning Heaven, none surpasses valuing the people's lives; then punishments should be fitting and even.
translations.idiomatic: Of the great ways of patterning Heaven, none surpasses valuing the people's lives; then punishments should be fitting and even-handed.

sentences.zh: 陛下以重典繩下，逆黨有誅，封疆失事有誅。

translations.literal: Your Majesty restrains subordinates with heavy statutes: factions of rebellion are punished, frontier failures are punished.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty restrains subordinates with heavy statutes: factions of rebellion are punished, frontier failures are punished.

sentences.zh: 一切詿誤，重者杖死，輕者謫去，朝署中半染赭衣。

translations.literal: All who err in office—the severe are beaten to death, the light are banished; half the court offices are stained with cangue-clothing.
translations.idiomatic: All who err in office—the severe are beaten to death, the light are banished; half the court offices are stained with the garb of punishment.

sentences.zh: 而最傷國體者，無如詔獄。

translations.literal: Yet what most wounds the body's politic is nothing like the imperial prison of edict.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what most wounds the body's politic is nothing like the imperial prison of edict.

sentences.zh: 副都御史易應昌以平反下吏，法司必以鍛煉為忠直，蒼鷹乳虎接踵於天下矣。

translations.literal: Vice censor-in-chief Yi Yingchang was sent down to the clerks for having reversed a verdict; the judicial offices surely take forced confessions for loyalty and uprightness—azure hawks and suckling tigers follow one upon another in the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor-in-chief Yi Yingchang was sent down to the clerks for having reversed a verdict; the judicial offices surely take forced confessions for loyalty and uprightness—ruthless prosecutors follow one upon another throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 願體上天好生之心，首除詔獄，且寬應昌，則祈天永命之一道也。

translations.literal: I wish that you embody Heaven's heart that loves life, first abolish the imperial prison of edict, and moreover pardon Yingchang—then this is one path of praying to Heaven for enduring mandate.
translations.idiomatic: I wish that you embody Heaven's heart that loves life, first abolish the imperial prison of edict, and moreover pardon Yingchang—then this is one path of praying to Heaven for an enduring mandate.

sentences.zh: 法天之大者，莫過於厚民生，則賦斂宜緩宜輕。

translations.literal: Of the great ways of patterning Heaven, none surpasses enriching the people's livelihood; then levies and collections should be slow and light.
translations.idiomatic: Of the great ways of patterning Heaven, none surpasses enriching the people's livelihood; then levies and collections should be slow and light.

sentences.zh: 今者宿逋見征及來歲預征，節節追呼，閭閻困敝，貪吏益大為民厲。

translations.literal: Now arrears in taxes are being collected, and next year's levies are being gathered in advance; section by section collectors press for payment, village lanes are exhausted and ruined, and grasping officials ever more greatly become scourges to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Tax arrears are being exacted at once, and next year's dues are already being collected in advance; at every level collectors hound the people for payment, neighborhoods are worn to exhaustion, and corrupt officials have become an ever greater calamity for common folk.

sentences.zh: 貴州巡按蘇琰以行李被訐於監司。

translations.literal: Guizhou touring censor Su Yan had his baggage denounced before a surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Guizhou, touring censor Su Yan was reported to his superiors over items found in his luggage.

sentences.zh: 巡方黷貨，何問下吏？

translations.literal: When the touring censor greedily accepts goods, why inquire about subordinate clerks?
translations.idiomatic: If the touring inspector himself accepts bribes, why bother investigating his lower-ranking staff?

sentences.zh: 吸膏吮脂之輩，接跡於天下矣。

translations.literal: Those who suck grease and sip fat follow one upon another throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Predatory officials who bleed the people dry are everywhere to be found across the realm.

sentences.zh: 願體上天好生之心，首除新餉，並嚴飭官方，則祈天永命之又一道也。

translations.literal: I wish that you embody Heaven's heart that loves life, first abolish the new military stipend, and also strictly regulate official conduct—then this is another path of praying to Heaven for enduring mandate.
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to honor Heaven's compassion for living things by abolishing the new military levy first and strictly disciplining the official class—another way to seek Heaven's blessing for a lasting reign.

sentences.zh: 然大君者，天之宗子；

translations.literal: Yet the great ruler is Heaven's eldest son by descent;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the sovereign is, after all, Heaven's principal heir;

sentences.zh: 輔臣者，宗子之家相。

translations.literal: the assisting ministers are the eldest son of the clan's household chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: and his chief ministers are the household stewards of that heir.

sentences.zh: 陛下置輔，率由特簡。

translations.literal: Your Majesty appoints assistants, all through special direct selection.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty chooses ministers through special imperial appointment.

sentences.zh: 亦願體一人好生之心，毋驅除異己，構朝士以大獄，結國家朋黨之禍；

translations.literal: I also wish you to embody the heart of one man who loves life, do not drive out and eliminate those unlike yourself, construct great cases against court scholars, and knot the calamity of faction in the state;
translations.idiomatic: I also beg you to share that same humane spirit—do not purge your opponents, manufacture major prosecutions against court officials, and visit upon the state the disaster of factional strife;

sentences.zh: 毋寵利居成功，導人主以富強，釀天下土崩之勢。

translations.literal: Do not favor those who dwell in success for profit, guide the ruler toward wealth and power, and brew the momentum of the empire's collapse like earth crumbling.
translations.idiomatic: Do not coddle those who profit from their achievements, steer the sovereign toward ruthless accumulation of power, and bring about the conditions for the empire to crumble from within.

sentences.zh: 周延儒、溫體仁見疏不懌。

translations.literal: Zhou Yanru and Wen Tiren, upon seeing the memorial, were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yanru and Wen Tiren were displeased when they read the memorial.

sentences.zh: 以時方禱雨，而宗周稱疾，指為偃蹇，激帝怒，擬旨詰之。

translations.literal: Because at that time rain was being prayed for and Zongzhou claimed illness, they pointed to this as insubordinate arrogance, incited the emperor's anger, and drafted an edict to interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: Because the court was praying for rain while Zongzhou claimed illness, they accused him of deliberate defiance, aroused the emperor's wrath, and drafted an imperial reply to rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 且令陳足兵、足餉之策，宗周條畫以對，延儒、體仁不能難。

translations.literal: They moreover ordered him to set forth plans sufficient for troops and sufficient for provisions; Zongzhou laid them out item by item in reply, and Yanru and Tiren could not refute him.
translations.idiomatic: They also demanded that he present plans to supply the army adequately; Zongzhou answered with a detailed program, and neither Yanru nor Tiren could find fault with it.

sentences.zh: 為京尹，政令一新，挫豪家尤力。

translations.literal: Serving as capital intendant, his orders were wholly renewed, and he curbed powerful families with special force.
translations.idiomatic: As mayor of the capital, he overhauled the administration and made a point of reining in the great clans.

sentences.zh: 閹人言事輒不應，或相詬誶，宗周治事自如。

translations.literal: When eunuchs spoke on affairs he invariably did not respond; sometimes they exchanged curses and abuse, yet Zongzhou conducted business as usual.
translations.idiomatic: When eunuchs tried to intervene in his affairs he simply ignored them; some traded insults with him, but Zongzhou kept governing as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 武清伯蒼頭毆諸生，宗周捶之，枷武清門外。

translations.literal: A male servant of the Earl of Wuqing beat a licentiate; Zongzhou beat him, and placed the cangue on him outside Wuqing's gate.
translations.idiomatic: When a retainer of the Earl of Wuqing assaulted a student, Zongzhou had the man beaten and put in the cangue outside the earl's residence.

sentences.zh: 嘗出，見優人籠篋，焚之通衢。

translations.literal: Once going out, he saw an actor's caged chests and burned them in the public thoroughfare.
translations.idiomatic: On one of his outings he saw actors carrying locked trunks; he had them burned in the open street.

sentences.zh: 周恤單丁下戶尤至。

translations.literal: He showed special thoroughness in caring for lone households and lower households.
translations.idiomatic: He showed particular concern for widowed households and the poorest families.

sentences.zh: 居一載，謝病歸，都人為罷市。

translations.literal: After one year in office, he took leave on grounds of illness and returned home; the capital's people went on strike in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After a year in office he resigned citing illness and went home; the people of the capital shut down the markets in protest.

sentences.zh: 八年七月，內閣缺人，命吏部推在籍者，以孫慎行、林釬及宗周名上。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year, the Grand Secretariat lacked personnel; the emperor ordered the Ministry of Personnel to recommend those on leave at home, and submitted the names of Sun Shenxing, Lin Qian, and Zongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the eighth year, with the Grand Secretariat short of members, the emperor ordered the Ministry of Personnel to nominate officials at home on leave, and the names of Sun Shenxing, Lin Qian, and Zongzhou were submitted.

sentences.zh: 詔所司敦趨，宗周固辭不許。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to press them urgently; Zongzhou firmly declined but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commanded the relevant offices to press them to come at once; Zongzhou firmly declined, but the emperor would not accept his refusal.

sentences.zh: 明年正月入都，慎行已卒，與釬入朝。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year he entered the capital; Shenxing had already died, and he entered court together with Qian.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the first month, he reached the capital; Shenxing had already died, and he attended court together with Lin Qian.

sentences.zh: 帝問人才、兵食及流寇猖獗狀。

translations.literal: The emperor inquired about talent, military provisions, and the rampant state of the roving bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked about the availability of capable men, military supplies, and the raging disorder of the roving rebels.

sentences.zh: 宗周言：「陛下求治太急，用法太嚴，布令太煩，進退天下士太輕。

translations.literal: Zongzhou said: "Your Majesty seeks good governance too urgently, applies the law too severely, issues orders too frequently, and treats the advancement and dismissal of men throughout the empire too lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou said: "Your Majesty is too eager for quick results, too harsh in applying the law, too busy issuing orders, and too casual in promoting or dismissing officials throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 諸臣畏罪飾非，不肯盡職業，故有人而無人之用，有餉而無餉之用，有將不能治兵，有兵不能殺賊。

translations.literal: All the ministers, fearing guilt, cover wrongs and are unwilling to fulfill their duties; therefore there are men but no use of men, there are provisions but no use of provisions, there are generals who cannot control troops, and there are troops who cannot kill bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Officials fear punishment and hide their mistakes rather than do their jobs; so there are men but they serve no purpose, funds but they are wasted, generals who cannot discipline their troops, and soldiers who cannot defeat the rebels.

sentences.zh: 流寇本朝廷赤子，撫之有道，則還為民。

translations.literal: The roving bandits are originally the crimson children of the court; if pacified with proper method, they return to become commoners.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel bands are your own people; treat them wisely and they will return to peaceful life as ordinary subjects.

sentences.zh: 今急宜以收拾人心為本，收拾人心在先寬有司。

translations.literal: Now what is urgently fitting is to take the winning back of hearts as the root; to win back hearts, one must first be lenient to the responsible officials.
translations.idiomatic: What matters now above all is winning back popular loyalty, and that begins with easing the pressure on local administrators.

sentences.zh: 參罰重則吏治壞，吏治壞則民生困，盜賊由此日繁。」

translations.literal: When censure and punishment are heavy, official governance is ruined; when official governance is ruined, the people's livelihood is distressed, and bandits and robbers from this daily multiply."
translations.idiomatic: Heavy punishment destroys local governance; ruined governance drives the people to despair—and from that despair, banditry grows daily."

sentences.zh: 帝又問兵事。

translations.literal: The emperor again inquired about military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongzhou had finished speaking, the emperor turned to military affairs.

sentences.zh: 宗周言：「禦外以治內為本。

translations.literal: Zongzhou said: "To defend against the outer, take governance of the inner as root.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou replied: "The key to resisting foreign enemies is to put our own house in order first.

sentences.zh: 內治修，遠人自服，幹羽舞而有苗格。

translations.literal: When inner governance is cultivated, distant people of themselves submit; with shield and feathered dance, the Miao people came.
translations.idiomatic: When domestic order is sound, distant peoples will submit of their own accord—just as the savage Miao yielded when the sage-king danced with shield and plumes rather than fought.

sentences.zh: 願陛下以堯、舜之心，行堯、舜之政，天下自平。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty, with the heart of Yao and Shun, to execute the government of Yao and Shun—then the empire of itself will be pacified."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty governs with the same heart as Yao and Shun and follows their example, the empire will settle itself without further force."

sentences.zh: 對畢趨出。

translations.literal: When the reply was finished he hurried out.
translations.idiomatic: With that he finished his answer and hurried out of the hall.

sentences.zh: 帝顧體仁迂其言，命釬輔政，宗周他用。

translations.literal: The emperor, turning to Tiren, called his words impractical, ordered Qian to assist in government, and assigned Zongzhou elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Wen Tiren, dismissed Zongzhou's advice as unrealistic, named Lin Qian to the Grand Secretariat, and gave Zongzhou a different post.

sentences.zh: 旋授工部左侍郎。

translations.literal: Immediately he was appointed left vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou was soon made left vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 逾月，上《痛憤時艱疏》，言：

translations.literal: After more than a month, he submitted the 《Memorial of Grief and Indignation at the Times' Hardship》, saying:
translations.idiomatic: A month later he submitted the 《Memorial of Grief and Indignation at the Hardships of the Age》, saying:

sentences.zh: 陛下銳意求治，而二帝三王治天下之道未暇講求，施為次第猶多未得要領者。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is keen in spirit to seek good governance, yet the ways by which the two emperors and three kings governed the empire have not had leisure for study and seeking; in sequence of actions many still lack grasp of essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is determined to set things right, yet you have had no time to study the principles by which the sage-kings of antiquity ruled, and much of what has been attempted has missed the mark.

sentences.zh: 首屬意於邊功，而罪督遂以五年恢復之說進，是為禍胎。

translations.literal: First attention was placed on frontier merit, and the frontier governor-general thereupon advanced the proposition of recovery within five years—this was the seed of calamity.
translations.idiomatic: You first fixed your hopes on frontier glory, and the governor-general then put forward the plan to recover lost territory within five years—the seed from which later disasters grew.

sentences.zh: 己巳之役，謀國無良，朝廷始有積輕士大夫之心。

translations.literal: In the Jisi campaign, there were no good men in planning for the state; the court began to harbor accumulated contempt for scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jisi campaign of 1629, the state lacked wise counsel, and the court began to look on the scholar-official class with growing contempt.

sentences.zh: 自此耳目參於近侍，腹心寄於幹城，治術尚刑名，政體歸叢脞，天下事日壞而不可救。

translations.literal: From this, eyes and ears were entrusted to close attendants, the heart and belly were entrusted to military commanders, governing techniques valued legalistic strictness, the governmental structure returned to fragmented trivia, and affairs under Heaven daily worsened beyond saving.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the court's eyes and ears fell to palace attendants, its trust to military commanders, governance came to prize harsh legalism, policy dissolved into petty detail, and the empire's affairs grew worse by the day until they seemed beyond repair.

sentences.zh: 廠衛司譏察，而告訐之風熾；

translations.literal: The Brocade Guard and Palace Guard supervised scrutiny, and the wind of denunciation flared;
translations.idiomatic: The secret police kept watch on all sides, and the culture of informers flourished;

sentences.zh: 詔獄及士紳，而堂廉之等夷；

translations.literal: the imperial prison of edict reached scholar-gentry, and the hall and courtyard were made equal;
translations.idiomatic: the imperial prison reached even into the gentry, and no distinction remained between high office and low;

sentences.zh: 人人救過不給，而欺罔之習轉甚；

translations.literal: everyone barely saved themselves from fault, and the habit of deceit grew ever more severe;
translations.idiomatic: everyone scrambled merely to avoid blame, and deceit became ever more widespread;

sentences.zh: 事事仰成獨斷，而諂諛之風日長。

translations.literal: in every matter one looked upward to sole decision, and the wind of flattery daily lengthened.
translations.idiomatic: every decision awaited the emperor's word alone, and flattery grew day by day.

sentences.zh: 三尺法不伸於司寇，而犯者日眾，詔旨雜治五刑，歲躬斷獄以數千，而好生之德意泯。

translations.literal: The three-foot law did not extend to the Minister of Justice, yet offenders daily multiplied; imperial edicts mixed in administering the five punishments, each year personally judging cases by the thousands, and the virtuous intent to love life was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The law no longer ran through the Ministry of Justice, yet offenders multiplied daily; imperial edicts piled punishment upon punishment, and the emperor personally judged thousands of cases each year until the virtue of sparing life was altogether lost.

sentences.zh: 刀筆治絲綸而王言褻，誅求及瑣屑而政體傷。

translations.literal: Clerks' writing governed imperial pronouncements and the king's words were debased; extortionate demands reached trivialities and the governmental structure was wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Petty scribes shaped the emperor's decrees until the throne's words lost their dignity, and exactions reached down to the smallest matters until the body of government itself was injured.

sentences.zh: 參罰在錢谷而官愈貪，吏愈橫，賦愈逋；

translations.literal: Censure and punishment fell on grain and tribute accounts, yet officials grew greedier, clerks grew more overbearing, and tax arrearage grew greater;
translations.idiomatic: Punishment fell heaviest on tax collection, yet officials grew greedier, clerks more brutal, and arrears ever larger;

sentences.zh: 敲撲繁而民生瘁，嚴刑重斂交困而盜賊日起。

translations.literal: Beating and flogging multiplied and the people's livelihood was exhausted; harsh punishments and heavy exactions together distressed, and bandits and robbers daily arose.
translations.idiomatic: Beatings multiplied until the people were worn to the bone; harsh law and heavy levies together crushed them, and banditry rose day by day.

sentences.zh: 總理任而臣下之功能薄，監視遣而封疆之責任輕。

translations.literal: When a grand coordinator was appointed, the ministers' functional capacity grew thin; when supervising inspectors were dispatched, frontier responsibilities grew light.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint a grand coordinator and the ministers' real authority thins; dispatch supervising commissioners and frontier commanders' responsibility grows faint.

sentences.zh: 督、撫無權而將日懦，武弁廢法而兵日驕，將懦兵驕而朝廷之威令並窮於督、撫。

translations.literal: Governors and governors-general had no authority and generals daily grew cowardly; military officers abandoned the law and troops daily grew arrogant; generals cowardly and troops arrogant, and the court's awestriking commands together reached exhaustion at governors and governors-general.
translations.idiomatic: Governors and governors-general lost real power and generals grew daily more timid; military officers ignored the law and soldiers grew daily more insolent—and with cowardly generals and arrogant troops, the court's authority stopped at the desk of every frontier commander.

sentences.zh: 朝廷勒限平賊，而行間日殺良報功，生靈益塗炭。

translations.literal: The court imposed deadlines to pacify bandits, yet in the camps they daily killed the innocent to report merit, and living souls ever more suffered charred destruction.
translations.idiomatic: The court set deadlines for suppressing rebels, yet in the field commanders daily killed innocent people to claim credit, and the common folk suffered ever more grievously.

sentences.zh: 一旦天牖聖衷，撤總監之任，重守令之選，下弓旌之招，收酷吏之威，布維新之化，方與二三臣工洗心滌慮，以聯泰交，而不意君臣相遇之難也。

translations.literal: Once Heaven opened the sage heart, the grand supervisor's appointment was withdrawn, the selection of prefects and magistrates was weighted, the bow-and-banner summons was issued, the awestriking power of harsh officials was reined in, and renewing transformation was proclaimed—only then, together with two or three ministers, to wash the heart and cleanse thoughts and join in great harmony, yet one did not expect the difficulty of ruler and minister meeting.
translations.idiomatic: Then Heaven seemed at last to move your heart: you removed the grand supervisors, chose local officials with greater care, issued invitations to worthy men, reined in ruthless magistrates, and proclaimed a new beginning—I and a few colleagues had begun to wash away our doubts and hope for genuine accord between ruler and ministers, never imagining how hard that meeting would prove.

sentences.zh: 得一文震孟而以單辭報罷，使大臣失和衷之誼；

translations.literal: Gaining one Wen Zhenmeng and dismissing him on a single phrase, causing great ministers to lose the bond of harmonious accord;
translations.idiomatic: You found a man like Wen Zhenmeng and dismissed him on a single accusation, breaking the bond of trust among your chief ministers;

sentences.zh: 得一陳子壯而以過戇坐辜，使朝寧無籲咈之風。

translations.literal: Gaining one Chen Zizhuang and making him guilty through excessive bluntness, causing the court to lack the wind of anxious remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: You found a man like Chen Zizhuang and punished him for excessive bluntness, until the court no longer heard the anxious voice of honest remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 此關於國體人心非淺鮮者。

translations.literal: This concerns the state's body and popular hearts—not shallow or slight.
translations.idiomatic: These matters touch the very body of the state and the hearts of the people; they are no small thing.

sentences.zh: 陛下必體上天生物之心以敬天，而不徒倚風雷；

translations.literal: Your Majesty must embody Heaven's heart of generating things to revere Heaven, and not merely rely on wind and thunder;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty must honor Heaven by sharing its will to nurture life, and not rely on thunder and terror alone;

sentences.zh: 必念祖宗鑒古之制以率祖，而不輕改作。

translations.literal: Must remember the ancestral system of taking antiquity as mirror to follow the ancestors, and not lightly make changes.
translations.idiomatic: You must follow the ancestral institutions that took antiquity as their guide, and not change them lightly.

sentences.zh: 以簡要出政令，以寬大養人才，以忠厚培國脈。

translations.literal: Issue governmental orders with brevity and essentials, nurture talent with magnanimity, and cultivate the nation's vital pulse with loyalty and generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Issue orders that are brief and to the point, nurture talent with generosity, and strengthen the nation's lifeblood with loyalty and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 發政施仁，收天下泮渙之人心，而且還內廷掃除之役，正懦帥失律之誅，慎天潢改授之途。

translations.literal: Proclaim policies and bestow benevolence, gather the dispersed hearts of all under Heaven—and moreover restore inner-court sweeping duties, rectify the punishment of cowardly commanders who violated discipline, and be cautious in the path of altering fief assignments for imperial clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: Proclaim benevolent policies and win back the scattered loyalty of the realm; restore the inner court to its proper duties, punish cowardly commanders who broke discipline, and be cautious in altering the fiefs of imperial clansmen.

sentences.zh: 遣廷臣賫內帑巡行郡國為招撫使，赦其無罪而流亡者。

translations.literal: Dispatch court officials bearing inner treasury funds to tour commanderies and kingdoms as pacification commissioners, pardoning those who fled without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Send court officials with funds from the inner treasury to tour the provinces as pacification commissioners, and pardon those who fled into exile without guilt.

sentences.zh: 陳師險隘，堅壁清野，聽其窮而自歸。

translations.literal: Deploy troops at strategic passes, strengthen walls and clear the countryside, and let them exhaust themselves and return of their own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Station troops at strategic passes, fortify defenses and clear the countryside, and let the rebels exhaust themselves until they surrender of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 誅渠之外，猶可不殺一人，而畢此役，奚待於觀兵哉。

translations.literal: Beyond punishing the ringleaders, one may yet need to kill not a single person and complete this campaign—why wait to review troops.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond punishing the ringleaders, you could finish this campaign without killing another soul—why must you parade the army in review.

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝怒甚，諭閣臣擬嚴旨再四。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor was exceedingly angry and instructed the Grand Secretariat ministers to draft stern edicts again and again.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor was furious and repeatedly ordered the Grand Secretariat to draft a harsh reply.

sentences.zh: 每擬上，帝輒手其疏覆閱，起行數周。

translations.literal: Each time one was drafted and submitted, the emperor would take the memorial in hand and read it again, rising and walking several circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Each time a draft was submitted, the emperor would take the memorial in hand, read it again, rise from his seat, and pace back and forth several times.

sentences.zh: 已而意解，降旨詰問，謂大臣論事宜體國度時，不當效小臣歸過朝廷為名高，且獎其清直焉。

translations.literal: Before long his mood softened; he issued an edict of inquiry, saying that great ministers discussing affairs should consider the state and measure the times, and should not imitate petty officials who shift blame to the court to gain a name for integrity—and yet praised his purity and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his anger cooled; he issued an edict of inquiry, saying that senior ministers should weigh affairs in light of the state's needs and the times, and should not imitate petty officials who blame the court to burnish their own reputations—yet he also praised Zongzhou's integrity and blunt honesty.

sentences.zh: 時太仆缺馬價，有詔願捐者聽，體仁及成國公朱純臣以下皆有捐助。

translations.literal: At that time the Court of the Imperial Stud lacked funds for horse prices; an edict permitted those willing to donate, and Tiren together with the Duke of Chengguo Zhu Chunchen and those below all made contributions.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Court of the Imperial Stud lacked funds for horse prices; an edict invited voluntary donations, and Wen Tiren, the Duke of Chengguo Zhu Chunchen, and many others contributed.

sentences.zh: 又議罷明年朝覲。

translations.literal: They also deliberated abolishing next year's court audience tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: The court also debated canceling the next year's tribute audience at court.

sentences.zh: 宗周以輸貲、免覲為大辱國。

translations.literal: Zongzhou regarded paying tribute contributions and exempting court audiences as great disgrace to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou regarded soliciting donations and canceling court audiences as a grave humiliation for the state.

sentences.zh: 帝雖不悅，心善其忠，益欲大用。

translations.literal: Though the emperor was displeased, in his heart he approved his loyalty and wished all the more to employ him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased, but in his heart he admired Zongzhou's loyalty and wanted all the more to give him greater responsibility.

sentences.zh: 體仁患之，募山陰人許瑚疏論之，謂宗周道學有余，才谞不足。

translations.literal: Tiren feared this; he recruited a man of Shanyin named Xu Hu to submit a memorial discussing him, saying Zongzhou had abundance in the learning of the Way but insufficiency in practical talent and judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tiren feared this outcome and recruited a fellow townsman from Shanyin named Xu Hu to submit a memorial arguing that Zongzhou was strong in moral learning but weak in practical judgment.

sentences.zh: 帝以瑚同邑，知之宜真，遂已不用。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Hu was from the same district and should know truly, thereupon ceased further appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xu Hu came from the same district as Zongzhou, the emperor took his account as reliable and dropped the plan to promote him further.

sentences.zh: 其秋，三疏請告去。

translations.literal: That autumn, thrice by memorial he requested leave to depart.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he submitted three memorials asking to resign and leave office.

sentences.zh: 至天津，聞都城被兵，遂留養疾。

translations.literal: Reaching Tianjin, he heard the capital was under attack by troops, and therefore remained to nurse his illness.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Tianjin he learned that the capital was under attack, and so he stayed there to recover from his illness.

sentences.zh: 十月，事稍定，乃上疏曰：

translations.literal: In the tenth month, when affairs had somewhat settled, he then submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, once affairs had settled somewhat, he submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 己巳之變，誤國者袁崇煥一人。

translations.literal: The change of Jisi—he who misled the state was Yuan Chonghuan alone.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jisi crisis, Yuan Chonghuan alone misled the state.

sentences.zh: 小人競修門戶之怨，異己者概坐以崇煥黨，日造蜚語，次第去之。

translations.literal: Petty men competed to nurture factional resentments; those unlike themselves were broadly implicated as members of Chonghuan's faction, daily fabricating slander, and removed them in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men competed to settle old factional scores; anyone who differed from them was branded a member of Chonghuan's clique, slandered day after day, and driven from office one by one.

sentences.zh: 自此小人進而君子退，中官用事而外廷浸疏。

translations.literal: From this petty men advanced while gentlemen withdrew; palace eunuchs managed affairs while the outer court was gradually estranged.
translations.idiomatic: From that point petty men rose while upright officials fell back; eunuchs handled affairs while the outer court was steadily pushed aside.

sentences.zh: 文法日繁，欺罔日甚，朝政日隳，邊防日壞。

translations.literal: Legalistic forms daily multiplied, deceit daily intensified, court governance daily collapsed, and frontier defense daily worsened.
translations.idiomatic: Paperwork multiplied daily, deceit grew worse daily, court governance decayed daily, and frontier defense deteriorated daily.

sentences.zh: 今日之禍，實己巳以來釀成之也。

translations.literal: Today's calamity was in fact brewed since Jisi.
translations.idiomatic: The disaster we face today has in truth been brewing ever since the Jisi crisis.

sentences.zh: 且以張鳳翼之溺職中樞也，而俾之專征，何以服王洽之死？

translations.literal: Moreover, with Zhang Fengyi's dereliction of duty at the central pivot, yet appointing him to sole command of expeditions—how can this satisfy Wang Qia's death?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fengyi was derelict at the center of government, yet you gave him sole command of the campaign—how can that answer for the death of Wang Qia?

sentences.zh: 以丁魁楚等之失事於邊也，而責之戴罪，何以服劉策之死？

translations.literal: With Ding Kuichu and others' failures on the frontier, yet charging them to serve while bearing guilt—how can this satisfy Liu Ce's death?
translations.idiomatic: Ding Kuichu and others failed on the frontier, yet you allowed them to serve while bearing guilt—how can that answer for the death of Liu Ce?

sentences.zh: 諸鎮勤王之師，爭先入衛者幾人，不聞以逗留蒙詰責，何以服耿如杞之死？

translations.literal: Among the relief armies from various garrisons, how many competed to enter the capital first to defend it—and none are heard to have received censure for delay; how can this satisfy Geng Ruju's death?
translations.idiomatic: Of the relief armies sent from the garrisons, how many raced to reach the capital first—and none were punished for delay; how can that answer for the death of Geng Ruju?

sentences.zh: 今且以二州八縣之生靈，結一飽飏之局，則廷臣之累累若若可幸無罪者，又何以謝韓爌、張鳳翔、李邦華諸臣之或戍或去？

translations.literal: And now, to take the living souls of two prefectures and eight counties and settle one fully-fed bandit situation—then how can the court officials who accumulate in numbers as if fortunate and blameless answer to Han Kuang, Zhang Fengxiang, Li Banghua, and other ministers who were either banished to frontier service or dismissed?
translations.idiomatic: And now you would spend the people of two prefectures and eight counties merely to settle the affairs of a band of well-fed marauders—how then can the court officials who crowd together as if they had nothing to answer for make amends to Han Kuang, Zhang Fengxiang, Li Banghua, and others who were banished or driven from office?

sentences.zh: 豈昔為異己驅除，今不難以同己相容隱乎？

translations.literal: Was it not that in the past they drove out those unlike themselves, yet today find no difficulty in shielding those like themselves?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not that they once purged their opponents without mercy, yet today find it easy enough to shield their own allies?

sentences.zh: 臣於是而知小人之禍人國無已時也。

translations.literal: Your servant thereby understands that petty men's calamitizing the state knows no end.
translations.idiomatic: From this I understand that petty men will never stop bringing calamity upon the state.

sentences.zh: 昔唐德宗謂群臣曰：「人言盧杞奸邪，朕殊不覺。」

translations.literal: Formerly Tang Dezong said to his assembled ministers: "People say Lu Qi is treacherous and wicked; I am wholly unaware of it."
translations.idiomatic: Once Tang Dezong said to his ministers: "People say Lu Qi is treacherous and wicked, but I myself notice nothing of the kind."

sentences.zh: 群臣對曰：「此乃杞之所以為奸邪也。」

translations.literal: The assembled ministers replied: "This is precisely why Qi is treacherous and wicked."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers replied: "That is precisely what makes Lu Qi treacherous and wicked."

sentences.zh: 臣每三覆斯言，為萬世辨奸之要。

translations.literal: Your servant thrice reverently reviews this saying—as the essential key to distinguishing treachery for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: I have pondered this saying again and again; it holds the essential key to unmasking villains for all time.

sentences.zh: 故曰：「大奸似忠，大佞似信。」

translations.literal: Therefore it is said: "The greatest villain resembles loyalty; the greatest flatterer resembles faithfulness."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: "The greatest villain looks loyal; the greatest flatterer looks sincere."

sentences.zh: 頻年以來，陛下惡私交，而臣下多以告訐進；

translations.literal: In recent years Your Majesty hates private associations, yet ministers mostly advance through denunciation;
translations.idiomatic: In recent years Your Majesty has hated cliques and private alliances, yet officials have mostly risen by informing on one another;

sentences.zh: 陛下錄清節，而臣下多以曲謹容；

translations.literal: Your Majesty records pure integrity, yet ministers mostly gain acceptance through cautious compliance;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has valued integrity, yet officials have mostly won favor through cautious conformity;

sentences.zh: 陛下崇勵精，而臣下奔走承順以為恭；

translations.literal: Your Majesty exalts striving diligence, yet ministers rush about in compliance and take this for respect;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has prized diligence, yet officials have rushed to agree with you and called that respect;

sentences.zh: 陛下尚綜核，而臣下瑣屑吹求以示察。

translations.literal: Your Majesty still values comprehensive scrutiny, yet ministers pick at trivialities and blow upon them to display keenness.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has valued thorough oversight, yet officials have nitpicked petty matters to show how sharp they are.

sentences.zh: 凡若此者，正似信似忠之類，究其用心，無往不出於身家利祿。

translations.literal: All such are precisely the sort that seem faithful and seem loyal; investigating their intentions, nothing fails to proceed from personal profit and emolument.
translations.idiomatic: All such men belong to the very type that looks loyal and sincere; examine their motives and you find nothing but self-interest and salary.

sentences.zh: 陛下不察而用之，則聚天下之小人立於朝，有所不覺矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not discern and yet employs them, then all the petty men under Heaven will stand in court—and you will be unaware of it.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty fails to see through them and keeps employing them, you will gather every petty man in the empire at court without even realizing it.

sentences.zh: 天下即乏才，何至盡出中官下？

translations.literal: Even if talent under Heaven is scarce, how could it reach the point that all emerge from beneath eunuchs?
translations.idiomatic: Even if the realm lacks talent, how could it be that every capable man comes from the ranks of the eunuchs?

sentences.zh: 而陛下每當緩急，必委以大任。

translations.literal: Yet whenever Your Majesty faces urgency, you invariably entrust them with great responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever crisis comes, Your Majesty invariably entrusts them with great responsibility.

sentences.zh: 三協有遣，通、津、臨、德有遣；

translations.literal: The three auxiliaries had dispatches; Tongzhou, Tianjin, Linqing, and Dezhou had dispatches;
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch commissioners were sent to the three auxiliary garrisons, and to Tongzhou, Tianjin, Linqing, and Dezhou;

sentences.zh: 又重其體統，等之總督。

translations.literal: Moreover their status was weighted, made equal to governors-general.
translations.idiomatic: Their rank was then raised until it matched that of governors-general.

sentences.zh: 中官總督，置總督何地？

translations.literal: Eunuch governors-general—where then is the place for governors-general?
translations.idiomatic: If eunuchs serve as governors-general, what place is left for the actual governors-general?

sentences.zh: 總督無權，置撫、按何地？

translations.literal: The governor-general has no authority—then where is the place for establishing governors and censors?
translations.idiomatic: If the governor-general has no real power, what purpose is there in appointing provincial governors and censors?

sentences.zh: 是以封疆嘗試也。

translations.literal: Thus the frontier posts were repeatedly put to trial.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the border provinces became a proving ground.

sentences.zh: 且小人每比周小人，以相引重，君子獨岸然自異。

translations.literal: Moreover petty men always band together with petty men to mutually boost each other's weight, while the gentleman alone stands aloof in self-difference.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men constantly band together to bolster one another, while the gentleman stands apart in dignified independence.

sentences.zh: 故自古有用小人之君子，終無黨比小人之君子。

translations.literal: Thus since antiquity there have been gentlemen who employ petty men, yet ultimately there are no gentlemen who form factions with petty men.
translations.idiomatic: There have always been upright officials who made use of lesser men, but no upright official has ever joined a faction of them.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠欲進君子退小人，決理亂消長之機，猶復用中官參制之，此明示以左右袒也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly wishes to advance gentlemen and dismiss petty men, deciding the pivot of order and chaos and waxing and waning, yet again uses eunuchs to interfere and restrain—this openly shows them which sleeve to bare.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly wishes to promote the upright and remove the corrupt—the very hinge on which order and chaos turn—yet still lets eunuchs interfere, you are openly telling them which side to favor.

sentences.zh: 有明治理者起而爭之，陛下即不用其言，何至並逐其人？

translations.literal: When one who clearly understands governance rises to dispute it, even if Your Majesty does not employ his words, how need it reach the point of also expelling the man?
translations.idiomatic: When a clear-sighted minister remonstrates, even if Your Majesty rejects his advice, why must you also drive him from office?

sentences.zh: 而御史金光辰竟以此逐，若惟恐傷中官心者，尤非所以示天下也。

translations.literal: Yet Censor Jin Guangchen was actually expelled for this, as though fearing to wound eunuch hearts—it is especially not how to show the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Censor Jin Guangchen was actually dismissed for it, as if Your Majesty feared offending the eunuchs—that is scarcely the message to send the empire.

sentences.zh: 至今日刑政之最舛者，成德，傲吏也，而以贓戍，何以肅懲貪之令？

translations.literal: As for today's most errant criminal administration: Cheng De was an arrogant official, yet was banished for embezzlement—how can this enforce the command to punish greed?
translations.idiomatic: Among today's worst abuses of criminal justice: Cheng De was an overbearing official, yet he was banished only on a corruption charge—how does that vindicate the decree against graft?

sentences.zh: 申紹芳，十余年監司也，而以莫須有之鉆刺戍，何以昭抑競之典？

translations.literal: Shen Shaofang had been a provincial inspector for more than ten years, yet was banished for baseless soliciting and drilling—how can this manifest the canon restraining factional rivalry?
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shaofang had served more than ten years as a provincial inspector, yet was banished on a trumped-up charge of lobbying—how does that uphold the standard meant to curb factionalism?

sentences.zh: 鄭鄤之獄，或以誣告坐，何以示敦倫之化？

translations.literal: In the Zheng Yan case, one was punished on a false accusation—how can this display the transformation of reverencing human relations?
translations.idiomatic: In the Zheng Yan affair, men were punished on false charges—how does that teach the people to honor family duty?

sentences.zh: 此數事者，皆為故輔文震孟引繩批根，即向驅除異己之故智，而廷臣無敢言。

translations.literal: These several matters were all through the former aide Wen Zhenmeng drawing the cord and striking at the root—the very old artifice of driving out those unlike oneself—and court ministers dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: In each of these cases the former Grand Secretary Wen Zhenmeng pulled strings and settled scores—the old trick of purging rivals—and no courtier dared object.

sentences.zh: 陛下亦無從知之也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty also had no means from which to know it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty had no way of learning any of this.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，八年之間，誰秉國成，而至於是！

translations.literal: Alas, within eight years, who held the nation's destiny—and it reached this point!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—in eight years, who held the reins of government, that things have come to this!

sentences.zh: 臣不能為首揆溫體仁解矣。

translations.literal: This minister cannot explicate for the Chief Grand Secretary Wen Tiren.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant cannot defend Chief Grand Secretary Wen Tiren.

sentences.zh: 語曰：「誰生厲階，至今為梗。」

translations.literal: The saying goes: "Who raised the evil step, that to this day remains a stumbling block."
translations.idiomatic: As the ode says: "Who raised the mischief—still, to this day, a grievous thorn?"

sentences.zh: 體仁之謂也。

translations.literal: This refers to Tiren.
translations.idiomatic: That describes Tiren.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝大怒，體仁又上章力詆，遂斥為民。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor was greatly angered; Tiren also submitted a memorial vigorously denouncing, and he was thereupon expelled as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne the Emperor flew into a rage; Tiren submitted a furious rebuttal, and Zongzhou was reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 十四年九月，吏部缺左侍郎，廷推不稱旨。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourteenth year, the Ministry of Personnel lacked a Left Vice Minister; court recommendation did not suit the imperial mind.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year fourteen the Ministry of Personnel needed a Left Vice Minister; the court's nomination did not please the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝臨朝而嘆，謂大臣：「劉宗周清正敢言，可用也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor attended court and sighed, telling the ministers: "Liu Zongzhou is upright and clear and dares to speak—he can be used."
translations.idiomatic: At court the Emperor sighed and told his ministers: "Liu Zongzhou is honest and outspoken—he will serve well."

sentences.zh: 遂以命之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was made at once.

sentences.zh: 再辭不得，乃趨朝。

translations.literal: He declined twice but could not succeed, and thereupon hastened to court.
translations.idiomatic: He declined twice but could not refuse, and set out for the capital.

sentences.zh: 道中進三劄：一曰明聖學以端治本，二曰躬聖學以建治要，三曰重聖學以需治化，凡數千言。

translations.literal: En route he submitted three memorials: first, clarifying sagely learning to set right the root of governance; second, personally practicing sagely learning to establish the essentials of order; third, honoring sagely learning to await the transformation of governance—altogether several thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he submitted three memorials: on clarifying sage learning as the foundation of rule; on embodying it as the core of government; and on upholding it as the path to a well-ordered realm—in all, several thousand words.

sentences.zh: 帝優旨報之。

translations.literal: The Emperor replied with gracious edict.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor responded with a warm commendation.

sentences.zh: 明年八月，未至擢左都御史。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the following year, before he had arrived he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The following August, before he even reached the capital, he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 力辭，有詔敦趨。

translations.literal: He vigorously declined; an edict urgently pressed him on.
translations.idiomatic: He protested vigorously, but an imperial order commanded him to proceed at once.

sentences.zh: 逾月，入見文華殿。

translations.literal: After more than a month, he entered for audience at the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was received in audience at Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝問都察院職掌安在，對曰：「在正己以正百僚。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked where lay the Censorate's charge; he replied: "It lies in rectifying oneself to rectify the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked what the Censorate's duty was. He answered: "To set one's own house in order, and thereby set the bureaucracy in order.

sentences.zh: 必存諸中者，上可對君父，下可質天下士大夫，而後百僚則而象之。
