translations.literal: What must be preserved within: above, one can answer to sovereign and father; below, one can hold account before the empire's scholar-officials—only then do the hundred officials take it as model and mirror it.
translations.idiomatic: What must be kept within: uprightness before sovereign and father, integrity before every scholar-official under Heaven—only then will the bureaucracy take that standard as its mirror.

sentences.zh: 大臣法，小臣廉，紀綱振肅，職掌在是，而責成巡方其首務也。

translations.literal: Great ministers set the law; petty ministers show integrity; statutes are roused and disciplined—the charge lies herein, and holding provincial inspectors accountable is the foremost task.
translations.idiomatic: Senior officials must uphold the law, junior officials must stay honest, and discipline must be restored—that is the duty, and holding touring censors accountable comes first.

sentences.zh: 巡方得人，則吏治清，民生遂。」

translations.literal: If provincial inspection gets the right men, then official administration is clear and the people's livelihood prospers."
translations.idiomatic: Appoint the right men as touring censors, and local governance will be clean and the people will thrive."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿力行以副朕望。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Minister, exert yourself to fulfill my expectations."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Carry this out with all your strength, as I expect of you."

sentences.zh: 乃列建道揆、貞法守、崇國體、清伏奸、懲官邪、飭吏治六事以獻，帝褒納焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he listed six matters—establishing the course of governance, steadfast law-keeping, exalting the body politic, clearing hidden villains, punishing official corruption, and rectifying official administration—to present; the Emperor praised and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a program of six reforms: restoring proper governance, upholding the law, defending the dignity of the state, uprooting hidden enemies, punishing corrupt officials, and tightening administrative discipline—and the Emperor approved it warmly.

sentences.zh: 俄劾御史喻上猷、嚴雲京而薦袁愷、成勇，帝並從之。

translations.literal: Shortly he impeached Censors Yu Shangyou and Yan Yunjing and recommended Yuan Kai and Cheng Yong; the Emperor approved both.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he impeached Censors Yu Shangyou and Yan Yunjing and recommended Yuan Kai and Cheng Yong in their place—the Emperor agreed to both.

sentences.zh: 其後上猷受李自成顯職，卒為世大詬。

translations.literal: Subsequently Shangyou accepted a prominent office from Li Zicheng, and in the end became greatly reviled by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shangyou later accepted a high post from Li Zicheng and was forever after condemned by posterity.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，京師被兵。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, the capital was struck by troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter the capital came under attack.

sentences.zh: 請旌死事盧象升，而追戮誤國奸臣楊嗣昌，逮跋扈悍將左良玉；

translations.literal: He requested encomiums for Lu Xiangsheng who died in service, while pursuing execution of the state-harming traitorous minister Yang Sichang, and arresting the overbearing fierce general Zuo Liangyu;
translations.idiomatic: He called for honors for Lu Xiangsheng, who had died in the field; for posthumous punishment of Yang Sichang, the minister who had betrayed the realm; and for the arrest of the domineering general Zuo Liangyu;

sentences.zh: 防關以備反攻，防潞以備透渡，防通、津、臨、德以備南下。

translations.literal: Defend the pass to guard against counterattack; defend Lu to guard against piercing crossing; defend Tongzhou, Tianjin, Linqing, and Dezhou to guard against southward descent.
translations.idiomatic: Fortify the passes against a rebel counterthrust; hold Lu against a breakthrough crossing; and strengthen Tongzhou, Tianjin, Linqing, and Dezhou against a southward advance.

sentences.zh: 帝不能盡行。

translations.literal: The Emperor could not fully carry it all out.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor could not adopt all of these measures.

sentences.zh: 閏月晦日召見廷臣於中左門。

translations.literal: On the last day of the intercalary month he summoned court ministers for audience at the Middle Left Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the intercalary month he summoned his ministers to audience at the Middle Left Gate.

sentences.zh: 時姜埰、熊開元以言事下詔獄，宗周約九卿共救。

translations.literal: At the time Jiang Cai and Xiong Kaiyuan had been sent to the imperial prison for speaking on affairs; Zongzhou arranged for the Nine Ministers jointly to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Cai and Xiong Kaiyuan had been thrown into the imperial prison for remonstrating; Zongzhou rallied the Nine Ministers to intercede.

sentences.zh: 入朝，聞密旨置二人死。

translations.literal: Entering court, he heard a secret edict set the two men to death.
translations.idiomatic: On entering court he learned that a secret order had condemned both men to death.

sentences.zh: 宗周愕然謂眾曰：「今日當空署爭，必改發刑部始已。」

translations.literal: Zongzhou, startled, told the crowd: "Today we must argue with empty seals; only when it is changed and sent to the Ministry of Punishments will it stop."
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou stared in shock and told the others: "Today we must remonstrate with every seal left blank—we cannot rest until the case is transferred to the Ministry of Justice."

sentences.zh: 及入對，御史楊若橋薦西洋人湯若望善火器，請召試。

translations.literal: When they entered for response, Censor Yang Ruoqiao recommended the Western man Adam Schall as skilled in firearms, requesting summoning for trial.
translations.idiomatic: When they came before the throne, Censor Yang Ruoqiao recommended the Westerner Adam Schall as an expert in firearms and asked that he be summoned for a trial demonstration.

sentences.zh: 宗周曰：「邊臣不講戰守屯戍之法，專恃火器。

translations.literal: Zongzhou said: "Border ministers do not discuss methods of fighting, defending, garrisoning, and stationing troops—they rely solely on firearms.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou said: "Frontier officials no longer study the arts of defense and garrison duty—they rely entirely on firearms.

sentences.zh: 近來陷城破邑，豈無火器而然？

translations.literal: In recent times cities have fallen and towns been broken—was it because there were no firearms that this happened?
translations.idiomatic: Cities have fallen one after another lately—is that because we lacked firearms?

sentences.zh: 我用之制人，人得之亦可制我，不見河間反為火器所破乎？

translations.literal: When we use them to control others, if others obtain them they can also control us—have you not seen Hejian in turn broken by firearms?
translations.idiomatic: We use them to subdue the enemy, but once the enemy has them they can subdue us—did not Hejian fall precisely to enemy firearms?

sentences.zh: 國家大計，以法紀為主。

translations.literal: The great plan of the state takes law and discipline as its mainstay.
translations.idiomatic: The fundamental policy of the state rests on law and discipline.

sentences.zh: 大帥跋扈，援師逗遛，奈何反姑息，為此紛紛無益之舉耶？」

translations.literal: Great commanders are overbearing, relief armies dawdle and linger—why instead show indulgence and make these confused, useless moves?"
translations.idiomatic: Field marshals grow insubordinate and relief columns stall—why indulge them and waste effort on such useless schemes?"

sentences.zh: 因議督、撫去留，則請先去督師範誌完。

translations.literal: Thereupon in discussing the removal or retention of governors-general and governors, he requested first removing Grand Secretary Fan Zhichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Turning to the question of which commanders should stay or go, he called first for the removal of Supreme Commander Fan Zhichuan.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「十五年來，陛下處分未當，致有今日敗局。

translations.literal: Moreover he said: "For fifteen years Your Majesty's dispositions have not been apt, leading to today's defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "For fifteen years Your Majesty's decisions have missed the mark, and that has brought us to today's ruin.

sentences.zh: 不追禍始，更弦易轍，欲以一切茍且之政，補目前罅漏，非長治之道也。」

translations.literal: Without tracing the origin of calamity and changing the strings and altering the track, wishing to use every makeshift policy to patch present cracks and leaks—is not the way of long-lasting order."
translations.idiomatic: Without reckoning with how disaster began, and instead trying to patch present failures with every expedient at hand—that is not the path to lasting stability."

sentences.zh: 帝變色曰：「前不可追，善後安在？」

translations.literal: The Emperor changed color and said: "The past cannot be pursued—where lies the good aftermath?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's face darkened. "The past cannot be undone—what then is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 宗周曰：「在陛下開誠布公，公天下為好惡，合國人為用舍，進賢才，開言路，次第與天下更始。」

translations.literal: Zongzhou said: "It lies in Your Majesty opening sincerity and spreading fairness, making the empire's likes and dislikes public, gathering the nation's people for appointment and dismissal, advancing worthy talent, opening the path of speech, and step by step renewing all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou answered: "Your Majesty must speak plainly and govern openly—let the whole realm share in judgment of right and wrong, let the nation participate in choosing officials, promote talent, open the channels of remonstrance, and step by step begin anew with the people."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「目下烽火逼畿甸，且國家敗壞已極，當如何？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "At present beacon fires press upon the capital region, and moreover the state's ruin is already extreme—what ought to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "War fires are already at the capital's gates, and the state is near collapse—what is to be done now?"

sentences.zh: 宗周曰：「武備必先練兵，練兵必先選將，選將必先擇賢督、撫，擇賢督、撫必先吏、兵二部得人。

translations.literal: Zongzhou said: "Military readiness must first train troops; training troops must first select generals; selecting generals must first choose worthy governors-general and governors; choosing worthy governors-general and governors must first have the Ministries of Personnel and War get the right men.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou said: "Military strength begins with trained soldiers; trained soldiers require chosen generals; good generals require worthy governors and commanders; and worthy governors require the right leaders in the Ministries of Personnel and War.

sentences.zh: 宋臣曰：『文官不愛錢，武官不惜死，則天下太平。』

translations.literal: A Song minister said: "[If] civil officials do not love money and military officials do not spare death, then all under Heaven is at peace."
translations.idiomatic: As a Song statesman said: "When civil officials refuse bribes and military officers fear no death, the realm is at peace."

sentences.zh: 斯言，今日針砭也。

translations.literal: This saying is today's needle-stone therapy.
translations.idiomatic: Those words are the very medicine the age needs.

sentences.zh: 論者但論才望，不問操守；

translations.literal: Discussers only discuss talent and reputation, not asking about integrity of conduct;
translations.idiomatic: Men are judged today only on brilliance and reputation, never on moral character;

sentences.zh: 未有操守不謹，而遇事敢前，軍士畏威者。

translations.literal: There never has been one whose conduct was not strict yet who dared advance when matters arose and whose soldiers feared his authority.
translations.idiomatic: no commander lacking in integrity has ever dared lead from the front or inspired real discipline in his troops.

sentences.zh: 若徒以議論捷給，舉動恢張，稱曰才望，取爵位則有余，責事功則不足，何益成敗哉？」

translations.literal: If one merely because debate is quick and actions are expansive is called talent and reputation—gaining rank and position there is surplus, but charging with achievement there is insufficiency—what benefit for success and failure?"
translations.idiomatic: Men who talk fast and act boldly are praised as talented, but such gifts win promotions, not victories—what good are they in deciding the fate of the realm?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「濟變之日，先才後守。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "On days of meeting change, first talent, afterward integrity."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "In a crisis, talent comes before scruples."

sentences.zh: 宗周曰：「前人敗壞，皆由貪縱使然；

translations.literal: Zongzhou said: "The ruin of predecessors all proceeded from greed and indulgence causing it;
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou replied: "Every past collapse has come from greed and lax discipline;

sentences.zh: 故以濟變言，愈宜先守後才。」

translations.literal: Therefore speaking of meeting change, all the more one ought to put integrity first and talent after."
translations.idiomatic: so in a crisis integrity must come before talent."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「大將別有才局，非徒操守可望成功。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Great generals have separate patterns of talent—not merely integrity can be hoped for success."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "A great commander needs a broader vision than mere integrity alone can provide."

sentences.zh: 宗周曰：「他不具論，如範誌完操守不謹，大將偏裨無不由賄進，所以三軍解體。

translations.literal: Zongzhou said: "Others need not be fully discussed; take Fan Zhichuan—his conduct was not strict, and grand and subordinate generals all entered through bribery, hence the three armies disintegrated.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou said: "Need I argue further? Take Fan Zhichuan—lacking in integrity, with every officer from general to captain buying his post—that is why the army fell apart.

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，操守為主。」

translations.literal: Viewed from this, integrity is the main thing."
translations.idiomatic: From this it is clear that character must come first."

sentences.zh: 帝色解曰：「朕已知之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor's color eased and he said: "I already know it."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's expression softened. "I understand," he said.

sentences.zh: 敕宗周起。

translations.literal: He ordered Zongzhou to rise.
translations.idiomatic: He told Zongzhou to rise.

sentences.zh: 於是宗周出奏曰：「陛下方下詔求賢，姜埰、熊開元二臣遽以言得罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zongzhou went out and memorialized, saying: "Your Majesty has just issued an edict seeking the worthy, yet the two ministers Jiang Cai and Xiong Kaiyuan were abruptly punished for speech.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou then submitted a memorial from the floor: "Your Majesty has just issued an edict calling for men of talent, yet Jiang Cai and Xiong Kaiyuan have already been punished for speaking out.

sentences.zh: 國朝無言官下詔獄者，有之自二臣始。

translations.literal: In our dynasty remonstrating officials sent to the imperial prison—if there has been such, it begins with these two ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Never in this dynasty has a censor been thrown into the imperial prison—if it happens now, these two will be the first.

sentences.zh: 陛下度量卓越，妄如臣宗周，戇直如臣黃道周，尚蒙使過之典，二臣何不幸，不邀法外恩？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty's magnanimity is surpassing—even reckless as your minister Zongzhou, or blunt and straight as your minister Huang Daozhou, we still received the grace of overlooking faults—how unfortunate the two ministers, not invited to grace outside the law?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's generosity is boundless—even rash men like myself and blunt ones like Huang Daozhou have been granted mercy—why are these two men denied even that?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「道周有學有守，非二臣比。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Daozhou has learning and integrity—not comparable to the two ministers."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Huang Daozhou had learning and principles—they are not in the same class."

sentences.zh: 宗周曰：「二臣誠不及道周，然朝廷待言官有體，言可用用之，不可置之。

translations.literal: Zongzhou said: "The two ministers truly do not reach Daozhou, yet the court treats remonstrating officials with proper form—if speech can be used, use it; if not, do not dispose of them.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou said: "They may fall short of Huang Daozhou, but the court has always treated censors with dignity—accept good advice and reject bad, but do not destroy the men.

sentences.zh: 即有應得之罪，亦當付法司。

translations.literal: Even if there is guilt that should be answered for, it also ought to be entrusted to the judicial offices.
translations.idiomatic: Even if they deserve punishment, the matter belongs before the regular courts.

sentences.zh: 今遽下詔獄，終於國體有傷。」

translations.literal: Now abruptly sending them to the imperial prison—in the end the body politic is harmed."
translations.idiomatic: To throw them at once into the imperial prison is to wound the dignity of the state itself."

sentences.zh: 帝怒甚，曰：「法司錦衣皆刑官，何公何私？

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered and said: "The judicial offices and the Brocade Guard are all punishment officers—what public, what private?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flew into a rage. "The Ministry of Justice and the Brocade Guard are both courts of law—where is the distinction?

sentences.zh: 且罪一二言官，何遽傷國體？

translations.literal: Moreover, punishing one or two remonstrating officials—how hastily does that harm the body politic?
translations.idiomatic: And punishing one or two censors—how does that damage the state?

sentences.zh: 有如貪贓壞法，欺君罔上，皆可不問乎？」

translations.literal: If there are such as embezzling, breaking the law, deceiving the sovereign and misleading superiors—can all be not questioned?"
translations.idiomatic: Are graft, law-breaking, and deceit of the throne all to go unpunished?"

sentences.zh: 宗周曰：「錦衣，膏粱子弟，何知禮義？

translations.literal: Zongzhou said: "The Brocade Guard—sons of rich grain and fine meat—what do they know of ritual and righteousness?
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou said: "The Brocade Guard are pampered noblemen's sons—what do they know of justice?

sentences.zh: 聽寺人役使。

translations.literal: They listen to eunuch service and employment.
translations.idiomatic: They take their orders from the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 即陛下問貪贓壞法，欺君罔上，亦不可不付法司也。」

translations.literal: Even if Your Majesty asks about embezzling, breaking the law, deceiving the sovereign and misleading superiors—it also cannot fail to be entrusted to the judicial offices."
translations.idiomatic: Even for crimes of graft and treason, the case must still go to the regular judiciary."

sentences.zh: 帝大怒曰：「如此偏黨，豈堪憲職！」

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered and said: "Such partiality and faction—how can one bear the censorial charge!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor exploded: "Such blatant favoritism—how can you hold the censor's post!"

sentences.zh: 有間曰：「開元此疏，必有主使，疑即宗周。」

translations.literal: After an interval he said: "Kaiyuan's this memorial must have a mastermind—I suspect it is Zongzhou."
translations.idiomatic: After a pause he said: "Someone must be behind Xiong Kaiyuan's memorial—I suspect it is Zongzhou himself."

sentences.zh: 金光辰爭之。

translations.literal: Jin Guangchen disputed it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Guangchen objected.

sentences.zh: 帝叱光辰，並命議處。

translations.literal: The Emperor berated Guangchen and jointly ordered deliberation on punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor shouted Guangchen down and ordered both men punished.

sentences.zh: 翼日，光辰貶三秩調用，宗周革職，刑部議罪。

translations.literal: The next day Guangchen was demoted three ranks and transferred, Zongzhou was stripped of office, and the Ministry of Punishments deliberated guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jin Guangchen was demoted three ranks and reassigned; Zongzhou was dismissed; the Ministry of Justice deliberated his sentence.

sentences.zh: 閣臣持不發，捧原旨御前懇救，乃免，斥為民。

translations.literal: Grand secretaries held [the edict] without issuing it, carrying the original edict before the throne to earnestly plead rescue, and he was then spared, expelled as commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The grand secretaries withheld the order and pleaded before the Emperor with the original edict in hand; Zongzhou was spared execution but banished as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 歸二年而京師陷。

translations.literal: Returned two years and the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: Two years after his return home, the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 宗周徒步荷戈，詣杭州，責巡撫黃鳴駿發喪討賊，鳴駿誡以鎮靜，宗周勃然曰：「君父變出非常，公專閫外，不思枕戈泣血，激勵同仇，顧藉口鎮靜，作遜避計耶？」

translations.literal: Zongzhou went on foot bearing weapons, proceeding to Hangzhou, reproaching Governor Huang Mingjun to raise mourning and attack the bandits; Mingjun admonished him to keep calm—Zongzhou flared up and said: "Sovereign and father transformed in extraordinary fashion, you hold authority outside the passes, not thinking to pillow weapons and weep blood, rousing shared enmity, yet taking calm as pretext, making a plan of yielding avoidance?"
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou marched on foot with a weapon to Hangzhou and demanded that Governor Huang Mingjun proclaim the Emperor's death and raise troops against the rebels. Huang urged restraint. Zongzhou blazed with anger: "The throne itself has been overthrown, and you command the province—yet instead of taking up arms and weeping blood to rally vengeance, you cite 'restraint' as an excuse to do nothing?"

sentences.zh: 鳴駿唯唯。

translations.literal: Mingjun assented vaguely.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Mingjun murmured agreement.

sentences.zh: 明日，復趣之。

translations.literal: The next day, he again pressed him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zongzhou pressed him again.

sentences.zh: 鳴駿曰：「發喪必待哀詔。」

translations.literal: Mingjun said: "Raising mourning must await the lament edict."
translations.idiomatic: Huang Mingjun said: "We cannot proclaim the funeral without an imperial mourning edict."

sentences.zh: 宗周曰：「嘻，此何時也，安所得哀詔哉！」

translations.literal: Zongzhou said: "Alas, what time is this—where would one obtain a lament edict!"
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou said: "Good heavens—what moment is this, and where would such an edict come from!"

sentences.zh: 鳴駿乃發喪。

translations.literal: Mingjun thereupon raised mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Mingjun finally proclaimed the mourning.

sentences.zh: 問師期，則曰：「甲仗未具。」

translations.literal: Asking the date for dispatching troops, he then said: "Armor and weapons are not yet prepared."
translations.idiomatic: When asked when he would march, Huang said: "Our arms and armor are not yet ready."

sentences.zh: 宗周嘆曰：「嗟乎，是烏足與有為哉！」

translations.literal: Zongzhou sighed and said: "Alas, this one is not sufficient to achieve anything with!"
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou sighed: "Ah—this man is capable of nothing worth doing!"

sentences.zh: 乃與故侍郎朱大典，故給事中章正宸、熊汝霖召募義旅。

translations.literal: Thereupon with former Vice Minister Zhu Dadian, former Submitter of Petitions Zhang Zhenchen, and Xiong Rulin he recruited righteous troops.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined the former Vice Minister Zhu Dadian and the former palace advisers Zhang Zhenchen and Xiong Rulin in raising a volunteer army.

sentences.zh: 將發，而福王監國於南京，起宗周故官。

translations.literal: About to set out, yet the Prince of Fu supervised the state at Nanjing and restored Zongzhou to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Just as they were about to march, the Prince of Fu assumed regency at Nanjing and recalled Zongzhou to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 宗周以大仇未報，不敢受職，自稱草莽孤臣，疏陳時政，言：

translations.literal: Zongzhou, because the great vengeance was not yet repaid, dared not accept the office, styled himself a lone minister of the wilds, and in a memorial set forth current administration, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou declined the post while national vengeance remained unfulfilled, calling himself a private subject of the wilderness, and submitted a memorial on current policy, declaring:

sentences.zh: 今日大計，舍討賊復仇，無以表陛下渡江之心；

translations.literal: Today's great plan: apart from attacking bandits and revenging, there is no means to display Your Majesty's heart in crossing the river;
translations.idiomatic: The paramount task today is vengeance against the rebels—without it, Your Majesty's purpose in crossing the Yangtze cannot be made clear;

sentences.zh: 非毅然決策親征，無以作天下忠義之氣。

translations.literal: Unless one resolutely decides and personally campaigns, there is no way to rouse the spirit of loyalty and righteousness throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing short of a resolute decision to lead the campaign in person can stir the empire's spirit of loyal service.

sentences.zh: 一曰據形勝以規進取。

translations.literal: First: rely on strategic terrain to plan advance and seizure.
translations.idiomatic: First, seize advantageous ground and plan the advance north.

sentences.zh: 江左非偏安之業，請進圖江北。

translations.literal: The lands south of the Yangtze are not a foundation for partial peace; I ask that you advance to contrive the north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: The lower Yangtze is no place to settle for mere survival; I urge an active strategy to recover the north.

sentences.zh: 鳳陽號中都，東扼徐、淮，北控豫州，西顧荊、襄，而南去金陵不遠，請以駐親征之師。

translations.literal: Fengyang is called the Central Capital; east it throttles Xu and Huai, north it controls Yuzhou, west it looks to Jing and Xiang, and south it is not far from Jinling—I ask that the army of the personal campaign be stationed there.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyang—the old "Central Capital"—commands Xuzhou and the Huai region to the east, Henan to the north, and Jingzhou and Xiangyang to the west, while lying close to Nanjing to the south. Station Your Majesty's expeditionary force there.

sentences.zh: 大小銓除，暫稱行在，少存臣子負罪引慝之心。

translations.literal: Great and small appointments and removals should for the time be styled as from the mobile court, so as to retain somewhat the heart of ministers bearing guilt and acknowledging faults.
translations.idiomatic: Keep all appointments provisional under a "mobile court" designation, preserving among your ministers some sense of shared guilt and penitence.

sentences.zh: 從此漸進，秦、晉、燕、齊必有響應而起者。

translations.literal: Advancing gradually from this, in Qin, Jin, Yan, and Qi there will surely be those who rise in response.
translations.idiomatic: Advance step by step from there, and Qin, Jin, Yan, and Qi will surely rally to the cause.

sentences.zh: 一曰重藩屏以資彈壓。

translations.literal: Second: strengthen the screen-barriers to supply suppression and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Second, strengthen the frontier defenses so they can actually hold the line.

sentences.zh: 淮、揚數百里，設兩節鉞，不能禦亂，爭先南下，致江北一塊土，拱手授賊。

translations.literal: For several hundred li in Huai and Yang, two military commissioners were set, yet could not repel disorder; each raced to flee south, causing the whole stretch of land north of the river to be handed over to bandits with clasped hands.
translations.idiomatic: For hundreds of miles along the Huai and Yang regions, two commissioners with full military authority were stationed—yet they could not repel the enemy. They raced each other south and surrendered the entire north bank without a fight.

sentences.zh: 督漕路振飛坐守淮城，久以家屬浮舟遠地，是倡之逃也；

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator of the Grain Transport Lu Zhenfei sat defending Huai city, long keeping his family on boats at a distance—this was initiating flight;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhenfei, commissioner of grain transport, held Huai city while keeping his family on boats far away—a clear signal that flight was acceptable;

sentences.zh: 於是鎮臣劉澤清、高傑遂有家屬寄江南之說。

translations.literal: Thus the garrison commanders Liu Zeqing and Gao Jie then had talk of sending their families to lodge south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the garrison generals Liu Zeqing and Gao Jie were likewise sending their families south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 軍法臨陣脫逃者斬，臣謂一撫二鎮皆可斬也。

translations.literal: Military law holds that one who flees in battle is beheaded; I say the one governor and two garrison commanders may all be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Desertion on the battlefield is a capital offense. I say the governor and both garrison commanders all deserve execution.

sentences.zh: 一曰慎爵賞以肅軍情。

translations.literal: Third: be cautious with ranks and rewards to stern the military morale.
translations.idiomatic: Third, review ennoblements and rewards carefully to restore military discipline.

sentences.zh: 請分別各帥封賞，孰當孰濫，輕則收侯爵，重則奪伯爵。

translations.literal: I ask to distinguish the enfeoffments and rewards of each commander—who deserved them and who received them excessively; lightly, strip marquisates; heavily, revoke earldoms.
translations.idiomatic: Review every commander's titles and rewards: distinguish the deserved from the gratuitous. Strip lesser offenders of their marquisates; revoke earldoms from the worst.

sentences.zh: 夫以左帥之恢復而封，高、劉之敗逃亦封，又誰不當封者？

translations.literal: Now if the Left Marshal was enfeoffed for recovery, while Gao and Liu were also enfeoffed for defeat and flight—who then would not deserve enfeoffment?
translations.idiomatic: If the Left Marshal was ennobled for recovering territory while Gao and Liu were rewarded for defeat and flight, who would not claim a title?

sentences.zh: 武臣既濫，文臣隨之，外臣既濫，中珰隨之，恐天下聞而解體也。

translations.literal: Once military ministers are excessive, civil ministers follow; once external ministers are excessive, palace eunuchs follow—I fear the empire will hear of it and disintegrate.
translations.idiomatic: Indiscriminate rewards to generals invite the same from civil officials, and from regional officials to palace eunuchs. The empire will lose heart when it sees this.

sentences.zh: 一曰核舊官以立臣紀。

translations.literal: Fourth: verify former officials to establish the standard of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, audit former officials and restore ministerial standards.

sentences.zh: 燕京既破，有受偽官而叛者，有受偽官而逃者，有在封守而逃者，有奉使命而逃者，法皆不赦。

translations.literal: After Yanjing was fallen, there were those who accepted false appointments and rebelled, those who accepted false appointments and fled, those who were in garrison and fled, and those who bore missions and fled—the law pardons none.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Beijing, some took offices under the puppet regime and rebelled; some took such offices and fled; some abandoned their posts; some abandoned imperial missions. None deserve pardon.

sentences.zh: 亟宜分別定罪，為戒將來。

translations.literal: They should urgently be distinguished and sentenced, as a warning for the future.
translations.idiomatic: Judgment should be swift and differentiated, as a warning for the future.

sentences.zh: 至於偽命南下，徘徊順逆之間，實繁有徒；

translations.literal: As for false orders coming south, wavering between submission and resistance, they are truly numerous;
translations.idiomatic: Many more accepted the rebel regime's appointments in the south and wavered between loyalty and surrender;

sentences.zh: 必且倡為曲說，以惑人心，尤宜誅絕。

translations.literal: They will surely promote crooked explanations to bewilder people's hearts—they should especially be exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: They will surely spin excuses to confuse the people. These too must be punished without mercy.

sentences.zh: 又言：

translations.literal: He also said:
translations.idiomatic: He continued:

sentences.zh: 當賊入秦流晉，漸過畿南，遠近洶洶，獨大江南北晏然，而二三督撫不聞遣一騎以壯聲援，賊遂得長驅犯闕。

translations.literal: When bandits entered Qin and flowed through Jin, gradually passing south of the capital region, near and far were in uproar, yet south of the Yangtze alone was tranquil; two or three governors and grand coordinators never sent a single rider to bolster support—and the bandits were thus able to drive straight to violate the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels swept through Shaanxi and Shanxi toward the capital, panic spread everywhere—yet the Jiangnan region sat undisturbed while governors and commissioners failed to send a single rider to aid the capital. The rebels rode straight to the Forbidden City.

sentences.zh: 坐視君父之危亡而不救，則封疆諸臣之當誅者一。

translations.literal: Sitting and watching the sovereign and father in peril and death without rescue—that is the first reason frontier ministers deserve execution.
translations.idiomatic: Standing idle while the emperor and dynasty perished—that is the first count against the frontier officials.

sentences.zh: 兇問已確，諸臣奮戈而起，決一戰以贖前愆，自當不俟朝食。

translations.literal: Once evil tidings were confirmed, ministers should have grasped weapons and risen, deciding one battle to redeem former faults—they should naturally not wait for morning meal.
translations.idiomatic: Once the dreadful news was confirmed, ministers should have seized their arms and fought immediately to redeem themselves—not even waiting for breakfast.

sentences.zh: 方且仰聲息於南中，爭言固圉之策，卸兵權於閫外，首圖定策之功，則封疆諸臣之當誅者又一。

translations.literal: Yet they were leaning on breath and life in the south, contending to speak of strategies to secure the border, shedding military authority outside the command, seeking first credit for settling policy—that is another reason frontier ministers deserve execution.
translations.idiomatic: Instead they looked to Nanjing for safety, quarreled over defensive strategies, shirked military responsibility to outsiders, and fought over credit for policy decisions—that is another count against them.

sentences.zh: 新朝既立之後，謂宜不俟終日，首遣北伐之師。

translations.literal: After the new dynasty was established, it was said one should not wait a full day but first dispatch northern-expedition armies.
translations.idiomatic: Once the new court was established, a northern expedition should have been launched the very same day.

sentences.zh: 不然，則亟馳一介，間道北進，檄燕中父老，起塞上名王，哭九廟，厝梓宮，訪諸王。

translations.literal: Otherwise, then urgently send one envoy by hidden route northward, proclaim to the elders of Yan, raise the famed princes of the frontier passes, mourn the nine temples, lay out the imperial coffin, and seek out the imperial clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: At minimum, send an envoy by secret route north: rally the elders of Yan, summon the princes of the frontier, mourn the ancestral temples, recover the emperor's coffin, and find surviving members of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 更不然，則起閩帥鄭芝龍，以海師下直沽，九邊督鎮合謀共奮，事或可為。

translations.literal: If still not so, then raise the Fujian commander Zheng Zhilong, with sea forces descend to Zhigu, and the nine frontier governors and garrisons conspire together to exert effort—the matter may yet be done.
translations.idiomatic: Better still, mobilize Zheng Zhilong of Fujian: sail a fleet to Tianjin while the frontier governors and garrisons coordinate a rising—the cause might yet be saved.

sentences.zh: 而諸臣計不出此，則舉朝謀國不忠之當誅者又一。

translations.literal: Yet the ministers' plans did not go beyond this—that is yet another reason the whole court, in scheming for the state disloyally, deserve execution.
translations.idiomatic: The court conceived none of these plans—another count of disloyalty against the ministers.

sentences.zh: 罪廢諸臣，量從昭雪，自應援先帝遺詔及之，今乃概用新恩。

translations.literal: Ministers punished and dismissed should, according to measure, be cleared; they should naturally be reached through citing the former emperor's testament—yet now new grace is applied across the board.
translations.idiomatic: Officials punished and dismissed should have been restored according to the late emperor's will. Instead blanket amnesties have been granted.

sentences.zh: 誅閹定案，前後詔書鶻突，勢必彪虎之類，盡從平反而後已，則舉朝謀國不忠之當誅者又一。

translations.literal: Cases fixing guilt on eunuchs—edicts before and after were incoherent; inevitably men like Biao Hu would all be reversed until done—another reason the whole court deserves execution for disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The verdicts against the eunuchs have been overturned by contradictory edicts. Rapacious figures of that ilk will all be rehabilitated—yet another count of disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 臣謂今日問罪，當自中外諸臣不職者始。

translations.literal: Your subject says that today's assignment of guilt should begin with incompetent ministers at home and abroad.
translations.idiomatic: I say accountability should begin with every negligent minister, at court and in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 詔納其言，宣付史館，中外為悚動。

translations.literal: An edict accepted his words and ordered them proclaimed to the Historical Archives; at home and abroad there was startled trembling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the memorial and ordered it deposited in the Historical Archives. Court and country were shaken.

sentences.zh: 而馬士英、高傑、劉澤清恨甚，滋欲殺宗周矣。

translations.literal: But Ma Shi Ying, Gao Jie, and Liu Zeqing hated deeply and increasingly wished to kill Zongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shi Ying, Gao Jie, and Liu Zeqing were enraged and increasingly bent on killing Zongzhou.

sentences.zh: 宗周連疏請告不得命，遂抗疏劾士英，言：

translations.literal: Zongzhou repeatedly memorialized requesting leave but received no approval; then he submitted a defiant memorial impeaching Shi Ying, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou repeatedly requested leave without success, then submitted a bold memorial impeaching Ma Shi Ying, declaring:

sentences.zh: 陛下龍飛淮甸，天實予之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's dragon flight in the Huai region—Heaven truly granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's accession in the Huai region was Heaven's own gift.

sentences.zh: 乃有扈蹕微勞，入內閣，進中樞，宮銜世蔭，晏然當之不疑者，非士英乎？

translations.literal: Yet there was one with slight merit in escorting the imperial carriage who entered the Grand Secretariat, advanced to the central pivot, received hereditary palace titles, and calmly accepted it without doubt—is this not Shi Ying?
translations.idiomatic: Yet for escort duty of the slightest kind, one man entered the Grand Secretariat, took control of the central administration, and accepted hereditary honors without a qualm—was that not Ma Shi Ying?

sentences.zh: 於是李沾侈言定策，挑激廷臣矣。

translations.literal: Thus Li Zhan extravagantly spoke of settling policy and provoked the court ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Then Li Zhan boasted of having settled the succession and goaded the court into factional strife.

sentences.zh: 劉孔昭以功賞不均，發憤冢臣，朝端嘩然聚訟，而群陰且翩翩起矣。

translations.literal: Liu Kongzhao, because rewards for merit were unequal, vented rage on the chief minister; the court end erupted in clamor and gathered litigation—and the swarm of yin forces began to rise lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kongzhao, angered by unequal rewards, turned his fury on the chief minister. The court erupted in uproar, and the dark faction began to stir.

sentences.zh: 借知兵之名，則逆黨可以然灰，寬反正之路，則逃臣可以汲引，而閣部諸臣且次第言去矣。

translations.literal: Borrowing the name of military knowledge, then rebels can be reduced to ash; widening the path of return to righteousness, then fleeing ministers can be drawn up—and the Grand Secretariat ministers will in turn speak of leaving one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Invoking "military expertise" lets traitors off scot-free; opening the path to "surrender" welcomes back deserters—and ministers of the Grand Secretariat are resigning one after another.

sentences.zh: 中朝之黨論方興，何暇圖河北之賊？

translations.literal: Factional debate at the central court is just rising—what leisure to plan against the bandits of Hebei?
translations.idiomatic: With factional warfare consuming the court, who has time to fight the rebels in the north?

sentences.zh: 立國之本紀已疏，何以言匡攘之略？

translations.literal: The fundamental statutes of establishing the state are already lax—how speak of strategies to restore and expel?
translations.idiomatic: The foundations of the new state are already neglected—how can we speak of recovering the realm?

sentences.zh: 高傑一逃將也，而奉若驕子，浸有尾大之憂。

translations.literal: Gao Jie was a fleeing general, yet he was honored as a pampered son—gradually there was the worry of a tail growing too large.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jie was a deserter, yet he was treated like a spoiled favorite—a growing threat to the throne.

sentences.zh: 淮、揚失事，不難譴撫臣道臣以謝之，安得不長其桀驁，則亦恃士英卵翼也。

translations.literal: When Huai and Yang lost affairs, it would not have been hard to reprimand the governor and circuit intendant to apologize to him—how could this not lengthen his arrogance and insolence? This too relied on Shi Ying's sheltering wings.
translations.idiomatic: After the Huai-Yang disaster, the court could easily have reprimanded the governor and circuit intendant to appease him—but that only fed his arrogance, shielded as he was by Ma Shi Ying's protection.

sentences.zh: 劉、黃諸將，各有舊汛地，而置若弈棋，洶洶為連雞之勢，至分剖江北四鎮以慰之，安得不啟其雄心，則皆高傑一人倡之也。

translations.literal: The generals Liu and Huang each had old garrison territories, yet they were set out like chess pieces, in uproar forming the momentum of linked chickens—until the four garrisons north of the river were divided to appease him; how could this not open their ambitious hearts? All were initiated by Gao Jie alone.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Liu and Huang each held established garrison posts, yet their territories were shuffled like chess pieces until mutual suspicion reigned. The four garrisons north of the river were carved up to appease Gao Jie—how could that not inflame their ambitions? He alone started it all.

sentences.zh: 京營自祖宗以來，皆勛臣為政，樞貳佐之。

translations.literal: The Metropolitan Garrison, from the ancestors onward, has always been governed by meritorious ministers, with second-rank commissioners assisting.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of the dynasty, the Metropolitan Garrison has been commanded by meritorious nobles, with senior officers as deputies.

sentences.zh: 陛下立國伊始，而有內臣盧九德之命，則士英有不得辭其責者。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, at the very start of establishing the state, had the appointment of the inner attendant Lu Jiude—then Shi Ying cannot decline his responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: At the very founding of the state, Your Majesty appointed the eunuch Lu Jiude to command the Metropolitan Garrison—Ma Shi Ying cannot evade responsibility for that.

sentences.zh: 總之，兵戈盜賊，皆從小人氣類感召而生，而小人與奄宦又往往相表裏。

translations.literal: In sum, arms and banditry all arise from the mutual attraction of petty men's kind—and petty men and eunuchs often are outer and inner to each other.
translations.idiomatic: In sum, war and rebellion spring from the collusion of petty men—and petty men and eunuchs are invariably partners in crime.

sentences.zh: 自古未有奄宦用事，而將帥能樹功於方域者。

translations.literal: From antiquity there has never been eunuchs wielding power while generals could establish merit in the regions.
translations.idiomatic: Never in history have eunuchs held power while generals won victories in the field.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下首辨陰陽消長之機，出士英仍督鳳陽，聯絡諸鎮，決用兵之策。

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty first discern the mechanism of yin and yang waxing and waning: remove Shi Ying yet still have him supervise Fengyang, link the garrisons, and decide the policy of using troops.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to read the balance of power clearly: dismiss Ma Shi Ying but send him to supervise Fengyang, coordinate the garrisons, and settle on a military strategy.

sentences.zh: 史可法即不還中樞，亦當自淮而北，歷河以南，別開幕府，與士英相掎角。

translations.literal: Shi Kefa, even if not returning to the central pivot, should also from Huai go north, cross south of the river, separately open a headquarters, and with Shi Ying form pincers.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Shi Kefa does not return to the central administration, he should march north from the Huai, cross the Yellow River, establish a separate command, and coordinate with Ma Shi Ying in a pincer movement.

sentences.zh: 京營提督，獨斷寢之。

translations.literal: The Metropolitan Garrison supervisor—solely decide to let it rest.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Metropolitan Garrison command—cancel that appointment outright.

sentences.zh: 書之史冊，為弘光第一美政。

translations.literal: Record it in the historical annals as the first fine policy of the Hongguang reign.
translations.idiomatic: Record it in the annals as the Hongguang era's first great act of statecraft.

sentences.zh: 王優詔答之，而促其速入。

translations.literal: The king replied with a gracious edict and urged him to enter quickly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied with a gracious edict and urged him to come to court at once.

sentences.zh: 士英大怒，即日具疏辭位，且揚言於朝曰：「劉公自稱草莽孤臣，不書新命，明示不臣天子也。」

translations.literal: Shi Ying was greatly enraged; that very day he prepared a memorial resigning his post, and proclaimed in court, saying: "Lord Liu styled himself a lone minister of the wilds and did not write the new appointment—openly showing he will not serve the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shi Ying was furious. That same day he submitted his resignation and declared at court: "Lord Liu calls himself a private subject of the wilderness and omitted the new imperial title from his memorial—a plain refusal to acknowledge the Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 其私人朱統𨰥遂劾宗周疏請移蹕鳳陽：「鳳陽，高墻所在，欲以罪宗處皇上，而與史可法擁立潞王。

translations.literal: His private man Zhu Tonglei then impeached Zongzhou's memorial requesting the transfer of the imperial residence to Fengyang: "Fengyang is where high walls stand; he wishes to place the emperor in the place of guilt, and with Shi Kefa to support and establish the Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: His client Zhu Tonglei then impeached Zongzhou for requesting that the court move to Fengyang: "Fengyang is a prison city. He means to confine the emperor there while he and Shi Kefa install the Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 其兵已伏丹陽，當急備。」

translations.literal: His troops are already lying in ambush at Danyang—urgent preparations should be made."
translations.idiomatic: His troops are already hidden at Danyang. Guard against them at once."

sentences.zh: 而澤清、傑日夜謀所以殺宗周者不得，乃遣客十輩往刺宗周。

translations.literal: Yet Zeqing and Jie day and night schemed how to kill Zongzhou without success; then they sent ten batches of assassins to stab Zongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Liu Zeqing and Gao Jie plotted day and night to kill Zongzhou. Failing in that, they sent ten groups of assassins after him.

sentences.zh: 宗周時在丹陽，終日危坐，未嘗有惰容，客前後至者，不敢加害而去。

translations.literal: Zongzhou was then at Danyang, sitting upright all day, never showing a lazy countenance; assassins who came before and after did not dare harm him and left.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou was then at Danyang, sitting upright all day without a trace of fear. Assassins came and went but none dared strike.

sentences.zh: 而黃鳴駿入覲，兵抵京口，與防江兵相擊鬥。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Huang Mingjun entered audience; his troops reached Jingkou and clashed with the river-defense troops.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Huang Mingjun came to court, and his troops reached Jingkou and fought with the river-defense forces.

sentences.zh: 士英以統𨰥言為信也，亦震恐。

translations.literal: Shi Ying took Tonglei's words as true and was also shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shi Ying, believing Zhu Tonglei's accusation, was terrified as well.

sentences.zh: 於是澤清疏劾：「宗周陰撓恢復，欲誅臣等，激變士心，召生靈之禍。」

translations.literal: Thus Zeqing memorialized in impeachment: "Zongzhou secretly obstructs recovery, wishes to execute us ministers, stirs mutiny in soldiers' hearts, and summons calamity upon the people."
translations.idiomatic: Then Liu Zeqing memorialized: "Zongzhou secretly sabotages the recovery effort, seeks to execute us, inflames the troops, and invites disaster upon the people."

sentences.zh: 劉良佐亦具疏言宗周力持「三案」，為門戶主盟，倡議親征，圖晁錯之自為居守，司馬懿之閉城拒君。

translations.literal: Liu Liangzuo also prepared a memorial saying Zongzhou forcefully upheld the "Three Cases," acted as factional chief, advocated personal campaign, and schemed Chao Cuo's staying behind to hold the fort and Sima Yi's closing the gates to reject the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liangzuo also submitted a memorial accusing Zongzhou of championing the "Three Cases," leading the factional alliance, and urging a personal campaign—plotting, like Chao Cuo, to hold power while the emperor marched, and, like Sima Yi, to shut the gates against the throne.

sentences.zh: 疏未下，澤清復草一疏，署傑、良佐及黃得功名上之，言：「宗周勸上親征，謀危君父，欲安置陛下於烽火兇危之地。

translations.literal: Before the memorial was issued, Zeqing again drafted a memorial, signed by Jie, Liangzuo, and Huang Degong and submitted it, saying: "Zongzhou urged the sovereign to personally campaign, schemed peril to the sovereign and father, and wished to place Your Majesty in a place of beacon fires and fierce danger.
translations.idiomatic: Before that memorial was even issued, Liu Zeqing drafted another, signed by Gao Jie, Liu Liangzuo, and Huang Degong, declaring: "Zongzhou urged Your Majesty to lead the campaign personally, endangering the throne, and meant to place you in the midst of battle and peril.

sentences.zh: 蓋非宗周一人之謀，姜曰廣、吳甡合謀也。

translations.literal: This was not Zongzhou's plot alone—Jiang Yueguang and Wu Shen conspired together.
translations.idiomatic: This was not Zongzhou's plot alone—Jiang Yueguang and Wu Shen were his co-conspirators.

sentences.zh: 曰廣心雄膽大，翊戴非其本懷，故陰結死黨，翦除諸忠，然後迫劫乘輿，遷之別郡。

translations.literal: Yueguang's heart was bold and his courage great; supporting the enthronement was not his original intent—thus he secretly bound a diehard faction, cut down the loyal, and then coerced the imperial carriage and moved it to another commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yueguang is ambitious and bold; enthroning the emperor was never his true aim. He secretly formed a faction, purged the loyal, and then meant to seize the imperial carriage and relocate the court.

sentences.zh: 如甡、宗周入都，臣等即渡江赴闕，面訐諸奸，正《春秋》討賊之義。」

translations.literal: If Shen and Zongzhou enter the capital, we ministers will immediately cross the river and go to the palace, face-to-face denounce the traitors, and uphold the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 righteousness of punishing rebels."
translations.idiomatic: If Wu Shen and Zongzhou enter the capital, we shall cross the Yangtze, appear before the throne, denounce these traitors face to face, and uphold the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 principle of punishing rebels."

sentences.zh: 疏入，舉朝大駭，傳諭和衷集事。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the whole court was greatly alarmed; an edict was transmitted urging harmony of heart and gathering of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the court was horrified. An edict was issued calling for harmony and unity.

sentences.zh: 宗周不得已，以七月十八日入朝。

translations.literal: Zongzhou had no choice; on the eighteenth day of the seventh month he entered court.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou had no choice but to enter court on the eighteenth day of the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 初，澤清疏出，遣人錄示傑。

translations.literal: At first, when Zeqing's memorial was issued, he sent someone to copy and show it to Jie.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zeqing's memorial was issued, he sent a copy to Gao Jie.

sentences.zh: 傑曰：「我輩武人，乃預朝事耶？」

translations.literal: Jie said: "We military men—are we to participate in court affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jie said: "We are soldiers—since when do we meddle in court affairs?"

sentences.zh: 得功疏辨：「臣不預聞。」

translations.literal: Degong submitted a memorial in defense: "Your subject did not participate in hearing."
translations.idiomatic: Huang Degong submitted a defense: "Your subject had no part in this."

sentences.zh: 士英寢不奏。

translations.literal: Shi Ying shelved it and did not memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shi Ying suppressed it and never forwarded it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 可法不平，遣使遍詰諸鎮，咸云不知，遂據以入告，澤清輩由是氣沮。

translations.literal: Kefa was indignant; he sent envoys to question all the garrisons everywhere—they all said they did not know—then relied on this to enter and report, and Zeqing and company thereby lost their spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kefa, indignant, sent envoys to question every garrison. All denied knowledge of the plot. He reported this to the throne, and Liu Zeqing and his allies lost heart.

sentences.zh: 士英既嫉宗周，益欲去之，而薦阮大鋮知兵。

translations.literal: Shi Ying, already jealous of Zongzhou, further wished to remove him—and recommended Ruan Dacheng as knowing warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shi Ying, already hostile to Zongzhou, sought all the more to remove him—and recommended Ruan Dacheng as a military expert.

sentences.zh: 有詔冠帶陛見。

translations.literal: There was an edict for him to appear at court in formal cap and belt.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned him to court in formal dress.

sentences.zh: 未幾，中旨特授兵部添註右侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long, by central edict he was specially appointed additional Right Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, by special imperial order he was appointed additional Right Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 宗周曰：「大鋮進退，系江左興亡，老臣不敢不一爭之。

translations.literal: Zongzhou said: "Dacheng's advancement or withdrawal concerns the rise and fall of the lands south of the Yangtze—this old minister dares not fail to contend over it.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou said: "Whether Ruan Dacheng is appointed or dismissed bears on the survival of the southern regime—I cannot remain silent.

sentences.zh: 不聽，則亦將歸爾。」

translations.literal: If not heeded, then I too will return."
translations.idiomatic: If the court will not listen, I too shall resign."

sentences.zh: 疏入，不聽，宗周遂告歸，詔許乘傳。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, it was not heeded; Zongzhou then requested to return home, and an edict permitted him post-horses.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was rejected. Zongzhou resigned, and the emperor granted him the use of official transport.

sentences.zh: 將行，疏陳五事：

translations.literal: About to depart, he memorialized setting forth five matters:
translations.idiomatic: Before departing, he submitted a final memorial outlining five points:

sentences.zh: 一曰修聖政，毋以近娛忽遠猷。

translations.literal: First: cultivate sagely governance; do not let near diversions neglect far-reaching plans.
translations.idiomatic: First, restore sound governance; do not let present pleasures eclipse long-term strategy.

sentences.zh: 國家不幸，遭此大變，今紛紛制作，似不復有中原誌者。

translations.literal: The state is unfortunate, having met this great upheaval; now various constructions proliferate, as if there is no longer anyone with ambition for the Central Plain.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty has suffered catastrophe, yet the court busies itself with new projects as though no one any longer aspires to recover the north.

sentences.zh: 土木崇矣，珍奇集矣，俳優雜劇陳矣；

translations.literal: Construction is exalted, rare treasures are gathered, actors and mixed plays are displayed;
translations.idiomatic: Palaces rise, curios accumulate, and actors and plays fill the halls;

sentences.zh: 內豎充廷，金吾滿座，戚畹駢闐矣；

translations.literal: inner attendants fill the court, golden guards fill the seats, imperial in-laws crowd in abundance;
translations.idiomatic: eunuchs pack the court, imperial guards fill every seat, and royal in-laws crowd the halls;

sentences.zh: 讒夫昌，言路扼，官常亂矣。

translations.literal: slanderers flourish, the path of speech is choked, and official norms are in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: slanderers thrive, the channels of remonstrance are blocked, and official conduct is in chaos.

sentences.zh: 所謂狃近娛而忽遠圖也。

translations.literal: This is what is called clinging to near diversions and neglecting far-reaching plans.
translations.idiomatic: This is what it means to indulge the present and forget the larger design.

sentences.zh: 一曰明國是，無以邪鋒危正氣。

translations.literal: Second: clarify the right course of the state; do not let the sharp edge of evil endanger upright qi.
translations.idiomatic: Second, clarify the nation's true direction; do not let factional malice undermine upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 朋黨之說，小人以加君子，釀國家空虛之禍，先帝末造可鑒也。

translations.literal: The talk of factions—petty men use it against gentlemen, brewing the calamity of the state's emptiness; the late emperor's final years may serve as a mirror.
translations.idiomatic: The charge of "faction" is a weapon petty men wield against the upright—it hollowed out the state in the late emperor's reign, and that lesson stands before us.

sentences.zh: 今更為一二元惡稱冤，至諸君子後先死於黨、死於徇國者，若有余戮。

translations.literal: Now further, for one or two chief evils claims of injustice are made—until gentlemen who died earlier and later for faction or died for the state seem to have surplus punishment remaining.
translations.idiomatic: Now the chief villains are being rehabilitated, while gentlemen who died for their principles or for the country seem to have been punished beyond death itself.

sentences.zh: 揆厥所由，止以一人進用，動引三朝故事，排抑舊人。

translations.literal: Tracing the reason, it stems solely from one man's advancement and employment, constantly citing precedents of three reigns and suppressing old men.
translations.idiomatic: The cause is plain: one man's appointment, justified by precedents from three reigns, has been used to purge the old guard.

sentences.zh: 私交重，君父輕，身自樹黨，而坐他人以黨，所謂長邪鋒而危正氣也。

translations.literal: Private ties are heavy, sovereign and father are light; one builds a faction oneself yet sits others with the charge of faction—this is what is called lengthening the evil edge and endangering upright qi.
translations.idiomatic: Private alliances weigh heavier than loyalty to the throne; he forms a faction himself while accusing others of factionalism—this is how malice grows and upright conduct is destroyed.

sentences.zh: 一曰端治術，無以刑名先教化。

translations.literal: Third: rectify the methods of governance; do not let punishment and names precede teaching and transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Third, set governance on the right footing; do not put punitive law ahead of moral instruction.

sentences.zh: 先帝頗尚刑名，而殺機先動於溫體仁。

translations.literal: The former emperor quite favored punishment and names, and the killing impulse first stirred with Wen Tiren.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor leaned heavily on punitive law, and the appetite for executions began with Wen Tiren.

sentences.zh: 殺運日開，怨毒滿天下。

translations.literal: The momentum of killing opened day by day; resentment and poison filled the empire.
translations.idiomatic: The cycle of executions widened day by day until resentment poisoned the realm.

sentences.zh: 近如貪吏之誅，不經提問，遽科罪名；

translations.literal: Recently, as with the execution of corrupt officials—without passing through interrogation, charges were suddenly assigned;
translations.idiomatic: Recently corrupt officials have been condemned without proper inquiry;

sentences.zh: 未科罪名，先追贓罰。

translations.literal: before charges were assigned, restitution and fines were first pursued.
translations.idiomatic: restitution is demanded before guilt is even established.

sentences.zh: 假令有禹好善之巡方，借成德以媚權相，又孰辨之？

translations.literal: Suppose there were a Yu Haoshan's tour of the regions, borrowing Cheng De to flatter the power-holding minister—who then could distinguish it?
translations.idiomatic: If an inspector like Yu Haoshan were to tour the provinces, using Cheng De's case to curry favor with the chief minister—who could tell justice from flattery?

sentences.zh: 又職方戎政之奸弊，道路嘖有煩言，雖衛臣有不敢問者，則廠衛之設何為？

translations.literal: Again, the corrupt abuses of the Bureau of Appointments' military administration—on the roads there are noisy complaints; even guard ministers dare not inquire—then for what are the Factory and Guard establishments?
translations.idiomatic: Corruption in the Bureau of Appointments' military affairs draws public outrage, yet even the guard officials dare not investigate—what then is the purpose of the secret police?

sentences.zh: 徒令人主虧至德，傷治體，所謂急刑名而忘教化也。

translations.literal: It merely causes the sovereign to lose supreme virtue and injure the body of governance—this is what is called rushing punishment and names while forgetting teaching and transformation.
translations.idiomatic: It only diminishes the emperor's moral authority and damages the foundations of rule—this is what it means to fixate on punishment and forget moral instruction.

sentences.zh: 一曰固邦本，毋以外釁釀內憂。

translations.literal: Fourth: secure the foundation of the state; do not let external provocations brew internal troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, strengthen the nation's foundations; do not let troubles abroad ferment crisis at home.

sentences.zh: 前者淮、揚告變，未幾而高、黃二鎮治兵相攻。

translations.literal: Previously Huai and Yang reported disturbances; before long the two garrisons of Gao and Huang drilled troops and attacked each other.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai and Yang first reported unrest, it was not long before the Gao and Huang garrisons mobilized and turned on each other.

sentences.zh: 四鎮額兵各三萬，不以殺敵而自相屠毒，又日煩朝廷講和，何為者！

translations.literal: The four garrisons each had a quota of thirty thousand troops—not using them to kill the enemy but slaughtering one another, and daily troubling the court to mediate peace—what is the purpose of this!
translations.idiomatic: Four garrisons, each nominally thirty thousand strong, slaughter one another instead of fighting the enemy—and daily demand that the court broker peace. To what end?

sentences.zh: 夫以十二萬不殺敵之兵，索十二萬不殺敵之餉，必窮之術耳。

translations.literal: For one hundred twenty thousand troops that do not kill the enemy to demand one hundred twenty thousand troops' worth of rations that do not kill the enemy—this is surely a method of certain exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Maintaining a hundred and twenty thousand soldiers who never fight, and paying rations for a hundred and twenty thousand soldiers who never fight—this is a sure path to ruin.

sentences.zh: 不稍裁抑，惟加派橫征。

translations.literal: Without any slight curbing and restraint, only additional levies and violent taxation.
translations.idiomatic: Rather than cut them back, the court only adds new levies and exorbitant taxes.

sentences.zh: 蓄一二蒼鷹乳虎之有司，以天下徇之已矣，所謂積外釁而釀內憂也。

translations.literal: Keeping one or two officials who are fierce hawks and nursing tigers, letting the whole realm serve them—this is what is called accumulating external provocations and brewing internal troubles.
translations.idiomatic: To keep a few predatory warlords and sacrifice the realm to their ambitions—this is how external threats are nurtured into civil catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 優詔報聞。

translations.literal: An excellent edict acknowledged receipt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor responded with a gracious edict acknowledging the memorial.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，南都亡。

translations.literal: The next year in the fifth month, the Southern Capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: The following May, the Southern Capital was lost.

sentences.zh: 六月，潞王降，杭州亦失守。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the Prince of Lu surrendered, and Hangzhou also was lost.
translations.idiomatic: In June the Prince of Lu surrendered, and Hangzhou fell as well.

sentences.zh: 宗周方食，推案慟哭，自是遂不食。

translations.literal: Zongzhou was just eating; he pushed the table and wept bitterly. From this he ceased eating.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou was at his meal when he shoved the table aside and broke into agonized weeping. From that moment he refused food.

sentences.zh: 移居郭外，有勸以文、謝故事者。

translations.literal: He moved to live outside the city wall; there were those who urged him with the precedents of Wen and Xie.
translations.idiomatic: He moved outside the city walls. Some urged him to follow the examples of Wen Tianxiang and Xie Fangde.

sentences.zh: 宗周曰：「北都之變，可以死，可以無死，以身在田裏，尚有望於中興也。

translations.literal: Zongzhou said: "At the change in the Northern Capital, one could die or not die—being in the fields, there was still hope of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhou said, "When the Northern Capital fell, one might die or one might live; I was in the countryside, and restoration still seemed possible.

sentences.zh: 南都之變，主上自棄其社稷，尚曰可以死，可以無死，以俟繼起有人也。

translations.literal: At the change in the Southern Capital, the sovereign himself abandoned his altars of state—yet one could still say one might die or not die, waiting for someone to arise afterward.
translations.idiomatic: When the Southern Capital fell, the emperor had abandoned his own throne—yet one might still choose to die or to live, in hope that another leader would emerge.

sentences.zh: 今吾越又降矣，老臣不死，尚何待乎？

translations.literal: Now our Yue has also surrendered. If this old minister does not die, what is there still to wait for?
translations.idiomatic: Now our own region of Yue has surrendered. If an old minister such as I does not die, what am I waiting for?

sentences.zh: 若曰身不在位，不當與城為存亡，獨不當與土為存亡乎？

translations.literal: If one says that because one is not in office one should not share the city's survival or destruction, should one not alone share the land's survival or destruction?
translations.idiomatic: If one argues that without office one need not share a city's fate, must one not still share one's native soil's fate?

sentences.zh: 此江萬里所以死也。」

translations.literal: This is why Jiang Wanli died."
translations.idiomatic: This was why Jiang Wanli chose death."

sentences.zh: 出辭祖墓，舟過西洋港，躍入水中，水淺不得死，舟人扶出之。

translations.literal: He went out to take leave at his ancestral tombs; his boat passed Xiyang Harbor and he leaped into the water. The water was shallow and he could not die; the boatmen pulled him out.
translations.idiomatic: He went to pay farewell at his ancestors' graves, then took a boat past Xiyang Harbor and threw himself into the water. The water was too shallow, and the boatmen pulled him out.

sentences.zh: 絕食二十三日，始猶進茗飲，後勺水不下者十三日，與門人問答如平時。

translations.literal: He abstained from food for twenty-three days—at first he still took tea, but for thirteen days afterward not even a spoonful of water would he take. With his disciples he questioned and answered as in ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: He fasted for twenty-three days. At first he still drank tea; for the last thirteen days he would not swallow even a spoonful of water. With his disciples he discussed and answered as though nothing were amiss.

sentences.zh: 閏六月八日卒，年六十有八。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the intercalary sixth month he died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the eighth day of the intercalary sixth month, aged sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 其門人徇義者有祝淵、王毓蓍。

translations.literal: Among his disciples who died for righteousness were Zhu Yuan and Wang Muzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Among his disciples who died for principle were Zhu Yuan and Wang Muzhi.

sentences.zh: 淵，字開美，海寧人。

translations.literal: Yuan, styled Kaimei, was a native of Haining.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yuan, courtesy name Kaimei, was from Haining.

sentences.zh: 崇禎六年舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chongzhen he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Chongzhen (1633) he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 自以年少學未充，棲峰巔僧舍，讀書三年，山僧罕見其面。

translations.literal: Considering himself young and his learning not yet full, he dwelled in a monk's cell on a peak summit, reading books for three years; the mountain monks rarely saw his face.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling himself too young and his learning incomplete, he secluded himself in a hermitage on a mountain peak for three years of study, rarely showing his face even to the monks.

sentences.zh: 十五年冬，會試入都，適宗周廷諍姜埰、熊開元削籍。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year winter, he went to the capital for the metropolitan examination; it happened that Zongzhou remonstrated at court regarding Jiang Cai and Xiong Kaiyuan being struck from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifteenth year (1642) he traveled to the capital for the metropolitan examination, just as Liu Zongzhou was remonstrating at court over the dismissal of Jiang Cai and Xiong Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 淵抗疏曰：「宗周戇直性成，忠孝天授，受任以來，蔬食不飽，終宵不寢，圖報國恩。

translations.literal: Yuan submitted a bold memorial saying: "Zongzhou is blunt and upright by nature, loyalty and filial piety heaven-bestowed. Since receiving appointment, he eats plain food without satiety, through the night does not sleep, seeking to repay the state's grace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yuan submitted a forceful memorial: "Liu Zongzhou is blunt and upright by nature, endowed with loyalty and filial devotion. Since taking office he has lived on frugal meals and slept little, devoting himself to repaying the state's grace.

sentences.zh: 今四方多難，貪墨成風，求一清剛臣以司風紀，孰與宗周？

translations.literal: Now on all sides are many difficulties; greed and corruption become the prevailing wind. To seek one upright and resolute minister to oversee discipline—who compares with Zongzhou?
translations.idiomatic: The realm faces calamity on every side and corruption runs rampant. If you seek an upright man to enforce discipline, who is better than Liu Zongzhou?

sentences.zh: 宗周以迂戇斥，繼之者必淟涊；

translations.literal: If Zongzhou is dismissed for being stiff and blunt, his successor will surely be obsequious;
translations.idiomatic: If Liu Zongzhou is dismissed as inflexible, his successor will surely be obsequious;

sentences.zh: 宗周以偏執斥，繼之者必便捷。

translations.literal: if Zongzhou is dismissed for being biased and stubborn, his successor will surely be slick and expedient.
translations.idiomatic: if he is dismissed as obstinate, his successor will surely be sly and expedient.

sentences.zh: 淟涊便捷之夫進，必且營私納賄，顛倒貞邪。

translations.literal: When obsequious and expedient men advance, they will surely scheme for private gain, accept bribes, and invert right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Once such obsequious and crafty men rise, they will trade favors for bribes and invert right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 乞收還成命，復其故官，天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: I beg to recall the completed order and restore his former office—the realm would be greatly fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to revoke the order and restore him to office. The realm would be the better for it."

sentences.zh: 帝得疏不懌，停淵會試，下禮官議。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the memorial he was displeased, suspended Yuan's metropolitan examination, and sent it down to the Board of Rites for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, displeased, barred Zhu Yuan from the metropolitan examination and referred the matter to the Board of Rites.

sentences.zh: 淵故不識宗周，既得命往謁。

translations.literal: Yuan had originally not known Zongzhou; having received permission he went to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yuan had never met Liu Zongzhou before, but once granted leave he went to visit him.

sentences.zh: 宗周曰：「子為此舉，無所為而為之乎，抑動於名心而為之也？」

translations.literal: Zongzhou said: "You made this act—was it done with no motive, or moved by the heart of fame?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zongzhou asked, "Did you act without ulterior motive, or were you moved by a craving for reputation?"

sentences.zh: 淵爽然避席曰：「先生名滿天下，誠恥不得列門墻爾，願執贄為弟子。」

translations.literal: Yuan, refreshed, left his mat and said: "The master's name fills the realm—I am truly ashamed at not being able to stand within his gate and wall. I wish to present tribute and become his disciple."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yuan rose from his seat and said frankly, "Your reputation fills the realm. I would be ashamed not to join your school. I wish to become your disciple."

sentences.zh: 明年，從宗周山陰。

translations.literal: The next year he followed Zongzhou to Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he followed Liu Zongzhou to Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 禮官議上，逮下詔獄，詰主使姓名。

translations.literal: When the Board of Rites submitted its deliberation, he was arrested and sent to the prison of the edict, and questioned about the name of the principal instigator.
translations.idiomatic: When the Board of Rites reported its findings, Zhu Yuan was thrown into the imperial prison and interrogated about who had incited him.

sentences.zh: 淵曰：「男兒死即死爾，何聽人指使為！」

translations.literal: Yuan said: "A man dies when he dies—why act on others' orders!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yuan said, "A man lives or dies by his own conviction. Why would I take orders from anyone?"

sentences.zh: 移刑部，進士共疏出淵。

translations.literal: The case was transferred to the Ministry of Justice; degree-holders jointly memorialized to release Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The case passed to the Ministry of Justice, and fellow jinshi submitted a joint memorial demanding his release.

sentences.zh: 未幾，都城陷，營死難太常少卿吳麟征喪，歸其柩。

translations.literal: Before long the capital fell; he managed the funeral of Wu Linzheng, Vice Minister of Ceremonies who died in martyrdom, and returned his coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, the capital fell. Zhu Yuan arranged the funeral of Wu Linzheng, the Vice Minister of Ceremonies who had died in the fall, and escorted his coffin home.

sentences.zh: 詣南京刑部，竟前獄，尚書諭止之。

translations.literal: He went to the Nanjing Ministry of Justice to pursue his former case; the minister instructed him to stop.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the Nanjing Ministry of Justice to pursue his old case, but the minister ordered him to desist.

sentences.zh: 上疏請誅奸輔，通政司抑不奏。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial requesting execution of treacherous ministers; the Transmission Office suppressed it and did not present it.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized calling for the execution of corrupt ministers, but the Transmission Office suppressed it.

sentences.zh: 給事中陳子龍疏薦淵及待詔塗仲吉義士，可為臺諫。

translations.literal: Censor Chen Zilong submitted a memorial recommending Yuan and the Hanlin attendant Tu Zhongji as righteous men fit for remonstrance offices.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretary Chen Zilong recommended Zhu Yuan and the Hanlin attendant Tu Zhongji as men of principle fit for censorial posts.

sentences.zh: 仲吉者，漳浦人，以諸生走萬里上書明黃道周冤，得罪杖譴者也。

translations.literal: Zhongji was a native of Zhangpu; as a student he traveled ten thousand li to submit a memorial clarifying Huang Daozhou's injustice, and was punished with beating and banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Zhongji was from Zhangpu. As a common student he had traveled a vast distance to petition on Huang Daozhou's behalf and was punished with beating and exile.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: It was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The recommendation was rejected.

sentences.zh: 宗周罷官家居，淵數往問學。

translations.literal: When Zongzhou was dismissed and lived at home, Yuan often went to seek learning.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Zongzhou was dismissed and returned home, Zhu Yuan visited him frequently to study.

sentences.zh: 嘗有過，入曲室長跪流涕自撾。

translations.literal: When he had faults, he entered a private room, knelt long, wept, and punished himself.
translations.idiomatic: When he had done wrong, he would go to a private room, kneel in tears, and chastise himself.

sentences.zh: 杭州失守，淵方葬母，趣竣工。

translations.literal: When Hangzhou was lost, Yuan was just burying his mother and hastened to finish.
translations.idiomatic: When Hangzhou fell, Zhu Yuan was burying his mother and rushed to complete the funeral.

sentences.zh: 既葬，還家設祭，即投繯而卒，年三十五也。

translations.literal: Once buried, he returned home, set out offerings, and immediately hanged himself and died, aged thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he returned home, made offerings, and hanged himself. He was thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 逾二日，宗周餓死。

translations.literal: Over two days later, Zongzhou starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later Liu Zongzhou died of starvation.

sentences.zh: 毓蓍，字元趾，會稽人。

translations.literal: Muzhi, styled Yuanzhi, was a native of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Muzhi, courtesy name Yuanzhi, was from Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 為諸生，跌宕不羈。

translations.literal: As a student he was unrestrained and unbridled.
translations.idiomatic: A student, he was wild and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 已，受業宗周之門，同門生鹹非笑之。

translations.literal: Later he received instruction under Zongzhou's gate; fellow students all mockingly laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Liu Zongzhou's disciple, to the derision of his fellow students.

sentences.zh: 杭州不守，宗周絕粒未死，毓蓍上書曰：「願先生早自裁，毋為王炎午所吊。」

translations.literal: When Hangzhou was not held, Zongzhou had abstained from grain but not died; Muzhi submitted a letter saying: "I wish the master would early take his own life, lest he be lamented by Wang Yanwu."
translations.idiomatic: When Hangzhou fell, Liu Zongzhou was starving himself but had not yet died. Wang Muzhi wrote: "Master, I urge you to end your life soon, lest you be mocked by someone like Wang Yanwu."

sentences.zh: 俄一友來視，毓蓍曰：「子若何？」

translations.literal: Shortly a friend came to visit; Muzhi said: "What of you?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon a friend came to call. Wang Muzhi asked, "What will you do?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「有陶淵明故事在。」

translations.literal: He said: "There is Tao Yuanming's precedent."
translations.idiomatic: The friend replied, "One always has the example of Tao Yuanming."

sentences.zh: 毓蓍曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Muzhi said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Muzhi said, "No.

sentences.zh: 吾輩聲色中人，慮久則難持也。」

translations.literal: We are men of sound and color—I fear that over time it will be hard to maintain."
translations.idiomatic: We are men who love pleasure. Given time, I fear we could not hold to such restraint."

sentences.zh: 一日，遍召故交歡飲，伶人奏樂。

translations.literal: One day he called all old friends for merry drinking; musicians performed.
translations.idiomatic: One day he summoned all his old friends for a farewell feast, with musicians playing.

sentences.zh: 酒罷，攜燈出門，投柳橋下，先宗周一月死。

translations.literal: When the wine ended, carrying a lamp he went out the gate and cast himself beneath Willow Bridge, dying one month before Zongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine was spent, he took a lamp, walked out, and drowned himself beneath Willow Bridge—one month before Liu Zongzhou's death.

sentences.zh: 鄉人私謚正義先生。

translations.literal: His fellow townsmen privately posthumously titled him Master of Upright Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His countrymen gave him the posthumous title Master of Righteous Integrity.

sentences.zh: 宗周始受業於許孚遠。

translations.literal: Zongzhou first received instruction under Xu Fuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zongzhou first studied under Xu Fuyuan.

sentences.zh: 已，入東林書院，與高攀龍輩講習。

translations.literal: Later he entered the Donglin Academy and lectured and studied with Gao Panlong and company.
translations.idiomatic: He later entered the Donglin Academy, where he studied with Gao Panlong and others.

sentences.zh: 馮從吾首善書院之會，宗周亦與焉。

translations.literal: At Feng Congwu's Shoushan Academy gathering, Zongzhou also participated.
translations.idiomatic: He also took part in the gatherings at Feng Congwu's Shoushan Academy.

sentences.zh: 越中自王守仁後，一傳為王畿，再傳為周汝登、陶望齡，三傳為陶奭齡，皆雜於禪。

translations.literal: In Yue since Wang Shouren, the first transmission was Wang Ji, the second Zhou Rudeng and Tao Wangling, the third Tao Shiling—all mixed with Chan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yue region after Wang Yangming, learning passed through Wang Ji, then Zhou Rudeng and Tao Wangling, then Tao Shiling—each generation more infused with Chan Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 奭齡講學白馬山，為因果說，去守仁益遠。

translations.literal: Shiling lectured on White Horse Mountain, expounding causes and effects, departing ever farther from Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Shiling taught on White Horse Mountain, preaching karmic causality, drifting ever further from Wang Yangming's teaching.

sentences.zh: 宗周憂之，築證人書院，集同誌講肄。

translations.literal: Zongzhou worried about this, built the Zhengren Academy, and gathered like-minded men to lecture and study.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed by this trend, Liu Zongzhou founded the Zhengren Academy and gathered like-minded scholars for serious study.

sentences.zh: 且死，語門人曰：「學之要，誠而已，主敬其功也。

translations.literal: Near death he told his disciples: "The essence of learning is sincerity only; reverence is its function.
translations.idiomatic: Near death he told his disciples: "The heart of learning is sincerity; reverence is its practice.

sentences.zh: 敬則誠，誠則天。

translations.literal: Reverence then sincerity; sincerity then Heaven.
