translations.idiomatic: Through reverence comes sincerity; through sincerity one reaches Heaven.

sentences.zh: 良知之說，鮮有不流於禪者。」

translations.literal: The doctrine of innate knowledge rarely fails to flow into Chan."
translations.idiomatic: Few who preach innate moral knowledge avoid sliding into Chan."

sentences.zh: 宗周在官之日少，其事君，不以面從為敬。

translations.literal: Zongzhou's days in office were few; in serving the sovereign he did not take agreeable compliance as reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zongzhou spent little time in office. In serving the emperor he did not equate agreement with loyalty.

sentences.zh: 入朝，雖處暗室，不敢南向。

translations.literal: Entering court, even when in a dark chamber he did not dare face south.
translations.idiomatic: Even in a private room at court he would not sit facing south—the direction reserved for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 或訊大獄，會大議，對明旨，必卻坐拱立移時。

translations.literal: Whether interrogating in major cases, meeting in great deliberations, or receiving the bright edict, he would always sit back, bow standing, for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Whether presiding over major trials, attending great deliberations, or receiving imperial commands, he would always step back, bow, and stand for a long moment.

sentences.zh: 或謝病，徒步家居，布袍粗飯，樂道安貧。

translations.literal: When he pleaded illness, he walked on foot to live at home—cloth robe and coarse rice, delighting in the Way and content in poverty.
translations.idiomatic: When at home on sick leave he went about on foot in coarse robes, eating simple food, delighting in the Way and accepting poverty.

sentences.zh: 聞召就道，嘗不能具冠裳。

translations.literal: On hearing summons he set out on the road, yet often could not fully assemble cap and garments.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned to office he would set out at once, sometimes without even proper ceremonial dress.

sentences.zh: 學者稱念臺先生。

translations.literal: Scholars called him Master Niantai.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars know him as Master Niantai.

sentences.zh: 子汋，字伯繩。

translations.literal: His son Zuo, styled Bosheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Zuo, courtesy name Bosheng.

sentences.zh: 黃道周，字幼平，漳浦人。

translations.literal: Huang Daozhou, styled Youping, was a native of Zhangpu.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou, courtesy name Youping, was from Zhangpu.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Tianqi (1622).

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授編修，為經筵展書官。

translations.literal: He was changed to Hanlin bachelor, appointed Compiler, and served as book-displaying official at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a Hanlin bachelor and Compiler, serving as book bearer at the imperial lecture sessions.

sentences.zh: 故事，必膝行前，道周獨否，魏忠賢目攝之。

translations.literal: By precedent one must advance on knees; Daozhou alone refused. Wei Zhongxian glared to restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, book bearers advanced on their knees. Huang Daozhou alone refused. Wei Zhongxian fixed him with a menacing stare.

sentences.zh: 未幾，內艱歸。

translations.literal: Before long, on his mother's death he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, he returned home to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年起故官，進右中允。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen he resumed his former office and was promoted to Right Sub-Reader.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chongzhen (1629) he resumed office and was promoted to Right Sub-Reader.

sentences.zh: 三疏救故相錢龍錫，降調，龍錫得減死。

translations.literal: Three times he memorialized to save former Chancellor Qian Longxi; he was demoted and transferred, and Longxi's death sentence was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted three memorials to save the former chancellor Qian Longxi. Though Huang Daozhou himself was demoted, Qian's death sentence was commuted.

sentences.zh: 五年正月方候補，遘疾求去。

translations.literal: In the fifth year first month he was just waiting for reassignment when he fell ill and requested to leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year (1632), while awaiting reassignment, he fell ill and requested leave.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，上疏曰：

translations.literal: On the verge of departure, he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Before departing, he submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣自幼學《易》，以天道為準。

translations.literal: Your minister from youth has studied the Changes, taking the Way of Heaven as standard.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has studied the Book of Changes since youth, taking Heaven's way as his standard.

sentences.zh: 上下載籍二千四百年，考其治亂，百不失一。

translations.literal: In the records above and below of two thousand four hundred years, examining their order and chaos, in a hundred cases not one fails.
translations.idiomatic: Across twenty-four centuries of history, its judgments of order and chaos have scarcely ever missed.

sentences.zh: 陛下禦極之元年，正當《師》之上九，其爻云：「大君有命，開國承家，小人勿用。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty's first year upon ascending the throne exactly matches the top ninth line of the Hexagram of the Army; its line says: "The great lord has commands—establish states and inherit families; do not use petty men."
translations.idiomatic: The year Your Majesty took the throne corresponds to the top line of the Hexagram Army, which reads: "The sovereign receives Heaven's mandate to establish states and lineages; petty men must not be employed."

sentences.zh: 陛下思賢才不遽得，懲小人不易絕，蓋陛下有大君之實，而小人懷幹命之心。

translations.literal: Your Majesty thinks talented men are not quickly obtained and that punishing petty men is not easily ended—generally Your Majesty has the substance of the great lord, while petty men harbor hearts of usurping the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: You seek worthy men but cannot find them quickly; you would punish the wicked but cannot easily cut them off. Your Majesty possesses the qualities of a true sovereign, yet petty men harbor ambitions to seize power.

sentences.zh: 臣入都以來，所見諸大臣皆無遠猷，動尋苛細，治朝寧者以督責為要談，治邊疆者以姑息為上策。

translations.literal: Since your minister entered the capital, the great ministers seen all lack far-reaching plans, constantly pursuing petty minutiae; those governing the tranquil court take stern oversight as essential talk, those governing the frontier take indulgence as the supreme strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Since coming to court I have found the ministers devoid of vision, obsessed with petty details. Those managing domestic affairs speak only of harsh enforcement; those managing the frontiers preach only appeasement.

sentences.zh: 序仁義道德，則以為迂昧而不經；

translations.literal: When setting forth benevolence, righteousness, morality, and the Way, they deem it stodgy, obscure, and unorthodox;
translations.idiomatic: Speak of benevolence and righteousness and they dismiss it as impractical pedantry;

sentences.zh: 奉刀筆簿書，則以為通達而知務。

translations.literal: when honoring legal documents and ledger books, they deem it penetrating and knowing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: praise legalism and administrative minutiae and they call it worldly wisdom.

sentences.zh: 一切磨勘，則葛藤終年；

translations.literal: In every case of verification and audit, entanglements last the whole year;
translations.idiomatic: Endless audits tie the bureaucracy in knots for months on end;

sentences.zh: 一意不調，而株連四起。

translations.literal: one thread of disharmony and linked punishments rise on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: a single inconsistency triggers a chain of reprisals.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲整頓紀綱，斥攘外患，諸臣用之以滋章法令，摧折縉紳；

translations.literal: Your Majesty wishes to rectify discipline and repel external troubles—the ministers use this to multiply statutes and decrees, crushing the gentry;
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty seeks to restore discipline and repel foreign threats, ministers use it to multiply laws and crush the scholar-official class;

sentences.zh: 陛下欲剔弊防奸，懲一警百，諸臣用之以借題修隙，斂怨市權。

translations.literal: Your Majesty wishes to root out abuses and guard against villainy, punishing one to warn a hundred—the ministers use this to borrow topics and mend grudges, gathering resentment and trading for power.
translations.idiomatic: when you seek to purge corruption and punish the guilty, they use it to settle scores and consolidate power.

sentences.zh: 且外廷諸臣敢誑陛下者，必不在拘攣守文之士，而在權力謬巧之人；

translations.literal: Moreover, among outer court ministers those who dare deceive Your Majesty are surely not among the constrained and text-keeping gentlemen, but among the power-seeking and cunningly erroneous men;
translations.idiomatic: Those in the outer court who dare deceive Your Majesty are not the rigid conservatives but the power-hungry schemers;

sentences.zh: 內廷諸臣敢誑陛下者，必不在錐刀泉布之微，而在阿柄神叢之大。

translations.literal: among inner court ministers those who dare deceive Your Majesty are surely not among the petty penny-and-coin minions, but among the great holders of hidden handles and sacred groves.
translations.idiomatic: those in the inner court who dare deceive you are not minor peculators but the great wielders of hidden patronage and influence.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下超然省覽，旁稽載籍，自古迄今，決無數米量薪，可成遠大之猷，吹毛數睫，可奏三五之治者。

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty transcendentally examine and review, consulting records on all sides—from ancient to present, assuredly none by counting rice and measuring firewood can achieve far-reaching plans, nor by blowing hairs and counting eyelashes can accomplish the governance of the Three Five.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to rise above petty counsel and consult history: from antiquity to the present, no ruler who counted grains of rice or hairs on eyelashes ever achieved a great vision or the golden age of the sage-kings.

sentences.zh: 彼小人見事，智每短於事前，言每多於事後。

translations.literal: Those petty men in viewing affairs—their wisdom is always short before the event, their words always abundant after the event.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men are always wise after the fact and never before.

sentences.zh: 不救淩圍，而謂淩城必不可築；

translations.literal: They did not rescue the siege at Ling, yet claimed the fort at Ling absolutely could not be built;
translations.idiomatic: They refused to relieve the siege at Ling, yet insisted the fort at Ling could never have been built;

sentences.zh: 不理島民，而謂島眾必不可用；

translations.literal: They did not attend to the island people, yet claimed the island populace absolutely could not be employed;
translations.idiomatic: They neglected the islanders, yet insisted the island forces were unusable;

sentences.zh: 兵逃於久頓，而謂亂生於無兵；

translations.literal: Troops fled from prolonged encampment, yet they claimed disorder arose from having no troops;
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers deserted from prolonged stagnation, yet they blamed the unrest on insufficient troops;

sentences.zh: 餉糜於漏邑，而謂功銷於無餉。

translations.literal: Provisions were wasted at leaky posts, yet they claimed achievement was lost from lack of provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies were squandered through leaky administration, yet they attributed failure to inadequate funding.

sentences.zh: 亂視熒聽，浸淫相欺，馴至極壞，不可復挽，臣竊危之。

translations.literal: Gazing in confusion and listening in bewilderment, gradually deluding one another, tame until utterly ruined—beyond recovery. Your minister privately fears this.
translations.idiomatic: Men look blindly and listen falsely, deceiving one another until all is ruined beyond repair. I tremble at where this leads.

sentences.zh: 自二年以來，以察去弊，而弊愈多；

translations.literal: Since the second year, using scrutiny to remove abuses—yet abuses have grown more numerous;
translations.idiomatic: Since the second year of your reign, every effort to purge corruption through investigation has only multiplied the abuses;

sentences.zh: 以威創頑，而威滋殫。

translations.literal: Using severity to chastise the stubborn—yet authority has grown ever more exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Every attempt to cow the wicked through harsh punishment has only drained your authority.

sentences.zh: 是亦反申、商以歸周、孔，捐苛細以崇惇大之時矣。

translations.literal: This is also the time to turn back from Shen and Shang to return to Zhou and Confucius, to abandon harsh minutiae and exalt magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: Surely this is the moment to abandon the Legalism of Shen Buhai and Shang Yang and return to the Confucian ideals of the Zhou—to set aside petty severity in favor of generous governance.

sentences.zh: 帝不懌，摘「葛藤」、「株連」數語，令具陳。

translations.literal: The Emperor was displeased, picked out the several phrases "entanglements" and "linked punishment," and ordered a full account.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took offense, seized on the phrases "entanglements" and "guilt by association," and ordered Huang Daozhou to explain himself in full.

sentences.zh: 道周上言曰：

translations.literal: Daozhou submitted words saying:
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou submitted a memorial stating:

sentences.zh: 邇年諸臣所目營心計，無一實為朝廷者。

translations.literal: In recent years what the various ministers have eyed and plotted in their hearts—not one was truly for the court.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the ministers' every scheme and calculation has served anything but the throne.

sentences.zh: 其用人行事，不過推求報復而已。

translations.literal: Their employing men and conducting affairs amounts to nothing but pursuing revenge.
translations.idiomatic: In appointing men and handling affairs they do nothing but settle scores.

sentences.zh: 自前歲春月以後，盛談邊疆，實非為陛下邊疆，乃為逆珰而翻邊疆也；

translations.literal: Since the spring month of the year before last, they have talked extravagantly of the frontier—yet in truth not for Your Majesty's frontier, but to overturn the frontier for a treacherous eunuch faction;
translations.idiomatic: Since the spring before last they have talked endlessly of border affairs—not for Your Majesty's frontiers, but to weaponize the borders on behalf of a treacherous eunuch faction;

sentences.zh: 去歲春月以後，盛言科場，實非為陛下科場，乃為仇隙而翻科場也。

translations.literal: Since the spring month of last year, they have spoken extravagantly of the examination field—yet in truth not for Your Majesty's examinations, but to overturn the examinations over private enmity.
translations.idiomatic: Since last spring they have harped on the examination system—not for Your Majesty's examinations, but to turn the examinations into a weapon against personal enemies.

sentences.zh: 此非所謂「葛藤」、「株連」乎？

translations.literal: Is this not what is called "entanglements" and "linked punishment"?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not precisely what I meant by "entanglements" and "guilt by association"?

sentences.zh: 自古外患未弭，則大臣一心以憂外患；

translations.literal: From antiquity, when external troubles were not yet settled, great ministers with one heart worried over external troubles;
translations.idiomatic: Throughout history, when foreign threats persisted, ministers united in fear of foreign threats;

sentences.zh: 小人未退，則大臣一心以憂小人。

translations.literal: When petty men had not withdrawn, great ministers with one heart worried over petty men.
translations.idiomatic: When petty men had not been removed, ministers united in fear of petty men.

sentences.zh: 今獨以遺君父，而大臣自處於催科比較之末。

translations.literal: Now alone is this left to the ruler and father, while great ministers place themselves at the tail end of tax collection and litigation.
translations.idiomatic: Now they leave everything to Your Majesty and the dynasty, while ministers reduce themselves to squabbling over tax collection and legal disputes.

sentences.zh: 行事而事失，則曰事不可為；

translations.literal: When in conducting affairs affairs fail, they say affairs cannot be done;
translations.idiomatic: When their policies fail, they declare that nothing can be done;

sentences.zh: 用人而人失，則曰人不足用。

translations.literal: When in employing men men fail, they say men are insufficient to employ.
translations.idiomatic: When their appointees fail, they declare that no worthy men can be found.

sentences.zh: 此臣所謂舛也。

translations.literal: This is what your minister calls perversity.
translations.idiomatic: This is what I call getting everything backward.

sentences.zh: 三十年來，釀成門戶之禍，今又取縉紳稍有器識者，舉網投阱，即緩急安得一士之用乎！

translations.literal: For thirty years factional strife has been brewing; now again they cast the net and drop the trap on gentry of slight talent and insight—when urgency comes how can one man be of use!
translations.idiomatic: Thirty years of factional strife have brought us to this pass. Now they hunt down every gifted scholar-official—and in an emergency, who will be left to serve?

sentences.zh: 凡絕餌而去者，必非魚；

translations.literal: All who cut off bait and depart must not be mandarin fish;
translations.idiomatic: Those who refuse bait and walk away are never ordinary fish;

sentences.zh: 戀棧而來者，必非駿馬。

translations.literal: Those who cling to the manger and come must not be fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: Those who cling to the trough for feed are never fine horses.

sentences.zh: 以利祿豢士，則所豢者必嗜利之臣；

translations.literal: To feed scholars with profit and stipend, then those fed must be ministers who covet profit;
translations.idiomatic: Feed scholars with salary and emoluments, and you will attract only those who crave wealth;

sentences.zh: 以箠楚驅人，則就驅者必駑駘之骨。

translations.literal: To drive men with beating and lashes, then those who submit to driving must be jaded nags.
translations.idiomatic: Drive men with the whip, and only worn-out hacks will answer the call.

sentences.zh: 今諸臣之才具心術，陛下其知之矣。

translations.literal: Now as to the talents and schemes of the various ministers—Your Majesty surely knows them.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty knows full well what sort of talents and motives these ministers possess.

sentences.zh: 知其為小人而又以小人矯之，則小人之焰益張；

translations.literal: Knowing they are petty men yet using petty men to correct them, then petty men's arrogance grows stronger;
translations.idiomatic: If you recognize them as petty men yet employ petty men to restrain them, the petty men's power only grows;

sentences.zh: 知其為君子而更以小人參之，則君子之功不立。

translations.literal: Knowing they are gentlemen yet further mixing in petty men with them, then gentlemen's achievements cannot stand.
translations.idiomatic: If you recognize worthy men yet pair them with petty men, the worthy will accomplish nothing.

sentences.zh: 天下總此人才，不在廊廟則在林藪。

translations.literal: Under Heaven talent is all of this—if not in the halls of government, then in the forests and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: All the talent in the empire is either in office or in the wilderness.

sentences.zh: 臣所知識者有馬如蛟、毛羽健、任贊化，所聞習者有惠世揚、李邦華，在仕籍者有徐良彥、曾櫻、朱大典、陸夢龍、鄒嘉生，皆卓犖駿偉，使當一面，必有可觀。

translations.literal: Those your minister knows personally include Ma Rujiao, Mao Yujian, and Ren Zanhua; those heard and acquainted with include Hui Shiyang and Li Banghua; those on the official register include Xu Liangyan, Zeng Ying, Zhu Dadian, Lu Menglong, and Zou Jiasheng—all outstanding and bold; give them each a command and there will surely be something to see.
translations.idiomatic: Men I know personally include Ma Rujiao, Mao Yujian, and Ren Zanhua; men of known reputation include Hui Shiyang and Li Banghua; men still on the rolls include Xu Liangyan, Zeng Ying, Zhu Dadian, Lu Menglong, and Zou Jiasheng—all of them exceptional. Given each his own theater of command, they would surely distinguish themselves.

sentences.zh: 語皆刺大學士周延儒、溫體仁，帝益不懌，斥為民。

translations.literal: The words all stung Grand Secretaries Zhou Yanru and Wen Tiren; the Emperor grew more displeased and dismissed him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: His words were aimed at Grand Secretaries Zhou Yanru and Wen Tiren. The emperor grew angrier still and stripped him of office, reducing him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 九年用薦召，復故官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, through recommendation he was summoned and restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (1636), he was recalled on recommendation and restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 明年閏月，久旱修省，道周上言：「近者中外齋宿，為百姓請命，而五日內系兩尚書，未聞有人申一疏者。

translations.literal: The next year, intercalary month, during drought and self-examination, Daozhou submitted words: "Recently within and without the court fasted and lodged, pleading for the people, yet within five days two Ministers of State were imprisoned—no word was heard of anyone submitting a single memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the intercalary month, during a drought rite of self-examination Huang Daozhou memorialized: "Recently court and country have fasted and prayed for the people, yet within five days two ministers were thrown into prison—and not one official spoke up with a memorial.

sentences.zh: 安望其戡亂除兇，贊平明之治乎？

translations.literal: How can one look to them to suppress disorder and eliminate violence, to assist bright and enlightened governance?
translations.idiomatic: How can such men be expected to quell rebellion, punish the wicked, and support enlightened rule?

sentences.zh: 陛下焦勞於上，小民展轉於下，而諸臣括囊其間，稍有人心，宜不至此。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty toils anxiously above, the common people toss and turn below, yet the various ministers purse their sacks between—had they the slightest human heart, it ought not reach this."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty burns with anxiety above, the people suffer below, yet the ministers between them hold their tongues and pocket their hands. Men with any conscience at all ought not behave so."

sentences.zh: 又上疏曰：「陛下寬仁弘宥，有身任重寄至七八載罔效、擁權自若者。

translations.literal: Again he submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty is broad and forgiving, yet there are some who have borne heavy trust for seven or eight years without effect yet hold power as before.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial: "Your Majesty is generous and magnanimous, yet some ministers have held great power for seven or eight years without result and remain untouchable.

sentences.zh: 積漸以來，國無是非，朝無枉直，中外臣工率茍且圖事，誠可痛憤。

translations.literal: Gradually accumulating to the present, the state has no right and wrong, the court has no wrong and straight—ministers within and without generally take expedience in planning affairs. Truly this can pain and enrage.
translations.idiomatic: Over time the state has lost all moral compass, the court all sense of justice. Officials everywhere act with mere expediency. This is truly infuriating.

sentences.zh: 然其視聽一系於上。

translations.literal: Yet their seeing and hearing all depend on what is above.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what they see and hear depends entirely on the tone set from above.

sentences.zh: 上急催科則下急賄賂；

translations.literal: When above presses for tax collection, then below presses for bribes;
translations.idiomatic: When the throne presses for tax collection, officials below press for bribes;

sentences.zh: 上樂鍥核，則下樂巉險；

translations.literal: When above delights in engraved verification, then below delights in sharp peril;
translations.idiomatic: When the throne delights in petty legal exactitude, officials below delight in vicious cunning;

sentences.zh: 上喜告訐，則下喜誣陷。

translations.literal: When above delights in informing, then below delights in false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne delights in informers, officials below delight in false accusations.

sentences.zh: 當此南北交訌，奈何與市井細民，申勃谿之談，修睚眥之隙乎。」

translations.literal: At this moment north and south are in mutual strife—how can one with market folk and petty people discuss family squabbles and mend grudges over trifles?"
translations.idiomatic: With north and south at war, how can the court descend to the level of marketplace gossips, wrangling over family quarrels and settling petty grudges?"

sentences.zh: 時體仁方招奸人構東林、復社之獄，故道周及之。

translations.literal: At that time Tiren was just recruiting villains to frame cases against the Donglin and Fushe factions, so Daozhou reached this.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wen Tiren was recruiting scoundrels to engineer prosecutions against the Donglin and Fushe factions, which is why Huang Daozhou raised these points.

sentences.zh: 旋進右諭德，掌司經局，疏辭。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted Right Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, in charge of the Classics Bureau, and memorialized to decline.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Right Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and placed in charge of the Classics Bureau, but submitted a memorial declining the appointment.

sentences.zh: 因言己有三罪、四恥、七不如。

translations.literal: He then spoke of having three faults, four shames, and seven betters.
translations.idiomatic: In it he listed three faults, four shames, and seven men superior to himself.

sentences.zh: 三罪、四恥，以自責。

translations.literal: The three faults and four shames were self-reproach.
translations.idiomatic: The three faults and four shames were confessions of his own failings.

sentences.zh: 七不如者，謂「品行高峻，卓絕倫表，不如劉宗周；

translations.literal: The seven betters meant: "In upright conduct lofty and surpassing all others, not equal to Liu Zongzhou;
translations.idiomatic: The seven betters ran: "In moral character lofty and peerless, I am not the equal of Liu Zongzhou;

sentences.zh: 至性奇情，無愧純孝，不如倪元璐；

translations.literal: In utmost nature and singular feeling, without shame before pure filial piety, not equal to Ni Yuanlu;
translations.idiomatic: In sincerity of feeling and depth of devotion, I cannot match Ni Yuanlu;

sentences.zh: 湛深大慮，遠見深計，不如魏呈潤；

translations.literal: In profound deliberation and great consideration, in farseeing plans and deep design, not equal to Wei Chengrun;
translations.idiomatic: In depth of thought and far-reaching vision, I cannot match Wei Chengrun;

sentences.zh: 犯言敢諫，清裁絕俗，不如詹爾選、吳執禦；

translations.literal: In violation of speech and daring remonstrance, in pure judgment transcending the vulgar, not equal to Zhan Erxuan and Wu Zhiyu;
translations.idiomatic: In bold remonstrance and uncompromising integrity, I cannot match Zhan Erxuan and Wu Zhiyu;

sentences.zh: 誌尚高雅，博學多通，不如華亭布衣陳繼儒、龍溪舉人張燮；

translations.literal: In noble aspiration and elegance, in broad learning and manifold mastery, not equal to the Huating commoner Chen Jiru and the Longxi expectant official Zhang Xie;
translations.idiomatic: In refined taste and erudition, I cannot match the Huating scholar Chen Jiru and the Longxi licentiate Zhang Xie;

sentences.zh: 至圜土累系之臣，樸心純行，不如李汝璨、傅朝佑；

translations.literal: And among officials imprisoned in the round-earth prisons, in plain hearts and pure conduct, not equal to Li Ruchen and Fu Chaoyou;
translations.idiomatic: And among the men languishing in prison, in simple integrity and pure conduct, I cannot match Li Ruchen and Fu Chaoyou;

sentences.zh: 文章意氣，坎坷磊落，不如錢謙益、鄭鄤。」

translations.literal: In literary spirit and moral vigor, in hardship yet lofty forthrightness, not equal to Qian Qianyi and Zheng Man."
translations.idiomatic: In literary talent and force of character, in unyielding integrity despite adversity, I cannot match Qian Qianyi and Zheng Man."

sentences.zh: 鄤方被杖母大詬，帝得疏駭異，責以顛倒是非。

translations.literal: Zheng Man was just then under harsh condemnation for beating his mother; the Emperor received the memorial with shock and reproached him for reversing right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Man was then facing severe condemnation for beating his mother. The emperor read the memorial with alarm and rebuked Huang Daozhou for turning truth on its head.

sentences.zh: 道周疏辯，語復營護鄤。

translations.literal: Daozhou memorialized in defense, his words again sheltering Man.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou submitted a defense, again shielding Zheng Man.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，嚴旨切責。

translations.literal: The Emperor grew angry and issued a stern edict of sharp rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and issued a stern edict of reprimand.

sentences.zh: 道周以文章風節高天下，嚴冷方剛，不諧流俗。

translations.literal: Daozhou's literary achievement and moral integrity were high under Heaven; stern, cold, upright and inflexible, he did not harmonize with vulgar custom.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou's literary renown and moral stature were unmatched. Stern, uncompromising, and inflexible, he would not bend to convention.

sentences.zh: 公卿多畏而忌之，乃藉不如鄤語為口實。

translations.literal: The dukes and ministers mostly feared and envied him, then borrowing the words of not being equal to Man as a pretext for talk.
translations.idiomatic: Grandees and ministers mostly feared and resented him, seizing on his "not equal to Zheng Man" remark as a talking point against him.

sentences.zh: 其冬，擇東宮講官。

translations.literal: That winter, lecturers for the Eastern Palace were chosen.
translations.idiomatic: That winter lecturers for the crown prince were selected.

sentences.zh: 體仁已罷，張至發當國，擯道周不與。

translations.literal: Tiren had already been dismissed; Zhang Zhifa held the state, excluding Daozhou from participation.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tiren had already been dismissed. Zhang Zhifa was chief minister and excluded Huang Daozhou from consideration.

sentences.zh: 其同官項煜、楊廷麟不平，上疏推讓道周。

translations.literal: His colleagues Xiang Yu and Yang Tinglin were indignant and submitted memorials yielding place to Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues Xiang Yu and Yang Tinglin protested, submitting memorials recommending Huang Daozhou in their stead.

sentences.zh: 至發言：「鄤杖母，明旨煌煌，道周自謂不如，安可為元良輔導。」

translations.literal: Zhifa spoke: "Zheng Man beat his mother—the clear edict shines bright; Daozhou himself said he was not equal—how can he serve as tutor to the heir apparent?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhifa objected: "Zheng Man beat his mother—the imperial decree on the matter is explicit. Huang Daozhou declared himself Zheng Man's inferior—how can he tutor the crown prince?"

sentences.zh: 道周遂移疾乞休，不許。

translations.literal: Daozhou then pleaded illness and requested retirement; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou then claimed illness and asked to retire. The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 十一年二月，帝御經筵。

translations.literal: Eleventh year, second month—the Emperor attended the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eleventh year (1638), the emperor attended the Classics lecture.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書鄭三俊方下吏，講官黃景昉救之，帝未許。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Zheng Sanjun had just been sent down for punishment; lecturer Huang Jingfang rescued him, but the Emperor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Zheng Sanjun had just been arrested. Lecturer Huang Jingfang interceded for him, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 而帝適追論舊講官姚希孟嘗請漕儲全折以為非。

translations.literal: Yet the Emperor just then pursued discussion of former lecturer Yao Ximeng, who had once petitioned that full conversion of tribute-grain transport to silver was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then revisiting the case of the former lecturer Yao Ximeng, who had once argued against converting all grain tribute payments to silver.

sentences.zh: 道周聽未審，謂帝將寬三俊念希孟也，因言：「故輔臣文震孟一生蹇直，未蒙帷蓋恩。

translations.literal: Daozhou had not heard clearly and supposed the Emperor would show leniency to Sanjun in remembrance of Ximeng, so he spoke: "Former Assistant Grand Secretary Wen Zhenmeng was upright all his life yet never received the grace of canopy and cover.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou had not followed the discussion closely and assumed the emperor meant to show leniency toward Zheng Sanjun out of regard for Yao Ximeng. He spoke up: "The late Assistant Grand Secretary Wen Zhenmeng was upright all his life yet never received imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 天下士，生如三俊，歿如震孟、希孟，求其影似，未可多得。」

translations.literal: Scholars under Heaven—living like Sanjun, dead like Zhenmeng and Ximeng—to seek their likeness, not many can be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: Scholars like Zheng Sanjun in life, like Wen Zhenmeng and Yao Ximeng in death—men even remotely like them are scarce."

sentences.zh: 帝以所對失實，責令回奏。

translations.literal: The Emperor, finding the reply inaccurate, rebuked and ordered him to memorialize in reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, finding his answer wide of the mark, rebuked him and ordered a written reply.

sentences.zh: 再奏再詰，至三奏乃已。

translations.literal: He memorialized again and was questioned again; only after a third memorial did it cease.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted again and was rebuked again; only after a third submission did the matter end.

sentences.zh: 凡道周所建白，未嘗得一俞旨，道周顧言不已。

translations.literal: In all Daozhou's proposals, never once did he obtain an assenting edict—yet Daozhou kept speaking without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: None of Huang Daozhou's proposals ever won imperial approval—yet he kept speaking without cease.

sentences.zh: 六月，廷推閣臣。

translations.literal: Sixth month—the court jointly recommended Grand Secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, the court conducted a joint nomination for grand secretaries.

sentences.zh: 道周已充日講官，遷少詹事，得與名。

translations.literal: Daozhou had already served as daily lecturer and been transferred to Junior Guardian, and qualified for nomination.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou, by then serving as daily lecturer and promoted to Junior Guardian, was among those nominated.

sentences.zh: 帝不用，用楊嗣昌等五人。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not employ him and employed Yang Sichang and four others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor passed him over and appointed Yang Sichang and four others.

sentences.zh: 道周乃草三疏，一劾嗣昌，一劾陳新甲，一劾遼撫方一藻，同日上之。

translations.literal: Daozhou then drafted three memorials—one impeaching Sichang, one impeaching Chen Xinji, one impeaching Liaodong Grand Coordinator Fang Yizao—submitting all on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou then drafted three memorials—one impeaching Yang Sichang, one Chen Xinji, one Fang Yizao, Liaodong grand coordinator—submitting all three the same day.

sentences.zh: 其劾嗣昌，謂：

translations.literal: In impeaching Sichang, he stated:
translations.idiomatic: In the memorial against Yang Sichang he wrote:

sentences.zh: 天下無無父之子，亦無不臣之子。

translations.literal: Under Heaven there is no son without a father, and no son who is not a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Under heaven there is no son without a father, and no subject without loyalty.

sentences.zh: 衛開方不省其親，管仲至比之豭狗；

translations.literal: Wei Kaifang did not visit his parents—Guan Zhong even compared him to a pig-dog;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Kaifang neglected his parents—Guan Zhong compared him to a pig or dog;

sentences.zh: 李定不喪繼母，宋世共指為人梟。

translations.literal: Li Ding did not mourn his stepmother—the Song age jointly pointed to him as a human owl.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ding failed to mourn his stepmother—the Song dynasty unanimously denounced him as less than human.

sentences.zh: 今遂有不持兩服，坐司馬堂如楊嗣昌者。

translations.literal: Now there are those who do not wear both mourning garments yet sit at the Sima Hall like Yang Sichang.
translations.idiomatic: Now we have Yang Sichang, who did not observe proper mourning yet took up office at Sima Hall.

sentences.zh: 宣大督臣盧象升以父殯在途，搥心飲血，請就近推補，乃忽有並推在籍守制之旨。

translations.literal: Xuan-Da Governor-General Lu Xiangsheng, with his father's coffin en route, beat his breast and drank blood, requesting nearby recommended replacement—yet suddenly there was an edict jointly recommending those at home observing mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuan-Da governor-general Lu Xiangsheng, with his father's coffin still on the road, pleaded in anguish for a nearby replacement—yet suddenly came an edict nominating men still at home in mourning.

sentences.zh: 夫守制者可推，則聞喪者可不去；

translations.literal: If those observing mourning can be recommended, then those who hear of a death need not leave;
translations.idiomatic: If men in mourning can be promoted, then officials who receive news of a parent's death need not resign;

sentences.zh: 聞喪者可不去，則為子者可不父，為臣者可不子。

translations.literal: If those who hear of a death need not leave, then those who are sons need not treat their fathers as fathers, and those who are subjects need not treat their rulers as sons.
translations.idiomatic: If they need not resign on receiving news of a death, then sons need not honor fathers and ministers need not serve their rulers with loyal devotion.

sentences.zh: 即使人才甚乏，奈何使不忠不孝者連苞引蘗，種其不祥以穢天下乎？

translations.literal: Even if talent is very scarce—how can one let the disloyal and unfilial link rotten roots and draw up sprouts, planting their ill omen to foul the world?
translations.idiomatic: Even if talent is desperately scarce, how can we let the disloyal and unfilial take office in succession, spreading their corruption through the empire?

sentences.zh: 嗣昌在事二年，張網溢地之談，款市樂天之說，才智亦可睹矣，更起一不祥之人，與之表裏。

translations.literal: Sichang in affairs two years—the talk of casting nets overflowing the earth, the doctrine of appeasement and complacency—his talent and wisdom can also be seen; to raise again an ill-omened man and pair him inside and out with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang's two years in office have already shown his caliber—his schemes to snare enemies everywhere, his talk of appeasement and self-congratulation. To raise another ill-omened man and set him alongside Yang Sichang is to invite disaster.

sentences.zh: 陛下孝治天下，縉紳家庭小小勃谿，猶以法治之，而冒喪斁倫，獨謂無禁，臣竊以為不可也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty governs the world through filial piety—even among gentry families, small family squabbles are still governed by law, yet violating mourning and destroying human relations alone is said to have no prohibition. Your minister privately thinks this cannot stand.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rules through filial piety. Even minor domestic disputes among scholar-officials are judged by law—yet violations of mourning and destruction of human relations are suddenly exempt. I submit that this cannot be allowed.

sentences.zh: 其論新甲，言：

translations.literal: In discussing Xinji, he stated:
translations.idiomatic: Regarding Chen Xinji, he wrote:

sentences.zh: 其守制不終，走邪徑，托捷足。

translations.literal: He did not complete his mourning observance, took crooked paths, and relied on swift feet.
translations.idiomatic: He did not complete his mourning, took underhanded shortcuts, and relied on court favoritism.

sentences.zh: 天下即甚無才，未宜假借及此。

translations.literal: Even if the world is very lacking in talent, one ought not lend authority to this extent.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the empire were utterly bereft of talent, men like this ought not be entrusted with such power.

sentences.zh: 古有忠臣孝子無濟於艱難者，決未有不忠不孝而可進乎功名道德之門者也。

translations.literal: In antiquity there were loyal ministers and filial sons who could not aid in hardship—never has there been one disloyal and unfilial who could enter the gate of merit, fame, morality, and the Way.
translations.idiomatic: History holds cases where loyal and filial men failed despite their virtue—but never has a disloyal, unfilial man passed through the gates of honor and moral achievement.

sentences.zh: 臣二十躬耕，手足胼胝，以養二人。

translations.literal: Your minister at twenty personally plowed, hands and feet calloused and blistered, to support two people.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty I farmed with my own hands until they cracked and blistered, supporting my two parents.

sentences.zh: 四十余削籍，徒步荷擔二千里，不解屝屨。

translations.literal: Past forty, stripped from the register, on foot carrying burdens two thousand li, not removing straw sandals.
translations.idiomatic: After forty, stripped of my rank, I walked two thousand li carrying my belongings on my back, never pausing to remove my sandals.

sentences.zh: 今雖逾五十，非有妻子之奉，婢仆之累。

translations.literal: Now though past fifty, there is no wife and children's support, no servant-girls' burden.
translations.idiomatic: Now past fifty, I have no wife and children to support, no servants to maintain.

sentences.zh: 天下即無人，臣願解清華，出管鎖鑰，何必使被棘負塗者，祓不祥以玷王化哉！

translations.literal: Even if the world has no men, your minister is willing to resign splendid office and go out to manage keys and locks—why must one make those who bear thorns through mire expel ill omens to stain royal transformation?
translations.idiomatic: Even if no one else remained, I would gladly surrender this fine office and take charge of a lock and key—why must you appoint men stained with filth and ill omen to defile the imperial court?

sentences.zh: 其論一藻，則力詆和議之非。

translations.literal: In discussing Yizao, he then vigorously denounced the wrongness of peace talks.
translations.idiomatic: Regarding Fang Yizao, he fiercely denounced the folly of seeking peace.

sentences.zh: 帝疑道周以不用怨望，而「縉紳」、「勃谿」語，欲為鄭鄤脫罪，下吏部行譴。

translations.literal: The Emperor suspected Daozhou resented not being used, and that the words "gentry" and "family squabbles" sought to exonerate Zheng Man; he sent the Ministry of Personnel to carry out reprimand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected Huang Daozhou of resenting his rejection and believed the references to "scholar-officials" and "family squabbles" were meant to exonerate Zheng Man. He ordered the Ministry of Personnel to discipline him.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌因上言：「鄤杖母，禽獸不如。

translations.literal: Sichang then submitted words: "Man beat his mother—not equal to beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang then memorialized: "Zheng Man beat his mother—he is beneath beasts.

sentences.zh: 今道周又不如鄤，且其意徒欲庇兇徒，飾前言之謬，立心可知。」

translations.literal: Now Daozhou again is not equal to Man—and moreover his intent is merely to shelter vicious men, adorn the error of his earlier words—his underlying motive can be known."
translations.idiomatic: Now Huang Daozhou declares himself inferior even to Zheng Man—and his purpose is plainly to shield the guilty and cover the absurdity of his earlier praise. His motives are transparent."

sentences.zh: 因自乞罷免，帝優旨慰之。

translations.literal: He then himself begged dismissal; the Emperor issued a gracious edict to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to be dismissed. The emperor issued a gracious edict reassuring him.

sentences.zh: 七月五日，召內閣及諸大臣於平臺，並及道周。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the seventh month, summoned the Grand Secretariat and various ministers at Ping Terrace, also including Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the seventh month, the emperor summoned the Grand Secretariat and the senior ministers to Ping Terrace, Huang Daozhou included.

sentences.zh: 帝與諸臣語所司事，久之，問道周曰：「凡無所為而為者，謂之天理；

translations.literal: The Emperor with the various ministers spoke affairs of their charge; after a long time, asked Daozhou saying: "Whatever is done without acting from motive—this is called Heavenly Principle;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor discussed official business with his ministers. After a long while he turned to Huang Daozhou and asked: "Whatever one does without ulterior motive is said to express Heavenly Principle;

sentences.zh: 有所為而為者，謂之人欲。

translations.literal: Whatever is done with motive—is called human desire.
translations.idiomatic: whatever one does from ulterior motive is called human desire.

sentences.zh: 爾三疏適當廷推不用時，果無所為乎？」

translations.literal: Your three memorials just happened at the time of court recommendation when you were not used—were they truly without motive?"
translations.idiomatic: Your three memorials came just as the court recommendation passed you over—were they truly without ulterior motive?"

sentences.zh: 道周對曰：「臣三疏皆為國家綱常，自信無所為。」

translations.literal: Daozhou replied saying: "Your minister's three memorials all were for the state's fundamental norms; I trust myself there was no motive."
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou replied: "All three of my memorials concerned the fundamental moral order of the state. I am confident they sprang from no private motive."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「先時何不言？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Why not speak then earlier?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Then why did you not speak out sooner?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「先時猶可不言，至簡用後不言，更無當言之日。」

translations.literal: Replied saying: "Earlier one could still not speak; once direct appointment came afterward, not speaking—there would be no further day when one ought to speak."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Before, silence was still possible. After Yang Sichang was directly appointed, if I held my tongue, there would never again be a day to speak."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「清固美德，但不可傲物遂非。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Purity is indeed a fine virtue, but one cannot be arrogant toward things and thereby persist in error.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Integrity is indeed a fine virtue, but one must not scorn others and stubbornly persist in error.

sentences.zh: 且惟伯夷為聖之清，若小廉曲謹，是廉，非清也。」

translations.literal: Moreover only Boyi was the Sage's purity; if petty integrity and meticulous caution—that is integrity, not purity."
translations.idiomatic: Only Boyi embodied the Sage's ideal of purity. Petty scruples and punctilious caution—that is mere probity, not true purity."

sentences.zh: 時道周所對不合指，帝屢駁，道周復進曰：「惟孝弟之人始能經綸天下，發育萬物。

translations.literal: At this time Daozhou's answers did not accord with the point; the Emperor repeatedly rebutted. Daozhou again advanced saying: "Only persons of filial piety and brotherly respect can order the world and nurture the ten thousand things.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou's answers missed the emperor's point, and the emperor rebuked him repeatedly. Daozhou pressed on: "Only the filial and dutiful can govern the empire and nurture all things beneath Heaven.

sentences.zh: 不孝不弟者，根本既無，安有枝葉。」

translations.literal: Those unfilial and without brotherly respect—if the root is already absent, how can there be branches and leaves?"
translations.idiomatic: Without filial piety and fraternal duty at the root, how can there be any branches or leaves?"

sentences.zh: 嗣昌出奏曰：「臣不生空桑，豈不知父母？

translations.literal: Sichang stepped forward to memorialize saying: "Your minister was not born under a hollow mulberry tree—how could I not know parents?
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang stepped forward and said: "Your servant was not born ignorant of the world—I know full well what a parent is.

sentences.zh: 顧念君為臣綱，父為子綱，君臣固在父子前。

translations.literal: Only consider: the ruler as minister's bond, the father as son's bond—ruler and minister are certainly placed before father and son.
translations.idiomatic: But consider: the bond between ruler and minister takes precedence, as does the bond between father and son—and the duty to one's sovereign comes before the duty to one's father.

sentences.zh: 況古為列國之君臣，可去此適彼；

translations.literal: Moreover in antiquity as ruler and minister of separate states, one could leave this and go to that;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when each state had its own ruler, a minister could leave one court for another;

sentences.zh: 今則一統之君臣，無所逃於天地之間。

translations.literal: Now then there are ruler and minister of unified rule—nowhere to escape between Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: but today ruler and subject belong to a single unified realm. There is nowhere under Heaven to flee one's sovereign.

sentences.zh: 且仁不遺親，義不後君，難以偏重。

translations.literal: Moreover benevolence does not abandon kin, righteousness does not put the ruler second—hard to weight heavily one side.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence does not abandon one's kin, yet righteousness does not defer to the ruler—one cannot simply favor one over the other.

sentences.zh: 臣四疏力辭，意詞臣中有如劉定之、羅倫者，抗疏為臣代請，得遂臣誌。

translations.literal: Your minister's four memorials strenuously declined; I intended that among Academicians there would be such as Liu Dingzhi and Luo Lun, who would submit bold memorials requesting on my behalf, enabling my wish to be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: I submitted four memorials begging to be excused, expecting that men such as Liu Dingzhi and Luo Lun among the Hanlin Academicians would memorialize boldly on my behalf and help me fulfill my duty.

sentences.zh: 及抵都門，聞道周人品學術為人宗師，乃不如鄭鄤。」

translations.literal: When arriving at the capital gate, I heard Daozhou's character, learning, and scholarship honored as a human master—yet he is not equal to Zheng Man."
translations.idiomatic: Yet when I reached the capital, I heard that Huang Daozhou—revered as a master of character and learning—declared himself inferior to Zheng Man."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然，朕正擬問之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "So—We were just about to ask about this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Exactly. I was just about to ask about that."

sentences.zh: 乃問道周曰：「古人心無所為，今則各有所主，故孟子欲正人心，息邪說。

translations.literal: Then asked Daozhou saying: "In antiquity people's hearts had no motive; now each has its own master. Therefore Mencius wished to rectify human hearts and cease heterodox doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked Huang Daozhou: "In antiquity men's hearts were without ulterior purpose; today each pursues its own master. That is why Mencius sought to rectify the human heart and silence pernicious doctrine.

sentences.zh: 古之邪說，別為一教，今則直附於聖賢經傳中，系世道人心更大。

translations.literal: Heterodox doctrines of antiquity separately formed one teaching; now they attach directly within the Classics and commentaries of sages and worthies—it ties to the age's way and human hearts even more greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The heterodox doctrines of old stood apart as a separate school. Today they attach themselves directly to the texts of the sages—a far greater threat to the moral order.

sentences.zh: 且爾言不如鄭鄤，何也？」

translations.literal: Moreover you say not equal to Zheng Man—why?"
translations.idiomatic: And why do you say you are not Zheng Man's equal?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「匡章見棄通國，孟子不失禮貌，臣言文章不如鄤。」

translations.literal: Replied saying: "Kuang Zhang was cast off by the entire state; Mencius did not lose courtesy. Your minister speaks that in literary composition he is not equal to Man."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "When Kuang Zhang was rejected by the whole state, Mencius still treated him with courtesy. I mean only that in writing I am not Zheng Man's equal."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「章子不得於父，豈鄤杖母者比。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Kuang Zhang did not get along with his father—how can he be compared to Man who beat his mother?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Kuang Zhang failed in his duty to his father—how can that be compared to Zheng Man, who beat his mother?

sentences.zh: 爾言不如，豈非朋比？」

translations.literal: Your saying not equal—is it not factional partiality?"
translations.idiomatic: When you declare yourself inferior to him, is that not mere factional loyalty?"

sentences.zh: 道周曰：「眾惡必察。」

translations.literal: Daozhou said: "When many hate, one must examine."
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou said: "When the multitude condemns a man, one must examine the matter carefully."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「陳新甲何以走邪徑，托捷足？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "How did Chen Xinji take crooked paths and rely on swift feet?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Why did Chen Xinji take underhanded shortcuts and rely on court favoritism?

sentences.zh: 且爾言軟美容悅，叩首折枝者誰耶？」

translations.literal: Moreover you speak of soft flattery and pleasing countenance—who is it that kowtows and breaks branches?"
translations.idiomatic: And you speak of soft flattery and ingratiating smiles—who is it that kowtows and performs every petty favor?"

sentences.zh: 道周不能對，但曰：「人心邪則行徑皆邪。」

translations.literal: Daozhou could not reply, but only said: "When the human heart is crooked, then conduct and paths are all crooked."
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou had no answer, and could only say: "When the heart is corrupt, every course of action becomes corrupt."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「喪固兇禮，豈遭兇者即兇人，盡不祥之人？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Mourning is indeed the inauspicious rite—can those who encounter mourning immediately be inauspicious persons, all ill-omened people?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Mourning is an inauspicious occasion by nature—but does that mean anyone in mourning is an ill-omened person? That all who suffer bereavement are bringers of misfortune?"

sentences.zh: 道周曰：「古三年喪，君命不過其門。

translations.literal: Daozhou said: "In antiquity for the three-year mourning, the ruler's command did not pass his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou said: "In antiquity during the three-year mourning, even the emperor's command did not cross the mourner's threshold.

sentences.zh: 自謂兇與不祥，故軍禮鑿兇門而出。

translations.literal: One regarded oneself as inauspicious and ill-omened; therefore in military rites one carved an inauspicious gate to pass out through.
translations.idiomatic: Mourners considered themselves bearers of ill omen; that is why military ritual required breaking a special "inauspicious gate" when troops marched forth.

sentences.zh: 奪情在疆外則可，朝中則不可。」

translations.literal: Exempting from mourning on the frontier can be permitted; in the court center cannot be permitted."
translations.idiomatic: Exemption from mourning duty at the frontier may be acceptable; at the court it is not."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「人既可用，何分內外？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "If a person can be used, why distinguish inner and outer?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "If a man is fit for service, why distinguish between court and frontier?"

sentences.zh: 道周曰：「我朝自羅倫論奪情，前後五十余人，多在邊疆。

translations.literal: Daozhou said: "Our dynasty since Luo Lun debated exemption from mourning, before and after more than fifty men, mostly at the border frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou said: "Since Luo Lun protested mourning exemptions, our dynasty has granted duoqing to more than fifty officials—and most served on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 故嗣昌在邊疆則可，在中樞則不可；

translations.literal: Therefore Sichang at the border frontier can be permitted, at the central hub cannot be permitted;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang on the frontier might be acceptable; at the seat of power he is not;

sentences.zh: 在中樞猶可，在政府則不可。

translations.literal: At the central hub still permissible, in the government cannot be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: even at the central command it would be questionable; in the Grand Secretariat it is unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 止嗣昌一人猶可，又呼朋引類，竟成一奪情世界，益不可。」

translations.literal: Only Sichang alone still permissible; again calling friends and drawing kindred, actually forming an exemption-from-mourning world—still less permissible."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang alone might be tolerated—but when he summons allies and draws in others like himself until the court becomes a realm of mourning exemptions, that is utterly intolerable."

sentences.zh: 帝又詰問久之。

translations.literal: The Emperor again interrogated for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed him with questions for a long while.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「少正卯當時亦稱聞人，心逆而險，行僻而堅，言偽而辨，順非而澤，記醜而博，不免聖人之誅。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Shaozheng Mao at that time was also called a renowned man—heart rebellious and treacherous, conduct eccentric and stubborn, words false yet eloquent, following wrong and glossing it, recording ugliness yet broadly learned—could not escape the Sage's execution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Shaozheng Mao was once also hailed as a man of renown—rebellious and treacherous in heart, perverse and obstinate in conduct, eloquent yet deceitful of speech, glossing over wrong as right, recording vileness with vast learning—and he did not escape the sage's punishment.

sentences.zh: 今人多類此。」

translations.literal: Today many people resemble this."
translations.idiomatic: Many men today resemble him."

sentences.zh: 道周曰：「少正卯心術不正，臣心正無一毫私。」

translations.literal: Daozhou said: "Shaozheng Mao's mind-craft was not upright; your minister's heart is upright without a hair's breadth of private motive."
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou said: "Shaozheng Mao's intentions were corrupt. My heart is upright—not a trace of private motive."

sentences.zh: 帝怒。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angered.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 有間，命出候旨。

translations.literal: After an interval, ordered him out to await the edict.
translations.idiomatic: After a pause, the emperor ordered him to withdraw and wait for the imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 道周曰：「臣今日不盡言，臣負陛下；

translations.literal: Daozhou said: "If your minister today does not fully speak, your minister fails Your Majesty;
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou said: "If I hold back today, I fail Your Majesty;

sentences.zh: 陛下今日殺臣，陛下負臣。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty today kills your minister, Your Majesty fails your minister."
translations.idiomatic: if Your Majesty executes me today, Your Majesty fails me."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「爾一生學問，止成佞耳！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Your whole life's learning—only achieves sycophant, that's all!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "A lifetime of learning, and all you have become is a sycophant!"

sentences.zh: 叱之退。

translations.literal: Shouted at him to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: He shouted at him to leave.

sentences.zh: 道周叩首起，復跪奏：「臣敢將忠佞二字剖析言之。

translations.literal: Daozhou kowtowed, rose, again knelt and memorialized: "Your minister dares to analyze and speak the two words loyal and sycophant.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou kowtowed, rose, then knelt again and said: "Your servant ventures to distinguish the meaning of loyalty and sycophancy.

sentences.zh: 夫人在君父前，獨立敢言為佞，豈在君父前讒諂面諛為忠耶？

translations.literal: When a person before ruler and father, standing alone and daring to speak—is sycophant; how can before ruler and father slandering, flattering, and face-to-face fawning be loyalty?
translations.idiomatic: When one speaks boldly and independently before one's sovereign, you call it sycophancy—yet slander, flattery, and barefaced adulation before one's lord you call loyalty?

sentences.zh: 忠佞不別，邪正淆矣，何以致治？」

translations.literal: Loyal and sycophant not distinguished, wrong and right mixed—how to achieve governance?"
translations.idiomatic: If loyalty and sycophancy cannot be told apart, right and wrong are confounded—how can the realm be well governed?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「固也，非朕漫加爾以佞。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Indeed so—We did not casually attach sycophant to you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "True enough—I did not casually call you a sycophant.

sentences.zh: 但所問在此，所答在彼，非佞而何？」

translations.literal: But what was asked is here, what was answered is there—if not sycophant, then what?"
translations.idiomatic: But I ask about one thing and you answer about another—if that is not sycophancy, what is?"

sentences.zh: 再叱之退。

translations.literal: Again shouted at him to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Again he shouted at him to leave.

sentences.zh: 顧嗣昌曰：「甚矣，人心偷薄也。

translations.literal: Gu Sichang said: "Extreme indeed—the human heart is shallow and mean.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang then said: "How far the moral sense of men has fallen!

sentences.zh: 道周恣肆如此，其能無正乎？」

translations.literal: Daozhou unrestrained to this degree—can he not be corrected?"
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou behaves with such brazen defiance—can he go uncorrected?"

sentences.zh: 乃召文武諸臣，鹹聆戒諭而退。

translations.literal: Then summoned civil and military various ministers, all to hear admonition and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned the civil and military officials, all listened to the emperor's admonition, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝憂兵事，謂可屬大事者惟嗣昌，破格用之。

translations.literal: At this time the Emperor worried over military affairs, considered that one who could be entrusted with great matters was only Sichang; broke regulations to use him.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the emperor was consumed by military concerns and believed Yang Sichang alone could be entrusted with great affairs. He appointed him despite the mourning prohibition.

sentences.zh: 道周守經，失帝意，及奏對，又不遜。

translations.literal: Daozhou upheld the classics, lost the Emperor's favor; when memorializing and responding, again was not deferential.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou clung to classical precedent and lost the emperor's favor. In audience his answers were anything but deferential.

sentences.zh: 帝怒甚，欲加以重罪，憚其名高，未敢決。

translations.literal: The Emperor was very angered, wished to impose heavy punishment; feared his high renown, did not dare decide.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's rage was intense and he wished to impose heavy punishment, but he feared Huang Daozhou's great reputation and did not dare act decisively.

sentences.zh: 會劉同升、趙士春亦劾嗣昌，將予重譴，而部擬道周譴顧輕。

translations.literal: It happened that Liu Tongsheng and Zhao Shichun also impeached Sichang, about to give heavy reprimand; but the ministry proposed Daozhou's reprimand comparatively light.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Tongsheng and Zhao Shichun also impeached Yang Sichang, the emperor was ready to impose severe punishment—but the ministry's proposed penalty for Huang Daozhou was conspicuously lenient.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌懼道周輕，則論己者將無已時也，亟購人劾道周者。

translations.literal: Sichang feared that if Daozhou were light, then those who discuss him would have no end; urgently purchased men to impeach Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang feared that if Huang Daozhou escaped lightly, the attacks against him would never cease. He urgently hired men to impeach Huang Daozhou.

sentences.zh: 有刑部主事張若麒謀改兵部，遂阿嗣昌意上疏曰：「臣聞人主之尊，尊無二上；

translations.literal: There was Ministry of Punishments principal clerk Zhang Ruoqi who schemed to transfer to Ministry of War; therefore toadying to Sichang's intent submitted memorial saying: "Your minister hears the human ruler's honor—honored with no second above;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ruoqi, a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments who sought transfer to the Ministry of War, curried Yang Sichang's favor with a memorial: "I have heard that the sovereign's dignity brooks no second master above him;

sentences.zh: 人臣無將，將而必誅。

translations.literal: Human ministers must not harbor [rebellious intent]; if they harbor it, must be executed.
translations.idiomatic: no minister may harbor treasonous ambition—and ambition once shown must be punished by death.

sentences.zh: 今黃道周及其徒黨造作語言，虧損聖德。

translations.literal: Now Huang Daozhou and his faction fabricate language, damaging sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou and his followers now fabricate accusations that damage Your Majesty's sacred virtue.

sentences.zh: 舉古今未有之好語盡出道周，無不可歸過於君父。

translations.literal: Citing good words without precedent in past and present—all come from Daozhou; nothing cannot be attributed as fault to ruler and father.
translations.idiomatic: They parade praises unprecedented in history—all originating with Huang Daozhou—and there is no fault they will not lay at the feet of their sovereign.

sentences.zh: 不頒示前日召對始末，背公死黨之徒，鼓煽以惑四方，私記以疑後世，掩聖天子正人心息邪說至意，大不便。」

translations.literal: Not promulgating the beginning and end of the other day's summoned audience—in parties that betray the public and die for faction, they drum and fan to confuse the four quarters, privately record to make later ages doubt, concealing the sacred Son of Heaven's utmost intent to rectify human hearts and cease heterodox doctrines—greatly inconvenient."
translations.idiomatic: By withholding the full record of the recent audience, these men who betray the public interest and cling to faction spread agitation to confuse the realm and keep private accounts to poison posterity—obscuring Your Majesty's sincere intent to rectify hearts and silence pernicious doctrine. This is deeply harmful."

sentences.zh: 帝即傳諭廷臣，毋為道周劫持相朋黨，凡數百言。

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately transmitted instructions to court ministers: do not be hijacked by Daozhou into mutual faction, in all several hundred words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately issued an edict to the court, warning officials not to let Huang Daozhou manipulate them into faction—several hundred words in all.

sentences.zh: 貶道周六秩，為江西按察司照磨，而若麒果得兵部。

translations.literal: Demoted Daozhou six ranks, made Jiangxi Surveillance Commission assistant registrar; and Ruoqi indeed obtained Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou was demoted six ranks and appointed assistant registrar of the Jiangxi Surveillance Commission. Zhang Ruoqi received his transfer to the Ministry of War as he had hoped.

sentences.zh: 久之，江西巡撫解學龍薦所部官，推獎道周備至。

translations.literal: After a long time, Jiangxi Provincial governor Xie Xuelong recommended officials of his jurisdiction, extolling Daozhou to the full.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, the Jiangxi governor Xie Xuelong submitted recommendations for officials under his jurisdiction and praised Huang Daozhou in the highest terms.

sentences.zh: 故事，但下所司，帝亦不覆閱。

translations.literal: By precedent, merely sent down to the relevant office; the Emperor also did not review again.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent such recommendations were simply forwarded to the relevant ministry for action, and the emperor did not review them again.

sentences.zh: 而大學士魏照乘惡道周甚，則擬旨責學龍濫薦。

translations.literal: But Grand Secretary Wei Zhaocheng hated Daozhou deeply; then drafted edict rebuking Xuelong for indiscriminate recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: But Grand Secretary Wei Zhaocheng, who deeply hated Huang Daozhou, drafted an edict rebuking Xie Xuelong for indiscriminate recommendation.

sentences.zh: 帝遂發怒，立削二人籍，逮下刑部獄，責以黨邪亂政，並杖八十，究黨與。

translations.literal: The Emperor then erupted in anger, immediately struck both from the register, arrested and sent down to Ministry of Punishments prison, charged with factional evil disrupting government; together caned eighty strokes, investigate faction accomplices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, immediately struck both from the rolls, and sent them to the Ministry of Punishments prison on charges of partisan subversion. Both were flogged eighty strokes, and a full investigation of their faction was ordered.

sentences.zh: 詞連編修黃文煥、吏部主事陳天定、工部司務董養河、中書舍人文震亨，並系獄。

translations.literal: Words implicated Compiler Huang Wenhuan, Ministry of Personnel principal clerk Chen Tianding, Ministry of Works clerk Dong Yanghe, Secretariat drafter Wen Zhenheng—all imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The case implicated the compiler Huang Wenhuan, the Ministry of Personnel clerk Chen Tianding, the Ministry of Works clerk Dong Yanghe, and the Secretariat drafter Wen Zhenheng—all were imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 戶部主事葉廷秀、監生塗仲吉救之，亦系獄。

translations.literal: Ministry of Revenue principal clerk Ye Tingxiu, student Tu Zhongji who rescued them—also imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Tingxiu of the Ministry of Revenue and the student Tu Zhongji, who had petitioned on their behalf, were also imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 尚書李覺斯讞輕，嚴旨切責，再擬謫戍煙瘴，帝猶以為失出，除覺斯名，移獄鎮撫司掠治，乃還刑部獄。

translations.literal: Minister Li Juesi's verdict was light; stern edict sharply rebuked; again proposed banishment to miasmic frontier; Emperor still considered it too lenient, removed Juesi's name, transferred prison to Brocade Guard for torture, then returned to Ministry of Punishments prison.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Li Juesi proposed a lenient sentence. The emperor issued a severe reprimand and ordered banishment to the malarial south. Still deeming this too lenient, he dismissed Li Juesi, transferred the prisoners to the Brocade Guard for interrogation under torture, then returned them to the Ministry of Punishments prison.

sentences.zh: 逾年，尚書劉澤深等言：「二人罪至永戍止矣，過此惟論死。

translations.literal: After a year, Minister Liu Zeshen and others said: "The two men's guilt reaches only perpetual banishment; beyond this only death is debated.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, Minister Liu Zeshen and others memorialized: "For these two men, perpetual banishment is the utmost penalty. Beyond that lies only death.

sentences.zh: 論死非封疆則貪酷，未有以建言者。

translations.literal: Death is debated not for frontier defense then for greed and cruelty—never has there been one who received death for submitting words.
translations.idiomatic: Death is reserved for failures on the frontier or for greed and cruelty—not for men who merely speak their minds.

sentences.zh: 道周無封疆貪酷之罪，而有建言蒙戮之名，於道周得矣，非我聖主覆載之量也。

translations.literal: Daozhou has no guilt of frontier or greed and cruelty, yet has the name of submitting words and receiving execution—this suffices for Daozhou, but is not our sacred ruler's capacity of covering and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou is guilty of neither border failure nor corruption, yet would gain the name of a man executed for speaking out. That may satisfy his enemies—but it is unworthy of our sage sovereign's magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 陛下所疑者黨耳，黨者，見諸行事。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's doubt is only faction; faction—is seen in actions.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's concern is faction—but faction is proved by conduct, not words.

sentences.zh: 道周抗疏，只托空言，一二知交相從罷斥，烏睹所謂黨，而煩朝廷大法乎？

translations.literal: Daozhou's bold memorials rely only on empty words; one or two intimate friends follow one another in dismissal—where is the so-called faction, yet troubling the court's great law?
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou's bold memorials are mere words. A few friends shared his fate in dismissal—where is the faction that warrants invoking the full force of imperial law?

sentences.zh: 且陛下豈有積恨道周，萬一聖意轉圜，而臣已論定，悔之何及。」

translations.literal: Moreover does Your Majesty necessarily bear accumulated resentment toward Daozhou? If by chance sacred intent turns—yet your ministers have already decided the verdict, how can regret catch up?"
translations.idiomatic: And surely Your Majesty bears no deep grudge against Huang Daozhou. If the imperial mind should soften but we have already settled on death, how could we undo it?"

sentences.zh: 仍以原擬請，乃永戍廣西。

translations.literal: Still submitted according to the original proposal; then perpetual banishment to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: They resubmitted their original proposal, and the two were banished permanently to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 十五年八月，道周戍已經年。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of year fifteen, Daozhou's banishment had already passed a year.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fifteenth year of the reign, Huang Daozhou had already been in exile for a year.

sentences.zh: 一日，帝召五輔臣入文華後殿，手一編從容問曰：「張溥、張采何如人也？」

translations.literal: One day the Emperor summoned five assisting ministers into Wenhua Rear Hall, holding one scroll, calmly asked saying: "Zhang Pu and Zhang Cai—what sort of men are they?"
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor summoned the five grand secretaries to the rear hall of Wenhua Palace. Holding a document, he asked casually: "What sort of men are Zhang Pu and Zhang Cai?"

sentences.zh: 皆對曰：「讀書好學人也。」

translations.literal: All replied saying: "Men who read books and love learning."
translations.idiomatic: They all answered: "Scholars who love learning."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「張溥已死，張采小臣，科道官何亟稱之？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Zhang Pu is already dead; Zhang Cai is a minor official—why do censorate officials so urgently praise them?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Zhang Pu is dead, and Zhang Cai is a minor official—why do censorial officials praise them so eagerly?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「其胸中自有書，科道官以其用未竟而惜之。」

translations.literal: Replied saying: "Their breasts naturally have books; censorate officials because their use was not finished pity them."
translations.idiomatic: They answered: "They are men of real learning. The censorial officials regret that their talents were not fully employed."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「亦不免偏。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Still cannot avoid partiality."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "They are not without bias, all the same."

sentences.zh: 時延儒自以嗣昌既已前死矣，而己方再入相，欲參用公議，為道周地也，即對曰：「張溥、黃道周皆未免偏，徒以其善學，故人人惜之。」

translations.literal: At this time Yanru himself thought Sichang had already died earlier, and he himself had just re-entered as Chancellor, wished to incorporate public opinion and make room for Daozhou; immediately replied saying: "Zhang Pu and Huang Daozhou both cannot avoid partiality; merely because they love learning well, therefore everyone pities them."
translations.idiomatic: At this Zhou Yanru, believing Yang Sichang already dead and himself newly restored as chief minister, wished to invoke public sentiment and create an opening for Huang Daozhou. He answered: "Zhang Pu and Huang Daozhou alike are not without prejudice—but because they are genuine scholars, everyone regrets their fate."

sentences.zh: 帝默然。

translations.literal: The Emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 德璟曰：「道周前日蒙戍，上恩寬大，獨其家貧子幼，其實可憫。」

translations.literal: Dejing said: "Daozhou the other day received banishment—superior grace was broad and generous; only his family is poor and children young—truly pitiable."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Dejing said: "Huang Daozhou was recently banished—a lenient punishment from Your Majesty. Yet his family is poor and his children young. He truly deserves pity."

sentences.zh: 帝微笑，演曰：「其事親亦極孝。」

translations.literal: The Emperor smiled faintly; Yan said: "His serving parents is also extremely filial."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled faintly. Huang Yan added: "He is also profoundly filial toward his parents."

sentences.zh: 行甡曰：「道周學無不通，且極清苦。」

translations.literal: Xingshen said: "Daozhou's learning has nothing he does not penetrate, and moreover is extremely pure hardship."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xingshen said: "Huang Daozhou's learning is encyclopedic, and he lives in the utmost austerity."

sentences.zh: 帝不答，但微笑而已。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not reply, only smiled faintly—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not reply—he only smiled.

sentences.zh: 明日傳旨復故官。

translations.literal: Next day transmitted edict restoring former office.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict restored Huang Daozhou to his former office.

sentences.zh: 道周在途疏謝，稱學龍、廷秀賢。

translations.literal: Daozhou on the road submitted memorial of thanks, praised Xuelong and Tingxiu as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou submitted a memorial of thanks from the road, praising Xie Xuelong and Ye Tingxiu as worthy men.

sentences.zh: 既還，帝召見道周，道周見帝而泣：「臣不自意今復得見陛下，臣故有犬馬之疾。」

translations.literal: After returning, the Emperor summoned and received Daozhou; Daozhou seeing the Emperor wept: "Your minister did not expect now again to see Your Majesty; your minister formerly has canine-and-horse illness."
translations.idiomatic: After his return the emperor summoned him. Huang Daozhou wept at the sight of the throne: "I never expected to see Your Majesty again. I have been ill with a condition of old age."

sentences.zh: 請假，許之。

translations.literal: Requested leave; permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He requested leave, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 居久之，福王監國，用道周吏部左侍郎。

translations.literal: After residing a long time, Prince Fu supervised the state, employed Daozhou as Left Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After some time the Prince of Fu assumed the regency and appointed Huang Daozhou Left Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 道周不欲出，馬士英諷之曰：「人望在公，公不起，欲從史可法擁立潞王耶？」

translations.literal: Daozhou did not wish to come out; Ma Shi Ying satirized him, saying: "Public hope rests on you, sir; if you do not rise, do you wish to follow Shi Kefa in supporting and establishing the Prince of Lu?"
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou was reluctant to take office. Ma Shi Ying goaded him: "All eyes are on you, sir. If you refuse to serve, do you mean to join Shi Kefa in installing the Prince of Lu?"

sentences.zh: 乃不得已趨朝。

translations.literal: Thereupon, having no choice, he hurried to court.
translations.idiomatic: At last he had no choice but to attend court.

sentences.zh: 陳進取九策，拜禮部尚書，協理詹事府事。

translations.literal: He submitted nine policies for advance and recovery, was appointed Minister of Rites, and concurrently managed the affairs of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He presented nine policies for recovery, was appointed Minister of Rites, and was charged with managing the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 而朝政日非，大臣相繼去國，識者知其將亡矣。

translations.literal: But court affairs daily worsened; grand ministers successively left the state; perceptive men knew it would soon perish.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court grew worse by the day. Ministers left office one after another. Those with insight could see the regime was doomed.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，遣祭告禹陵。

translations.literal: The following year in the third month, he was dispatched to offer sacrifice and announcement at Yu's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The next March he was sent to offer sacrifices at the tomb of Yu the Great.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，陳進取策，時不能用。

translations.literal: On the verge of departure, he submitted policies for advance and recovery; at the time they could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: Before his departure he again submitted his recovery policies, but they were not adopted.

sentences.zh: 甫竣事，南都亡，見唐王聿鍵於衢州，奉表勸進。

translations.literal: Just as duties were finished, the Southern Capital was lost; he met Prince Tang Zhu Yujian at Quzhou and presented a memorial urging him to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely finished his mission when the Southern Capital fell. He met Zhu Yujian, the Prince of Tang, at Quzhou and submitted a memorial urging him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 王以道周為武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: The Prince made Daozhou Grand Secretary of the Hall of Martial Brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: The prince appointed Huang Daozhou Grand Secretary of the Hall of Martial Brilliance.

sentences.zh: 道周學行高，王敬禮之特甚，賜宴。

translations.literal: Daozhou's learning and conduct were lofty; the Prince reverenced and treated him especially, and granted a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou's learning and integrity were of the highest order, and the prince treated him with exceptional respect, conferring a banquet in his honor.

sentences.zh: 鄭芝龍爵通侯，位道周上，眾議抑芝龍，文武由是不和。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhilong was enfeoffed as Marquis Who Penetrates All, with rank above Daozhou; public discussion sought to suppress Zhilong; civil and military officials from this were not harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhilong held the title Marquis Who Penetrates All and ranked above Huang Daozhou. Many urged that Zhilong be brought down—a quarrel that divided civil and military officials.

sentences.zh: 一諸生上書詆道周迂，不可居相位，王知出芝龍意，下督學御史撻之。

translations.literal: A commoner scholar submitted a memorial slandering Daozhou as pedantic and unfit to occupy the chancellor's position; the Prince knew it came from Zhilong's intention and sent it down to the provincial education censor to cane the petitioner.
translations.idiomatic: A student submitted a memorial attacking Huang Daozhou as impractical and unfit for the chancellorship. Knowing the hand of Zheng Zhilong behind it, the prince had the provincial education censor flog the petitioner.

sentences.zh: 當是時，國勢衰，政歸鄭氏，大帥恃恩觀望，不肯一出關募兵。

translations.literal: At this time the national situation declined; government returned to the Zheng clan; great commanders relied on favor and watched, unwilling even once to cross the pass and raise troops.
