translations.idiomatic: At this time national power was failing and real authority rested with the Zheng clan. The great commanders, confident in imperial favor, held back and would not once cross the frontier to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 道周請自往江西圖恢復。

translations.literal: Daozhou requested to go himself to Jiangxi to plan recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou volunteered to go to Jiangxi himself and plot recovery.

sentences.zh: 以七月啟行，所至遠近響應，得義旅九千余人，由廣信出衢州。

translations.literal: Setting out in the seventh month, wherever he went near and far responded; he obtained righteous troops of more than nine thousand men and marched by way of Guangxin toward Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He set out in the seventh month. Wherever he passed, men rallied from far and near; he raised more than nine thousand volunteer troops and marched from Guangxin toward Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月進至婺源，遇大清兵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he advanced to Wuyuan and encountered Great Qing troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he reached Wuyuan and met Qing forces.

sentences.zh: 戰敗，被執至江寧，幽別室中，囚服著書。

translations.literal: Defeated in battle, he was seized and taken to Jiangning, confined in a separate room, and in prisoner garb wrote books.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated in battle, he was seized and taken to Jiangning, confined in a separate cell, and in prison garb continued to write.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，過東華門，坐不起，曰：「此與高皇帝陵寢近，可死矣。」

translations.literal: Approaching execution, passing the East Flowery Gate, he sat and would not rise, saying: "This is near the tomb-palace of the High Emperor—I may die here."
translations.idiomatic: On the way to execution he passed the East Flowery Gate, sat down, and refused to rise. "This is close to the tomb of the dynastic founder," he said. "I can die here."

sentences.zh: 監刑者從之。

translations.literal: The execution supervisor complied.
translations.idiomatic: The executioner agreed.

sentences.zh: 幕下士中書賴雍、蔡紹謹，兵部主事趙士超等皆死。

translations.literal: Staff beneath his tent—Secretaries-in-Attendance Lai Yong and Cai Shaojin; Principal Clerk of the Ministry of War Zhao Shichao and others—all died.
translations.idiomatic: His aides—Secretaries-in-Attendance Lai Yong and Cai Shaojin, and Principal Clerk Zhao Shichao of the Ministry of War—died with him.

sentences.zh: 道周學貫古今，所至學者雲集。

translations.literal: Daozhou's learning penetrated ancient and modern; wherever he went scholars gathered like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daozhou's learning spanned the ages. Wherever he went, scholars flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 銅山在孤島中，有石室，道周自幼坐臥其中，故學者稱為石齋先生。

translations.literal: Tongshan stands on a lonely islet; there is a stone chamber; Daozhou from youth sat and lay within it; therefore scholars called him Master Stone Studio.
translations.idiomatic: On Tongshan, an islet off the coast, was a stone chamber where Huang Daozhou had lived and studied since childhood. Scholars therefore called him Master Stone Studio.

sentences.zh: 精天文歷數皇極諸書，所著《易象正》、《三易洞璣》及《太函經》，學者窮年不能通其說，而道周用以推驗治亂。

translations.literal: He was proficient in astronomy, calendrical calculation, the Supreme Ultimate, and such books; works he authored—《Correct Images of the Changes》, 《Profound Mirror of the Three Changes》, and 《Canon of the Grand Envelope》—scholars exhausting years could not penetrate their doctrine, yet Daozhou used them to infer and verify order and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered astronomy, calendrics, and cosmological texts. His works—《Correct Images of the Changes》, 《Profound Mirror of the Three Changes》, and 《Canon of the Grand Envelope》—puzzled scholars who spent years on them without fully grasping their doctrines, yet he applied them to forecast the rise and fall of dynasties.

sentences.zh: 歿後，家人得其小冊，自謂終於丙戌，年六十二，始信其能知來也。

translations.literal: After death, family members obtained his small booklet; he had said he would end in the bingxu year, age sixty-two; only then did they believe he could know what was to come.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his family found a small notebook in which he had written that he would die in the bingxu year at age sixty-two. Only then did they believe he could foretell the future.

sentences.zh: 葉廷秀，濮州人。

translations.literal: Ye Tingxiu was a man of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Tingxiu was a native of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fifth year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Tianqi reign.

sentences.zh: 歷知南樂、衡水、獲鹿三縣，入為順天府推官。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Nanle, Hengshui, and Huolu three counties; entered service as judicial assistant of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as magistrate of Nanle, Hengshui, and Huolu, then entered the capital as judicial assistant of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 英國公張惟賢與民爭田，廷秀斷歸之民。

translations.literal: Duke of Ying Zhang Weixian disputed fields with commoners; Tingxiu judged and returned them to the commoners.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Ying, Zhang Weixian, disputed land with commoners, Ye Tingxiu ruled in the commoners' favor.

sentences.zh: 惟賢屬御史袁弘勛駁勘，執如初。

translations.literal: Weixian entrusted Censor Yuan Hongxun to re-examine and overturn the judgment; the ruling held as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Weixian had Censor Yuan Hongxun petition for a rehearing, but the original judgment stood.

sentences.zh: 惟賢訴諸朝，帝卒用廷秀奏，還田於民。

translations.literal: Weixian appealed to court; the Emperor ultimately adopted Tingxiu's memorial and returned the fields to the commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Weixian appealed to the throne. The emperor ultimately upheld Ye Tingxiu's ruling and returned the land to the commoners.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，遷南京戶部主事，遭內外艱。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen reign he was transferred to Principal Clerk of the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue and encountered inner and outer bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he was promoted to Principal Clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, then went into mourning for the loss of both parents.

sentences.zh: 服闋，入都，未補官，疏陳吏治之弊，言：「催科一事，正供外有雜派，新增外有暗加，額辦外有貼助，小民破產傾家，安得不為盜賊。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he entered the capital; before receiving appointment, he submitted a memorial setting forth abuses in official governance, saying: "In tax collection alone, beyond regular levies there are miscellaneous exactions; beyond new additions there are secret surcharges; beyond quota assignments there are supplementary contributions—common people ruin families and lose all; how can they not become bandits?
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he came to the capital. Before receiving a new appointment he submitted a memorial on the abuses of local administration, saying: "In tax collection alone, beyond the regular levy come miscellaneous exactions; beyond newly added taxes come secret surcharges; beyond fixed quotas come forced contributions. Common people are ruined and dispossessed—how can they not turn to banditry?

sentences.zh: 夫欲救州縣之弊，當自監司郡守始。

translations.literal: If one wishes to remedy the abuses of prefectures and counties, one should begin with supervising commissioners and prefects.
translations.idiomatic: To remedy the abuses of the counties, one must begin with the supervising commissioners and prefects.

sentences.zh: 不澄其源，流安能潔。

translations.literal: If the source is not clarified, how can the flow be clean?
translations.idiomatic: If the source is not cleared, how can the stream run pure?

sentences.zh: 乃保舉之令行已數年，而稱職者希覯，是連坐法不可不嚴也。」

translations.literal: Yet the order for recommendations has been in force for several years, while men of competence are rarely seen—therefore the law of collective responsibility must be made strict."
translations.idiomatic: The recommendation system has been in place for years, yet worthy appointees remain scarce. The law of collective responsibility must therefore be enforced with rigor."

sentences.zh: 帝納之，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted it and appointed him Principal Clerk of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice and appointed him Principal Clerk of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 帝以傅永淳為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: The Emperor made Fu Yongchun Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Fu Yongchun Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 廷秀言永淳庸才，不當任統均。

translations.literal: Tingxiu said Yongchun was a mediocre talent and ought not hold charge of appointments and talent distribution.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Tingxiu declared that Fu Yongchun was a mediocrity unfit to direct appointments.

sentences.zh: 甫四月，永淳果敗。

translations.literal: Barely four months later, Yongchun indeed met disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Within four months Fu Yongchun was indeed disgraced.

sentences.zh: 道周逮下獄，廷秀抗疏救之。

translations.literal: Daozhou was arrested and imprisoned; Tingxiu submitted a defiant memorial to save him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Daozhou was arrested and imprisoned, Ye Tingxiu submitted an urgent memorial in his defense.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，杖百，系詔獄。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry; he was beaten one hundred strokes and imprisoned in the imperial prison of edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged. Ye Tingxiu was beaten one hundred strokes and thrown into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，遣戍福建。

translations.literal: The following winter he was sent to garrison in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: The next winter he was banished to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 廷秀受業劉宗周門，造詣淵邃，宗周門人以廷秀為首。

translations.literal: Tingxiu received instruction under Liu Zongzhou; his attainments were profound and far-reaching; among Liu Zongzhou's disciples Tingxiu ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Tingxiu had studied under Liu Zongzhou and attained profound mastery. Among Liu's disciples he ranked first.

sentences.zh: 與道周未相識，冒死論救，獲重罪，處之恬然。

translations.literal: He was not acquainted with Daozhou, yet risked death to argue for his rescue; receiving heavy punishment, he treated it calmly.
translations.idiomatic: Though he did not know Huang Daozhou personally, he had risked his life to plead for him. When he received a severe punishment, he bore it without distress.

sentences.zh: 及道周釋還，給事中左懋第、御史李悅心復相繼論薦，執政亦稱其賢，道周在途又為請。

translations.literal: When Daozhou was released and returned, Supervising Secretary Zuo Maodi and Censor Li Yuexin again successively memorialized recommending him; chief ministers also praised his worth; Daozhou on the road again pleaded on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: After Huang Daozhou was released, Supervising Secretary Zuo Maodi and Censor Li Yuexin successively recommended Ye Tingxiu again; the chief ministers also praised his worth, and Huang Daozhou pleaded for him once more from the road.

sentences.zh: 帝令所司核議，已而執政復薦。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the relevant office to examine and deliberate; soon the chief ministers again recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the relevant offices to review the case; before long the chief ministers recommended him again.

sentences.zh: 十六年冬，特旨起故官。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixteenth year, a special edict recalled him to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixteenth year a special edict restored him to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 會都城陷，未赴。

translations.literal: Just then the capital fell; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: But the capital fell before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 福王時，兵部侍郎解學龍薦道周，並及廷秀，命以僉都御史用。

translations.literal: During the time of Prince Fu, Vice Minister of War Xie Xuelong recommended Daozhou and also mentioned Tingxiu; an order appointed him Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, Vice Minister of War Xie Xuelong recommended Huang Daozhou and also named Ye Tingxiu, who was ordered to serve as Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 及還朝，馬士英惡之，抑授光祿少卿。

translations.literal: When he returned to court, Ma Shi Ying hated him and suppressed his appointment to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to court, Ma Shi Ying, who detested him, demoted the appointment to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 南都覆，唐王召拜左僉都御史，進兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Southern Capital was overturned, Prince Tang summoned and appointed him Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and promoted him to Right Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Southern Capital, the Prince of Tang summoned him, appointing him Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and promoting him to Right Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 事敗，為僧以終。

translations.literal: When the cause failed, he became a monk to end his days.
translations.idiomatic: When the cause failed, he took the tonsure and lived out his days as a monk.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：劉宗周、黃道周所指陳，深中時弊。

translations.literal: The encomium says: What Liu Zongzhou and Huang Daozhou pointed out and set forth deeply hit the abuses of the age.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: In what Liu Zongzhou and Huang Daozhou set forth, they struck deep at the abuses of their age.

sentences.zh: 其論才守，別忠佞，足為萬世龜鑒。

translations.literal: Their discussion of talent and integrity, distinguishing loyal from flatterers, is sufficient to serve as a mirror for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Their judgments on talent and integrity, distinguishing the loyal from the sycophantic, stand as a mirror for all ages.

sentences.zh: 而聽者迂而遠之，則救時濟變之說惑之也。

translations.literal: Yet listeners treated them as pedantic and kept their distance—doctrines of saving the age and adapting to change misled them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who heard them dismissed them as impractical and kept their distance—seduced by doctrines of expedient reform.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「雖危起居，竟信其誌，猶將不忘百姓之病也」，二臣有焉。

translations.literal: The 《Commentary》 says: "Though in peril in rising and sitting, ultimately trusting one's resolve, still not forgetting the people's illness"—the two ministers had this.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Commentary》 says: "Though in peril in every movement, yet holding firm to one's purpose and never forgetting the people's distress"—both ministers embodied this.

sentences.zh: 殺身成仁，不違其素，所守豈不卓哉！

translations.literal: Killing the body to perfect benevolence, not violating their plain character—what they upheld, was it not lofty!
translations.idiomatic: They gave their lives to perfect humanity, never betraying their plain integrity. What they upheld—was it not truly sublime!
